analysis_markdown_en:
This critical review synthesizes global and domestic empirical evidence on sorghum grain composition, bioavailable energy, and amino acid digestibility across diverse swine production stages. While sorghum possesses crude protein and gross energy concentrations comparable to or slightly exceeding yellow dent corn, its utilization efficiency is constrained by antinutritional polyphenolic tannins and kafirin prolamin protein matrices. Low-tannin cultivars achieve digestible and metabolizable energy densities directly competitive with corn diets. Implementing thermal extrusion, precise conditioning at 75 deg C to 80 deg C, mechanical particle size optimization, or exogenous carbohydrate and phytase supplementation effectively mitigates digestive barriers, enabling substitution rates of 30% to 100% without impairing growth performance.

## Proximate Nutritional Profile and Antinutritional Matrices

Sorghum grain comprises pericarp, endosperm, and germ fractions, maintaining an overall dry matter content between 89% and 90%. Crude fat varies between 0.78% and 4.74%, crude ash ranges from 1.23% to 2.91%, and crude fiber spans 1.20% to 2.71% across worldwide databases. Starch constitutes the primary carbohydrate energy component at 61.25% to 85.38% of dry matter, with amylose representing 0.18% to 28.21% and amylopectin occupying 71.79% to 99.82%. Starch granules are either spherical or polyhedral with indented surfaces that inherently attenuate alpha-amylase enzymatic penetration.

The primary antinutritional constituents limiting porcine bioavailability are condensed tannins and endosperm kafirins. Tannins bind endogenous digestive enzymes, mucosal glycoproteins, and dietary globular proteins, depressing apparent and standardized ileal digestibility of lysine, arginine, and threonine. Concurrently, kafirins account for approximately 55% of total sorghum protein and are dominated by alpha-kafirins (70% to 80%), beta-kafirins (7% to 8%), and gamma-kafirins (9% to 12%). Dense disulfide crosslinking within the peripheral beta- and gamma-kafirin layers creates an enzymatic shield that retards core alpha-kafirin hydrolysis and impedes inner starch digestion.

- Phosphorus concentrations parallel corn, but 67% to 72% remains bound to phytate complexes compared to approximately 59% in maize.

- Unsaturated fatty acids represent 83% to 88% of total sorghum lipids, dominated by linoleic acid (45.6% to 51.1%) and oleic acid (32.2% to 42.0%).

- Feeding sorghum rations increases longissimus dorsi saturated fatty acid proportions by 21.7% relative to corn diets, markedly stiffening carcass fat.

## Swine Available Energy Dynamics and Mathematical Prediction

Available energy values in pigs vary according to cultivar genetics, origin, processing, and physiological maturity. Across growing pig bioassays, digestible energy ranges from 2826 to 3794 kcal/kg while metabolizable energy spans 2785 to 3709 kcal/kg. Physiological maturity significantly enhances energetic extraction: gestating sows achieve a digestible energy of 3829 kcal/kg (16.02 MJ/kg) and metabolizable energy of 3757 kcal/kg (15.72 MJ/kg), outpacing 40 kg growing barrows at 3544 kcal/kg (14.83 MJ/kg) and 3512 kcal/kg, respectively.

Predictive mathematical modelling confirms that condensed tannin content represents the dominant negative predictor across both energy availability and standardized ileal amino acid digestibility. Regression models established for 25 to 50 kg pigs demonstrate strong predictive accuracy, where digestible energy decreases by 294 kcal/kg per percentage point of tannin, and standardized ileal crude protein digestibility is modeled by equations accounting for ether extract and antinutritional tannin fractions.

- Growing barrows (34.6 kg) fed sorghum diets achieve 3918 kcal/kg DE and 3870 kcal/kg ME on a dry matter basis.

- Incremental pig body weights from 13.3 kg to 111 kg exhibit minor upward numerical trajectories in sorghum DE (3440 to 3512 kcal/kg) and ME (3392 to 3464 kcal/kg).

- Direct versus indirect substitution assays generate closely matching DE differences restricted to 14 to 63 kcal/kg.

## Feed Processing Interventions and Swine Performance Outcomes

Low-tannin sorghum (tannin under 0.5%) can entirely substitute corn across grow-finish phases without depressing average daily gain, daily feed intake, or feed-to-gain ratio. In nursery pigs, replacing corn with sorghum at graded ratios supports steady gains when amino acid balances are sustained. Furthermore, replacement of corn by 65% and 100% significantly enhances porcine serum antioxidant enzyme activity by 32.4% and 38.7%, respectively.

Mechanical and hydrothermal processing strategies dismantle the dense kafirin-tannin-starch complex. Hammer-mill pulverization through finer screens (such as 60 mesh versus 20 mesh) enhances pig digestible energy by 12.42%. Conditioning meal diets at 75 deg C establishes peak apparent ileal digestibility for crude protein (87.95%) and starch (92.26%) alongside maximum daily gain (988 g/d), while multi-carbohydrase and phytase supplementation systematically counteracts fibrous antinutritional barriers.

- Extrusion processing dramatically elevates standardized ileal digestibility of amino acids in domestic cultivars, raising Chinese sorghum lysine digestibility from 54.8% to 83.1%.

- Decreasing sorghum mean particle diameter from 1262 mm to 471 mm markedly enhances nutrient ileal and total tract digestibilities in 30 kg pigs.

- Graded corn substitution up to 100% expands backfat thickness by 4.3% while enriching beneficial arachidic and arachidonic acid fractions.

## Digestive Limitations and Formulative Boundaries

Application of raw unprocessed high-tannin sorghum in swine rations is constrained by digestive enzyme precipitation, endogenous nitrogen depletion, and impaired amino acid absorption, particularly within early-weaned cohorts.

- Weaned piglet trials reveal that apparent ileal digestibility of crude protein and essential amino acids declines linearly when dietary sorghum incorporation increases from 15% to 61%.

- High-tannin sorghum cultivars exhibit elevated neutral detergent fiber up to 15.24%, accelerating mucin secretion and endogenous losses of glutamic acid, aspartic acid, arginine, and threonine.

- Bioavailable energy predictive equations established in 25 to 50 kg growing pigs risk overestimating dietary net energy when applied directly to immature weaned pigs.

Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) represents the fifth most prominent global cereal grain and serves as a highly viable partial or total replacement for corn in swine rations, particularly during periods of volatile feedstuff pricing. abstract_en: The study evaluated the effects of folic acid (FA) on rumen fermentation parameters, antioxidant indicators and microbial population in dairy cows in vitro. Four early lactation Holstein dairy cows served as donors of ruminal fluid, and a dairy cow total mixed ration was utilized as the fermentation substrate. The supplementation levels of FA were 0, 1.5, 3.0, 4.5, 6.0, 7.5, and 9.0 mg/kg dry matter (DM), respectively. Following anaerobic incubation at 39 degrees Celsius for 24 h, ruminal DM degradability (DMD), gas production (GP), antioxidant indicators, fermentation parameters, microbial enzyme activities, and microbial populations were determined. Supplemental FA at 1.5, 3.0, and 4.5 mg/kg DM increased DMD (P<0.05). All FA treatments significantly increased ruminal fluid FA concentrations and total volatile fatty acids (TVFA), while reducing malondialdehyde concentrations (P<0.05). Superoxide dismutase, glutathione peroxidase, and total antioxidant capacity activities were enhanced by intermediate FA doses. Furthermore, FA addition promoted cellobiase and xylanase activities and expanded populations of total bacteria, protozoa, Ruminococcus flavefaciens, Ruminococcus albus, and Fibrobacter succinogenes (P<0.05). Quadratic responses across microbial groups indicate that excessive FA supplies fail to yield additive nutritional benefits. Overall, dietary FA supplementation improves the ruminal oxidative microenvironment and stimulates fiber digestion, with 1.5 to 3.0 mg/kg DM identified as the appropriate ruminal supply level.

## Dose-Dependent Rumen Fermentation Kinetics and Volatile Fatty Acid Profiles

In vitro batch culture demonstrated that dietary folic acid directly alters the metabolic pathways of mixed rumen microbial consortia. Incubation of total mixed ration substrate with ruminal fluid from donor cows revealed significant quadratic responses in both dry matter degradability and cumulative 24-hour gas production across the 0 to 9.0 mg/kg dry matter addition gradient. Substrate degradation peaked under intermediate dosages, with 1.5, 3.0, and 4.5 mg/kg dry matter exhibiting significantly higher degradability than the unsupplemented control and excessive dosages at 7.5 and 9.0 mg/kg dry matter.

Fermentation end-product profiling indicated that total volatile fatty acid concentrations increased markedly from 65.1 mmol/L in control cultures to 75.8 mmol/L at 4.5 mg/kg dry matter supplementation. Acetate accumulation followed an identical quadratic trend, rising from 40.4 mmol/L in the control to 48.8 mmol/L at 4.5 mg/kg dry matter, whereas propionate concentrations displayed no statistically significant divergence. Consequently, the acetate-to-propionate ratio increased from 3.49 to between 3.70 and 3.87 across treated groups. Ammonia nitrogen content rose concurrently from 42.5 mg/dL to 50.6 mg/dL at the highest dose, reflecting elevated microbial proteolytic cleavage in the absence of ruminal absorption barriers.

- Acetate concentrations rose significantly across all supplemented batches relative to 40.4 mmol/L in the control culture.

- Propionate, valerate, isobutyrate, and isovalerate concentrations maintained baseline stability without significant treatment shifts.

- Microbial crude protein concentrations remained stable across treatments, ranging from 0.55 to 0.60 g/L.

This in vitro investigation evaluated the dose-dependent effects of supplemental folic acid across seven levels ranging from 0 to 9.0 mg/kg dry matter on dairy cow rumen batch cultures. Rumen fluid harvested from four lactating Holstein cows was incubated for 24 hours with a standard dairy total mixed ration substrate. Supplemental folic acid enhanced antioxidant defense, elevated cellulolytic enzyme activities, and promoted populations of key cellulolytic bacteria, notably Ruminococcus flavefaciens and Ruminococcus albus. Moderate supplementation between 1.5 and 3.0 mg/kg dry matter optimized total volatile fatty acid output and dry matter degradability.

Exogenous folic acid supplementation induced substantial improvements in the ruminal antioxidant status. The alleviation of oxidative stress helps preserve anaerobic microbial membrane integrity during active substrate degradation.

Structural polysaccharide degradation was reinforced by enhanced microbial enzyme secretion. ## Taxonomic Restructuring of Rumen Microbiota and Optimal Delivery Ratios

Quantitative real-time PCR profiling identified pronounced shifts in primary bacterial and eukaryote taxa. Total bacterial abundance increased from 11.5 log copies/mL in control to 12.0 log copies/mL at 4.5 mg/kg dry matter. Cellulolytic specialists displayed pronounced proliferation: Ruminococcus albus expanded from 7.91 log copies/mL to 9.32 log copies/mL, while Ruminococcus flavefaciens advanced from 8.04 log copies/mL to 9.49 log copies/mL. Fungal and ciliate protozoal counts also expanded significantly upon folic acid provision, providing enhanced physical penetration and enzymatic disruption of fibrous plant cell walls.

At supraphysiological supplementation levels of 7.5 and 9.0 mg/kg dry matter, bacterial counts for Ruminococcus albus and Ruminococcus flavefaciens retreated toward baseline levels, demonstrating distinct quadratic regulation. Folic acid serves as an essential coenzyme precursor in microbial one-carbon transfer networks, yet excess free cofactor creates metabolic feedback inhibition. Balancing the ruminal requirement with post-ruminal systemic dairy cow demands indicates that protected folic acid supplements should be engineered with a 25% to 50% ruminal release profile to target in situ delivery between 1.5 and 3.0 mg/kg dry matter.

- Total protozoal density increased from 5.99 log copies/mL in control to 6.41-6.48 log copies/mL across all folic acid groups.

- Fibrobacter succinogenes density expanded from 10.6 log copies/mL in control to 11.0 log copies/mL under 6.0 mg/kg dry matter supplementation.

- Prevotella ruminicola and Romboutsia amylophilus populations expanded linearly with increasing folic acid doses.

## Methodological Constraints and Practical In Vivo Translation Boundaries

This evaluation was conducted using a closed in vitro batch culture system over 24 hours, which restricts dynamic nutrient outflow and physiological ruminal wall absorption. The absence of epithelial transport mechanisms caused an artificial accumulation of ammonia nitrogen that diverges from observed in vivo responses. Furthermore, while these findings establish clear biological thresholds for microbial fermentation, commercial implementation requires coordinated coated folic acid delivery technologies to avoid premature ruminal degradation.

- Batch culture conditions lack continuous liquid passage and active volatile fatty acid absorption through rumen papillae, confounding pH and microbial protein turnover.

- Uncoated folic acid is subject to rapid microbial disappearance in vivo (approximately 97%), demanding microencapsulation matrices engineered to release 25% to 50% within the reticulorumen.

## 1. Executive Abstract

The study evaluated the effects of folic acid (FA) on rumen fermentation parameters, antioxidant indicators and microbial population in dairy cows in vitro. Four early lactation Holstein dairy cows served as donors of ruminal fluid, and a dairy cow total mixed ration was utilized as the fermentation substrate. The supplementation levels of FA were 0, 1.5, 3.0, 4.5, 6.0, 7.5, and 9.0 mg/kg dry matter (DM), respectively. Following anaerobic incubation at 39 degrees Celsius for 24 h, ruminal DM degradability (DMD), gas production (GP), antioxidant indicators, fermentation parameters, microbial enzyme activities, and microbial populations were determined. Supplemental FA at 1.5, 3.0, and 4.5 mg/kg DM increased DMD (P<0.05). All FA treatments significantly increased ruminal fluid FA concentrations and total volatile fatty acids (TVFA), while reducing malondialdehyde concentrations (P<0.05). Superoxide dismutase, glutathione peroxidase, and total antioxidant capacity activities were enhanced by intermediate FA doses. Furthermore, FA addition promoted cellobiase and xylanase activities and expanded populations of total bacteria, protozoa, Ruminococcus flavefaciens, Ruminococcus albus, and Fibrobacter succinogenes (P<0.05). Quadratic responses across microbial groups indicate that excessive FA supplies fail to yield additive nutritional benefits. Overall, dietary FA supplementation improves the ruminal oxidative microenvironment and stimulates fiber digestion, with 1.5 to 3.0 mg/kg DM identified as the appropriate ruminal supply level.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Dry matter degradability and 24-hour cumulative gas production increased significantly at 1.5 to 4.5 mg/kg DM supplemental folic acid (P<0.05).
- Folic acid supplementation reduced malondialdehyde from 3.84 nmol/L in control to 2.18-2.74 nmol/L across treated groups while elevating superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase activities.
- Total volatile fatty acid concentration rose from 65.1 mmol/L in control to peak values of 73.9-75.8 mmol/L at 3.0 to 4.5 mg/kg DM supplementation.
- Populations of cellulolytic species including Ruminococcus albus, Ruminococcus flavefaciens, and Fibrobacter succinogenes increased significantly in response to folic acid additions.
- An optimal ruminal folic acid target of 1.5 to 3.0 mg/kg DM suggests rumen-protected folic acid formulations should provide a 25% to 50% ruminal release fraction.

analysis_markdown_en:
A statewide germplasm investigation across Jiangxi Province evaluated 216 glutinous rice landraces assembled through national crop surveys. Geographical distribution analysis demonstrated that 80.6% of accessions cluster within mountainous prefectures, led by Shangrao (48 accessions) and Ganzhou (46 accessions). Two-year field agronomic trials and post-harvest grain quality assays confirmed wide phenotypic variability, encompassing indica (77.8%) and japonica (22.2%) subspecies alongside eight pigmented pericarps. Through systematic multi-trait screening, ten elite accessions were identified, exhibiting panicle grain counts up to 236.6 spikelets, seed setting rates reaching 94.0%, and theoretical grain yields up to 9.1 t/hm2.

## Geographical Dispersion and Morphological Architecture Diversity

Systematic field collections conducted under the Third National Survey and Collection of Crop Germplasm Resources assembled 216 glutinous rice landraces across Jiangxi Province. Spatial analysis revealed marked geographic divergence across 11 prefecture-level divisions. Mountainous jurisdictions with extensive agrarian traditions, complex microclimates, and ethnic minority settlements retained the vast majority of local cultivars: Shangrao contributed 48 accessions, Ganzhou contributed 46, Fuzhou contributed 31, Ji'an contributed 29, and Yichun contributed 20, collectively representing 80.6% of the collection. Conversely, industrialized plain sectors characterized by intensive commercial monoculture and hybrid adoption exhibited severe germplasm attrition, with Nanchang, Jiujiang, Jingdezhen, Pingxiang, Xinyu, and Yingtan contributing only 12, 9, 8, 5, 4, and 4 accessions, respectively.

Morphological evaluation demonstrated broad structural adaptation. The majority of landraces exhibited green leaf blades (94.4%), straw-yellow glume tips (86.1%), glabrous leaf pubescence (87.5%), and awnless panicles (66.2%). Intermediate panicle architecture was observed in 66.2% of entries, while erect and intermediate flag leaf angles accounted for 36.6% and 53.2%, respectively. Lodging evaluation classified 59.3% as intermediate and 21.3% as erect, confirming robust field standing ability under regional rainfall conditions.

- Ecological distribution: 80.6% concentrated in mountainous prefectures (Shangrao, Ganzhou, Fuzhou, Ji'an, Yichun); 19.4% in industrialized plain corridors.

- Botanical classification: 168 indica types (77.8%) and 48 japonica types (22.2%); all 216 accessions are lowland paddy ecotypes without upland forms.

## Two-Year Agronomic Variation and Yield Determinants

Replicated field trials spanning the 2023 and 2024 seasons at the Gao'an experimental station revealed normal distribution and highly significant inter-annual correlation (P<0.01) across all measured quantitative traits. Heading date ranged from 61.0 d to 131.0 d, with 53.2% of entries heading under 90 d. Plant height ranged between 88.3 cm and 168.3 cm with an overall mean of 121.8 cm, wherein 46.3% measured below 120.0 cm, exhibiting favorable dwarfing traits suitable for lodging resistance during late-stage grain filling.

Yield component parameters exhibited substantial phenotypic coefficients of variation (CV), ranging from 7.9% to 29.2%. Primary branch count ranged from 7.3 to 16.4, while secondary branch count spanned 7.2 to 54.6. Total spikelets per panicle varied between 67.2 and 226.1 grains, with Lianxinuodao recording the highest panicle capacity. Seed setting rates averaged 84.9% across seasons (ranging from 52.3% to 96.6%), and thousand-grain weight averaged 24.8 g (spanning 17.0 g to 35.4 g), demonstrating rich genetic elasticity for recombinant yield breeding.

- Phenotypic coefficients of variation: Highest plasticity observed in secondary branch count (29.2% CV) and panicles per plant (23.5% CV).

- High-capacity thresholds: 10 landraces exceeded 200 total grains per panicle; 19 accessions surpassed 92.0% seed setting rate; 5 entries exceeded 29.0 g thousand-grain weight.

## Grain Endosperm Starch Properties and Elite Selection

Physicochemical grain quality assays demonstrated excellent waxy endosperm characteristics. Amylose content ranged from 0.4% to 2.6% with a mean of 1.4%, with 92.6% of accessions measuring below 2.0%. Gel consistency averaged 110.2 mm (ranging from 81.0 mm to 123.0 mm), with 98.6% meeting high-grade glutinous standards (>=100 mm). Rapid Visco Analyzer (RVA) pasting profiles displayed high divergence, with CVs exceeding 20% for peak viscosity, hot paste viscosity, cool paste viscosity, breakdown value, and setback value.

Integrated multi-trait index selection isolated ten elite landraces exhibiting well-balanced plant stature, high spikelet density, robust seed setting, and optimal waxy cooking properties. These ten accessions exhibited heading dates between 81 d and 101 d, plant heights between 116.0 cm and 127.7 cm, effective panicle numbers between 8.2 and 10.3 per plant, and total grains per panicle from 183.4 to 236.6. Theoretical grain yields ranged from 7.1 t/hm2 in Beijingnuo to 9.1 t/hm2 in Ziyunuo, establishing immediate parental donors for specialized waxy rice breeding.

- Quality standards: 98.6% of accessions attained soft gel consistency (>=100 mm); mean amylose content stood at 1.4%.

- Top-yielding donor: Purple-pericarp landrace Ziyunuo achieved 9.1 t/hm2 theoretical yield with 223.5 grains per panicle and 87.1% seed setting rate.

## Genomic Characterization Gaps and In Situ Conservation Constraints

Although systematic phenotypic and quality profiling identified outstanding accessions, several genomic and ecological limitations remain to be resolved prior to commercial deployment.

- The current evaluation relies solely on macro-phenotypic observations and RVA pasting parameters; population genomic structure and target gene loci have not yet been resolved via whole-genome resequencing or SSR markers.

- Most collected landrace accessions initially exhibited genetic heterozygosity and admixture degradation, requiring 5 to 6 years of pedigree purification to achieve homozygosity before stable field screening.

- Field trials were conducted at a single experimental site in Gao'an, necessitating multi-environment trials across divergent ecological zones to verify genotype-by-environment stability.

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

analysis_markdown_en:
## Vegetative Morphology and Leaf Nutrient Dynamics Under Factorial Regimes

Banana displays high demand for potassium during vegetative and reproductive stages to maintain osmotic balance, enzyme activation, and assimilate transport. Under experimental conditions in Nanning, severe restriction of potassium input (100 or 300 g plant-1 K2O) notably impeded pseudostem enlargement and vertical extension. In the unsupplemented lowest potassium treatment (K1S1), plant height was restricted to 222.64 cm and stem girth reached only 65.68 cm. Incorporating exogenous sodium selenate (Na2SeO4) at 0.1 to 0.5 g plant-1 effectively counteracted potassium-deficiency dwarfism, raising plant height up to 248.77 cm in treatment K3S2, which exceeded K1S1 by 11.74%. When potassium was applied at adequate to high levels (500 and 700 g plant-1 K2O), selenium supplementation had no statistically significant effect on vertical height but continued to promote radial stem expansion, culminating in a maximum stem girth of 71.88 cm in K3S4.

Leaf tissue diagnostics revealed that foliar potassium and selenium concentrations responded proportionally to their respective supply. Foliar potassium peaked at 4.52 g 100 g-1 in treatment K2S2 (a 22.83% increase relative to 3.68 g 100 g-1 in K1S1). Exogenous selenium drenching under 100 and 300 g plant-1 K2O markedly enhanced leaf potassium accumulation, indicating that selenium facilitates root absorption and xylem translocation of potassium under deficient conditions. Foliar selenium concentration was highest 30 days post-drenching (reaching 14.43 mg kg-1 in K1S4 and 13.89 mg kg-1 in K2S4) before attenuating over time, dropping to 2.95 mg kg-1 in K1S4 after 90 days. Notably, low-potassium conditions favored greater leaf selenium accumulation than high-potassium conditions.

- Deficient potassium supply severely restricted vegetative growth, but 0.1 to 0.5 g plant-1 Na2SeO4 restored stem girth and height.

- Selenium drenching under low potassium significantly stimulated leaf potassium accumulation, peaking at 4.52 g 100 g-1.

- Foliar selenium declined over a 90-day post-application window across all potassium regimes.

This study evaluates the agronomic and biochemical interactions between reduced potassium fertilization and exogenous selenium drenching in field-grown banana (cv. Guijiao 9). A two-factor randomized block design tested K2O application rates of 100, 300, 500, and 700 g plant-1 crossed with Na2SeO4 rates of 0.0, 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 g plant-1. Severe potassium deficiency markedly suppressed vegetative development, single fruit weight, and yield. However, supplementing 0.1 to 0.5 g plant-1 Na2SeO4 under low-potassium regimes mitigated stress, elevated leaf potassium accumulation, and optimized fruit finger morphology. Combining 300 to 500 g plant-1 K2O with 0.1 g plant-1 Na2SeO4 maximized yield, while 0.3 g plant-1 Na2SeO4 enhanced soluble solids, starch, vitamin C, and potassium contents, achieving regional selenium biofortification standards.

## Fruit Yield Metrics and Finger Morphological Differentiation

Potassium deficiency imposed severe penalties on reproductive sink capacity and individual fruit development. In treatment K1S1, yield per plant dropped to 23.60 kg and single fruit weight declined to 163.27 g. When exogenous selenium was applied to potassium-restricted trees, yield metrics recovered substantially. The combination of 300 g plant-1 K2O with 0.1 g plant-1 Na2SeO4 (K2S2) produced the highest yield per plant across all 16 treatments at 26.80 kg, exceeding K1S1 by 13.56%. Similarly, single fruit weight peaked at 179.58 g in treatment K3S2 (500 g plant-1 K2O with 0.1 g plant-1 Na2SeO4), representing a 9.99% gain over K1S1. Conversely, supplying selenium under the conventional high potassium rate (700 g plant-1 K2O) depressed single fruit weight and overall yield, demonstrating that excessive combined nutrient loading can induce negative physiological interactions.

Morphometric assessment of the third fruit hand demonstrated that selenium and potassium synergistically governed finger dimensions and finger counts. The total number of fruit fingers ranged from 128.33 in K3S1 to 136.33 in K2S2. Outer fruit finger length reached its maximum of 23.10 cm under the high-potassium unsupplemented control (K4S1), which was 6.85% longer than the 21.62 cm recorded in K2S1. Outer fruit finger circumference attained a high of 12.89 cm in K3S2, exceeding K4S3 (12.13 cm) by 6.27%. Inner fruit finger length also exhibited positive responses to balanced nutrition, varying between 21.20 cm in K1S1 and 22.78 cm in K4S1, while inner fruit finger circumference remained stable across treatments.

- Single fruit weight peaked at 179.58 g under treatment K3S2, while selenium addition at 700 g plant-1 K2O depressed fruit weight.

- Moderate selenium application enlarged fruit finger circumference and length under reduced potassium regimes.

## Postharvest Fruit Biochemical Quality and Selenium Biofortification

Fruit chemical composition at commercial maturity responded sensitively to potassium-selenium interactions. In the unsupplemented low-potassium control (K1S1), vitamin C and potassium concentrations dropped to trial lows of 10.86 mg 100 g-1 and 300.00 mg 100 g-1, alongside soluble solids of 16.23%. Introducing selenium under reduced potassium conditions significantly enhanced sugar and organic metabolite accumulation. Soluble solids peaked at 19.87% in K1S3 (a 22.43% elevation over K1S1). Starch content reached a maximum of 8.66 g 100 g-1 in K2S3, outperforming the K4S1 baseline of 5.31 g 100 g-1 by 63.09%. Vitamin C also reached its pinnacle in K2S3 at 15.01 mg 100 g-1 (a 38.21% gain over K1S1), while fruit potassium peaked at 351.33 mg 100 g-1 in K3S3.

Non-supplemented treatments exhibited negligible fruit selenium (0.00 ug kg-1), confirming native soil selenium bioavailability was insufficient for fruit enrichment despite a total soil selenium baseline of 0.68 mg kg-1. Drenching Na2SeO4 at 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 g plant-1 elevated pulp selenium concentrations to 13.33-16.33 ug kg-1, 33.33-36.00 ug kg-1, and 38.33-51.67 ug kg-1, respectively. Every selenium-drenched regime met the regional selenium-enriched fruit threshold of 10 to 100 ug kg-1 defined by DB45/T 1061-2014, establishing that soil drenching during vigorous vegetative development provides dependable biofortification without perturbing titratable acidity.

- Vitamin C and starch concentrations peaked at 15.01 mg 100 g-1 and 8.66 g 100 g-1 in treatment K2S3.

- Fruit potassium concentration was maximized at 351.33 mg 100 g-1 under 500 g plant-1 K2O and 0.3 g plant-1 Na2SeO4.

- All selenium-treated bananas satisfied the 10 to 100 ug kg-1 biofortification standard, peaking at 51.67 ug kg-1 in K2S4.

## Experimental Scope and Agronomic Boundary Conditions

The field trial establishes actionable fertilizer reduction protocols specifically for Guijiao 9 banana within subtropical monsoon soil environments having neutral pH and moderate baseline nutrients.

- The experimental soil baseline featured a pH of 7.12, organic matter of 15.11 g kg-1, available potassium of 164.30 mg kg-1, and baseline selenium of 0.68 mg kg-1; responses may differ in acidic or severely depleted soils.

- Root drenching with Na2SeO4 was evaluated as a single application of 1 L per plant at 210 days after planting, precluding comparisons with split applications or foliar spray methods.

- Excessive input combinations, specifically 700 g plant-1 K2O paired with selenium, reduced single fruit weight, delineating an upper threshold beyond which co-application becomes counterproductive.

Flag leaf physiological attributes, Logistic grain filling parameters, total grain yields, and irrigation water use efficiency (IWUE) were quantified across main stems and tillers. Under W70, S23 maintained significantly higher post-anthesis flag leaf chlorophyll relative content, net photosynthetic rate, sucrose accumulation, and superoxide dismutase activity alongside lower malondialdehyde content than other treatments. Furthermore, the mean and maximum grain filling rates and active filling duration were prolonged in primary and secondary tillers. Consequently, W70 enhanced S23 single-plant yield by 8.39% to 45.16% and hectare yield by 5.76% to 44.32% relative to other regimes. While matching W90 grain yields, W70 reduced irrigation volumes by 14.82% to 52.61% and elevated IWUE by 22.33% to 122.74%, confirming that large-spike cultivars optimize water productivity under deficit supplemental replenishment.

## Physiological Canopy Senescence and Tiller Assimilate Dynamics

In the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain, seasonal precipitation patterns regularly mismatch the evapotranspiration demands of winter wheat during jointing and grain filling. Soil moisture depletion accelerates premature senescence, impairs light interception, and shortens the grain accumulation phase. Evaluating whether targeted moisture deficits influence tillers uniformly requires granular tracking of assimilate generation across specific stem tiers. Flag leaves of main stems (O) and successive tillers (I and II) demonstrate distinct physiological longevity depending on whether supplemental replenishment provides adequate hydration without generating hypoxic soil saturation.

Measurements of chlorophyll content, net photosynthetic rate, and enzymatic antioxidant systems revealed that maintaining 70% relative soil water content in the 0-40 cm layer (W70) prevented the abrupt declines observed under rainfed cultivation (W0). At 28 days post-anthesis, flag leaf net photosynthetic rate under W70 was 21.7% to 30.5% higher than W0 and exceeded full irrigation (W90) by 11.4% to 16.1% in tiller leaves. In parallel, superoxide dismutase activity remained significantly elevated while malondialdehyde concentrations dropped by 16.2% to 23.5% relative to W0, reflecting diminished membrane lipid peroxidation. These physiological enhancements were pronounced in the large-spike cultivar Shannong 23, allowing both primary and secondary tillers to sustain active sucrose synthesis via sucrose phosphate synthase into late grain filling.

- Flag leaf sucrose content under W70 increased by 71.0% to 86.4% across stem tiers relative to rainfed controls.

- Sucrose phosphate synthase activity in tiller flag leaves under W70 exceeded W90 levels by 12.8% to 21.6% at 28 days post-anthesis.

- Soluble protein reserves remained stabilized in S23 tiller flag leaves, averting nitrogen remobilization collapse.

## Stem-Specific Logistic Grain Filling Kinetics and Biomass Distribution

Grain mass accumulation follows a sigmoidal trajectory described by Logistic growth modeling, where the ultimate single-grain weight depends jointly on maximum filling rate, mean filling rate, and active filling duration. Excessive supplemental irrigation often leads to canopy lodging risk and impairs tiller grain filling rates, whereas severe water stress prematurely curtails active duration. Partitioning the ear dynamics across main stems and specific tiller nodes elucidates the structural divergence between ear architecture types under regulated soil deficits.

Under W70 conditions, the large-spike cultivar Shannong 23 achieved superior grain filling parameters compared to the medium-spike cultivar Jimai 22, particularly within the lower tiller hierarchy. The active grain filling period for S23 on the second tiller reached 29.46 d with a maximum filling rate of 2.25 mg grain-1 d-1, surpassing the corresponding J22 values of 28.28 d and 2.15 mg grain-1 d-1. Although full irrigation (W90) maintained high main stem performance, it depressed the maximum and mean filling rates of primary and secondary tillers. Regulated deficit replenishment at 70% field status concentrated assimilate transport into viable ears while curtailing non-productive tillering sink competition.

- Logistic fit coefficients of determination exceeded 0.99 across all tested tiller cohorts and irrigation regimes.

- Active grain filling duration of the main stem reached 27.82 d in S23 under W70 compared to 25.69 d in J22 under W70.

- Third tillers (III) under W70 exhibited lower filling rates than W90, reflecting sink suppression of late, non-dominant tillers.

## Agronomic Yield Components and Irrigation Water Conservation

Balancing grain productivity against water consumption is critical for sustainable agricultural production across water-limited plain environments. Over-irrigation frequently promotes luxury vegetative transpiration through excessive non-productive tiller proliferation, causing higher seasonal water consumption without yield improvements. In contrast, precision deficit supplementation matches irrigation delivery strictly to moisture deficits measured across the active root extraction depth.

Hectare grain yield in S23 reached 8039.85 kg hm-2 in 2019-2020 and 8738.92 kg hm-2 in 2020-2021 under W70, statistically equivalent to the 7949.59 kg hm-2 and 8840.64 kg hm-2 obtained under intensive W90 replenishment. Total irrigation depth applied under W70 was 60.26 mm and 71.54 mm across the two seasons, representing a reduction of 44.6% to 45.1% compared to W90. Consequently, irrigation water use efficiency peaked at 133.42 kg hm-2 mm-1 and 122.15 kg hm-2 mm-1, outperforming J22 by 22.2% to 22.4% due to fewer non-productive tillers and superior per-spike grain setting.

- Seasonal irrigation depth under W70 was reduced by 48.79 mm in 2019-2020 and 59.63 mm in 2020-2021 relative to W90.

- Single-plant grain yield of S23 reached 3.63 g plant-1 (2019-2020) and 3.86 g plant-1 (2020-2021) under W70.

- Three-way ANOVA confirmed significant interaction effects among growing season, cultivar, and irrigation on hectare grain yield.

## Soil Profiling Boundaries and Phenotypic Constraints

This research evaluates loam soil profiles in Shandong Province with fixed supplemental watering depths, which may differ across distinct soil textures, variable sowing densities, and fluctuating regional precipitation profiles.

- Supplemental irrigation calculations were calibrated exclusively to the 0-40 cm soil profile, leaving deeper subsoil moisture extraction unmeasured.

- Field trials were limited to a fixed seedling density of 225 plants m-2 across two test sites in Tai'an, Shandong Province.

- The physiological advantages of the large-spike cultivar depend upon timely water application at jointing and anthesis; delayed replenishment under severe seasonal drought may impair spikelet fertility differently.

## 1. Executive Abstract

To investigate the effects of water-saving supplemental irrigation on photosynthesis, senescence, and grain filling characteristics of flag leaves across different tillering stems, field trials were performed during the 2019-2020 and 2020-2021 growing seasons using the medium-spike cultivar Jimai 22 (J22) and the large-spike cultivar Shannong 23 (S23). While matching W90 grain yields, W70 reduced irrigation volumes by 14.82% to 52.61% and elevated IWUE by 22.33% to 122.74%, confirming that large-spike cultivars optimize water productivity under deficit supplemental replenishment.

- Water-saving supplemental irrigation (W70) reduced total seasonal irrigation by 44.6% to 45.1% compared to full irrigation (W90) while maintaining equivalent grain yields.

## Rice Yield Stability Under Graded Chemical Fertilizer Reduction

In the primary agricultural basin of northern Guangxi, excessive reliance on synthetic mineral inputs has historically degraded soil physicochemical quality while diminishing nutrient utilization efficiency. In this two-year field investigation utilizing cultivars 'Yexiangyou 818' and 'Shenliangyou 5814', standard chemical input was paired with a fixed basal dressing of 4 500 kg·hm-2 commercial organic fertilizer derived from humified lignite powder, soybean meal, and animal hide waste. Yield component analysis demonstrated that key agronomic determinants—specifically productive panicle density (238.27×10^4 to 246.40×10^4 hm-2), spikelet fertility, and 1 000-grain weight—did not experience statistically significant depression across treatments T1 through T5 compared to conventional chemical management (CK1).

Actual harvested paddy grain yields across combined regimes T1, T2, T3, T4, and T5 reached 8.40±0.30, 8.38±0.29, 8.37±0.31, 8.24±0.39, and 8.22±0.41 t·hm-2, respectively, maintaining statistical parity with CK1 (8.57±0.52 t·hm-2). Conversely, complete omission of chemical fertilizers in T6 and unfertilized CK2 resulted in steep yield declines of 13.0% and 19.1% relative to CK1, underscoring that organic nitrogen mineralization alone cannot satisfy early-to-mid vegetative demand without supplemental mineral nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Consequently, coupling 4 500 kg·hm-2 organic amendment with a 30% reduction in chemical fertilizer (T5) successfully stabilizes single-cropping rice output.

- Productive spikes remained between 238.27×10^4·hm-2 and 246.40×10^4·hm-2 across all chemical reduction combinations (T1–T5).

- Grain setting rates remained robust across combined treatments (83.78% to 85.00%), paralleling conventional chemical fertilization (86.56%).

- Theoretical yield under the 30% reduction regime (T5) reached 9.15±0.76 t·hm-2 compared to 9.70±1.46 t·hm-2 under CK1.

This two-year field agronomy study evaluates partial chemical fertilizer reduction combined with commercial organic fertilizer in single-cropping rice in northern Guangxi. Testing 4 500 kg·hm-2 organic fertilizer alongside 0% to 100% of standard chemical inputs against conventional and unfertilized controls revealed that reducing chemical fertilizer by 10% to 30% sustained actual rice yields (8.22 to 8.40 t·hm-2) without significant differences from 100% chemical fertilization (8.57 t·hm-2). Concurrently, combined amendments elevated soil organic matter by 22.1% to 31.1%, enhanced catalase and transglycosidase activities, stimulated fungal richness, and suppressed fungal pathogens, establishing a 30% synthetic reduction as an optimal sustainable regime.

## Pedological Amelioration and Soil Enzymatic Dynamics

Application of commercial organic fertilizer markedly influenced soil chemical properties in the 16 cm plow layer. Soil organic matter rose from 21.18±2.68 g·kg-1 in CK1 to between 25.87±1.18 and 27.77±1.54 g·kg-1 in organic-treated plots, representing statistically significant gains of 22.1% to 31.1%. Soil buffering capacity also improved, with T4 raising baseline pH by 0.27 units, mitigating acidification induced by continuous synthetic nitrogen application. Total nitrogen, cation exchange capacity, available phosphorus, and available potassium exhibited positive upward trends across all combined fertilization plots relative to unamended controls.

Soil enzymatic profiles, which serve as sensitive bioindicators of pedological metabolic activity, responded dynamically to fertilizer composition. Transglycosidase activity increased by 20.5% in T3 compared to CK1, while catalase activity increased by 12.3% in T3 and 13.6% in T4, reflecting heightened oxidative degradation of metabolic peroxides and stimulated aerobic microflora. Furthermore, urease activity under T4 and T5 exceeded organic-only application (T6) by 29.9% and 31.7%, while protease activity in T1 and T5 rose by 24.1% and 24.9% over T6, confirming that synchronized organic-inorganic inputs foster robust enzymatic cycling of macromolecular nitrogen.

## Microbial Community Reconfiguration and Driver Factor Analysis

High-throughput Illumina sequencing targeting bacterial 16S rRNA and fungal ITS1 regions revealed substantial phylogenetic remodeling within the rice rhizosphere. While bacterial Shannon diversity declined in treatments T2, T3, and T5, fungal species richness (Chao1 index) expanded significantly across all organic amendments relative to CK1. At the phylum level, combined fertilization increased the relative abundance of Proteobacteria (by 11.3% to 16.0% in T1 and T5), Bacteroidota (by 3.0% to 10.9%), and Actinobacteriota (by 0.9% to 21.1%), whereas oligotrophic Acidobacteriota declined by 8.1% to 29.3%.

In the fungal microbiome, combined treatments produced widespread reductions in pathogenic Ascomycota (1.9% to 41.7%) and Basidiomycota (10.5% in T1 and 31.5% in T5), while saprophytic Mortierellomycota expanded by 8.7% to 149.0%. Linear discriminant analysis effect size (LEfSe) differentiated 42 bacterial and 19 fungal diagnostic clades across treatments, identifying biomarker enrichment of Desulfobacterota and Myxococcota under T5. Redundancy analysis confirmed that edaphic variables significantly govern microbial assembly, pinpointing urease activity (R2=0.608 1) and soil organic matter (R2=0.592 5) as the predominant regulatory determinants for bacteria and fungi, respectively.

- Proteobacteria abundance increased by 11.3% in T1 and 16.0% in T5 relative to conventional fertilization.

- Mortierellomycota exhibited relative abundance increases ranging from 8.7% up to 149.0% across combined fertilization plots.

- Correlation analysis highlighted strong positive links between soil protease and Actinobacteriota, Desulfobacterota, and Proteobacteria.

## Pedological Boundaries and Agronomic Transferability Constraints

This study was conducted within a two-year experimental timeframe in a single-cropping rice agroecosystem in Yangshuo County, northern Guangxi, characterized by hydromorphic paddy soil with baseline available phosphorus of 49.7 mg·kg-1 and pH 5.8.

- The experimental duration spanned two consecutive cropping seasons (2022–2023), which was sufficient to record significant shifts in organic matter, enzyme activities, and microbial profiles, but represents a relatively brief window for detecting significant divergence in slow-turnover mineral fractions such as total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and total potassium.

- Surrounding agricultural plots featured intensive continuous rotations of crops such as water chestnut and arrowhead with elevated historical fertilizer inputs, potentially dampening macro-nutrient treatment contrasts via irrigation water exchange.

- The empirical evaluation focused on agronomic and soil biological metrics; comprehensive farm-scale input-output budgets, labor expenditures for organic manure application, and greenhouse gas flux monitoring were not quantified.

analysis_markdown_en:
Cyclic heat stress markedly compromises poultry carcass characteristics and induces postmortem glycolysis acceleration, oxidative degradation, and adverse fatty acid shifts in broiler breast muscle. In this 14-day controlled trial with 192 male Arbor Acres broilers exposed to cyclic heat stress (34±1) °C, dietary chitosan oligosaccharide (COS) supplementation mitigated postmortem glycogen breakdown and lactic acid accumulation by attenuating hexokinase activity. Furthermore, dietary COS restored essential antioxidant enzyme defenses (CAT, T-SOD, and GSH-Px), suppressed malondialdehyde generation, and enriched cardioprotective polyunsaturated fatty acids including DHA and EPA+DHA, with 200 mg/kg identified as the optimum dosage.

## Postmortem Glycolysis and Muscle Acidification Kinetics

High ambient thermal loads induce systemic endocrine alterations and hyperventilation in modern fast-growing broilers, disturbing postmortem energy homeostasis in skeletal muscle. Under cyclic heat stress conditions (34±1 °C for 8 h daily), rapid consumption of cellular energy triggers accelerated postmortem glycolysis. In this study, the untreated heat stress cohort experienced rapid depletion of breast muscle glycogen (0.84±0.07 mg/g compared to 1.15±0.16 mg/g in thermoneutral controls) and free glucose (0.66±0.17 mmol/g compared to 1.51±0.34 mmol/g), driven by significant upregulation of hexokinase activity to 129.70±7.54 U/mg.

The resulting accumulation of lactic acid (1.55±0.17 mmol/g versus 1.04±0.11 mmol/g in controls) precipitated a steep decline in muscle pH, reaching 6.11±0.11 at 45 min and 5.31±0.04 at 24 h postmortem. This premature acidification while carcass temperatures remain elevated denatures sarcoplasmic proteins and increases drip loss to 5.20±0.64%. Dietary addition of chitosan oligosaccharide at both 200 mg/kg and 400 mg/kg suppressed hexokinase hyperactivity, preserved residual glycogen reserves, and lowered lactic acid accumulation to 1.08±0.20 mmol/g and 0.96±0.23 mmol/g, successfully maintaining 24 h postmortem pH above 5.85.

- Hexokinase activity was suppressed from 129.70±7.54 U/mg in heat-stressed birds to 104.72±10.64 U/mg at 200 mg/kg COS.

- Postmortem glycogen retention was elevated from 0.84±0.07 mg/g to 1.18±0.16 mg/g with 200 mg/kg COS.

- Drip loss decreased numerically from 5.20±0.64% under unsupplemented heat stress toward baseline thermoneutral values (4.34±0.38%).

## Enzymatic Antioxidant Defense and Free-Radical Scavenging

Thermal stress stimulates mitochondrial respiratory electron leakage, leading to systemic overproduction of reactive oxygen species in avian skeletal tissues. When endogenous radical generation outpaces clearance mechanisms, extensive lipid peroxidation takes place, altering structural membrane integrity and deteriorating myofibrillar protein function. In the heat stress group, malondialdehyde concentrations rose markedly to 0.17±0.04 nmol/mgprot, accompanied by severe depletion of primary antioxidant enzyme activities including catalase (0.11±0.02 U/mgprot), total superoxide dismutase (129.56±16.66 U/mgprot), and glutathione peroxidase (5.21±2.42 U/mgprot).

Chitosan oligosaccharide contains active primary and secondary hydroxyl groups as well as amino moieties across its glucosamine oligomer backbone, enabling direct radical quenching and transcriptional upregulation of host antioxidant defenses. Broilers receiving dietary COS demonstrated robust recovery of total superoxide dismutase (154.78±18.91 U/mgprot at 200 mg/kg and 167.59±18.43 U/mgprot at 400 mg/kg) alongside dramatic elevations in glutathione peroxidase activity exceeding 12.40 U/mgprot. This enhanced enzymatic shield curtailed lipid peroxidation, reducing breast muscle malondialdehyde down to 0.06±0.04 nmol/mgprot.

- Catalase activity expanded from 0.11±0.02 U/mgprot in the heat stress group to 0.21±0.04 U/mgprot (200 mg/kg COS) and 0.27±0.10 U/mgprot (400 mg/kg COS).

- Glutathione peroxidase activity increased by more than twofold in both COS-supplemented groups compared to unsupplemented heat stress (5.21±2.42 U/mgprot).

- Malondialdehyde accumulation was suppressed below the baseline levels observed in non-stressed thermoneutral birds (0.12±0.03 nmol/mgprot).

## Breast Muscle Fatty Acid Profiles and Nutritional Quality Indices

Thermal exposure modifies hepatic lipid metabolism and accelerates systemic degradation of sensitive polyunsaturated fatty acids. Broilers exposed to cyclic heat stress exhibited marked reductions in health-promoting polyunsaturated fatty acids, such as docosahexaenoic acid (6.60±1.35 μg/g versus 9.27±0.84 μg/g in controls) and combined EPA+DHA (10.01±1.90 μg/g versus 13.51±1.62 μg/g in controls). Concurrently, heat stress elevated atherogenic and thrombogenic saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids, notably myristic acid (23.66±3.67 μg/g) and palmitoleic acid (310.66±53.56 μg/g), shifting nutritional indices unfavorably.

Inclusion of chitosan oligosaccharide reversed these lipid shifts by shielding double bonds within long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids from reactive oxygen attacks. Dietary COS significantly restored gamma-linolenic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, and EPA+DHA levels, while reducing myristic acid to 19.69±1.67 μg/g (200 mg/kg) and 17.06±3.59 μg/g (400 mg/kg). Notably, the 200 mg/kg dosage improved the unsaturated to saturated fatty acid ratio (UFA/SFA: 3.49±1.00 versus 2.25±0.78 in HS), increased the hypocholesterolemic to hypercholesterolemic ratio (HHR: 5.74±1.76 versus 3.05±1.50 in HS), and lowered atherogenic and thrombogenic risks.

- Combined EPA+DHA reached 12.49±0.67 μg/g in the HSC200 group compared to 10.01±1.90 μg/g under heat stress alone.

- The index of atherogenicity (IA) was reduced from 0.38±0.20 in the HS group to 0.19±0.07 at 200 mg/kg COS.

- The health-promoting index (HPI) recovered from 3.20±1.40 under heat stress to 5.66±1.66 with 200 mg/kg COS addition.

## Trial Constraints and Commercial Applicability Boundaries

This study evaluated male Arbor Acres broilers during a specific finisher window under controlled cyclic thermal protocols, establishing dietary dosage parameters while highlighting areas requiring commercial verification.

- The investigation tested a single 14-day intervention period (days 28 to 42 of age) using 192 male Arbor Acres broilers, leaving female broilers and alternative commercial genotypes unexamined.

- The experimental temperature regimen adhered strictly to an 8-hour cycle of (34±1) °C with 65% to 75% relative humidity, which may not capture unpredictable multi-day heatwave dynamics.

- While 200 mg/kg proved optimal for lipid indices and postmortem pH stabilization, 400 mg/kg produced greater reductions in abdominal fat percentage (1.25±0.25% vs 1.75±0.30% in HS), indicating divergent dosage targets depending on carcass priorities.

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

Here, garlic cultivar 'P196' was cultivated in a split-plot pot trial to evaluate the physiological and agronomic responses to three microplastic types (polyvinyl chloride [PVC], polyethylene [PE], and polystyrene [PS]; particle size 13 μm) across four concentration gradients (0, 10, 100, and 1 000 mg · kg-1). High microplastic accumulation imposed substantial phytotoxicity on garlic development, causing significant dose-dependent reductions in vegetative biomass, bulb yield, bulb nutritional quality, photosynthetic pigment retention, gas exchange rates, maximum photochemical efficiency (Fv/Fm), and actual photochemical efficiency [Y(II)], alongside an elevation in non-photochemical quenching (NPQ). Conversely, low-level exposure at 10 mg · kg-1 exerted a hormetic stimulatory effect, increasing plant height by 6.80%, leaf fresh weight by 12.66%, and pseudostem fresh weight by 19.00%. Among the evaluated polymers, PE exhibited the strongest phytotoxicity, reducing garlic yield by 7.09% compared with PVC.

## Dose-Dependent Vegetative Growth and Bulb Yield Divergence

Agronomic assessment revealed that microplastic polymers in agricultural soil exert pronounced regulatory control over vegetative development and bulb yield in Allium sativum L. cv. P196. The physiological responses followed distinct concentration thresholds, characterized by stimulation under low soil concentrations and progressive phytotoxicity under elevated concentrations. In the 10 mg · kg-1 treatment, garlic exhibited stimulatory growth across aboveground vegetative organs, attaining maximum values for plant height at 93.51 cm, leaf fresh weight at 91.46 g, and pseudostem fresh weight at 72.15 g.

In contrast, subterranean root expansion, pseudostem diameter, and storage bulb formation experienced dose-dependent inhibition without any stimulatory window. Elevating microplastic contamination to 1 000 mg · kg-1 reduced root fresh weight to 26.07 g compared to 47.10 g in the unamended control, while pseudostem thickness narrowed to 18.77 mm from 25.69 mm. Consequently, commercial bulb yield fell from 3.07 kg · m-2 in unamended control soil down to 2.14 kg · m-2 under 1 000 mg · kg-1 amendments, reflecting severe impairment of underground sink organ accumulation.

- Plant height increased to 93.51 cm under 10 mg · kg-1 but dropped to 77.69 cm at 1 000 mg · kg-1.

- Root biomass experienced the sharpest decline among organs, dropping from 47.10 g to 26.07 g at 1 000 mg · kg-1.

- Significant two-way interaction between polymer type and concentration was confirmed across all vegetative parameters.

This study investigates the physiological and agronomic effects of soil microplastics on garlic cultivar P196 using a split-plot experimental design. Three polymer types, polyvinyl chloride, polyethylene, and polystyrene at 13 μm particle size, were evaluated across four concentration gradients of 0, 10, 100, and 1 000 mg · kg-1. The findings demonstrate a distinct biphasic response: low-dose microplastic exposure at 10 mg · kg-1 stimulated vegetative growth and gas exchange, whereas higher concentrations imposed pronounced phytotoxicity. Polyethylene generated the most severe growth and yield depression among polymer types, primarily driven by impaired photosynthetic pigment accumulation and disrupted photosystem II electron transport.

## Polymer Toxicity Gradients and Phytochemical Quality Alterations

Evaluation across distinct polymer chemistries indicated that microplastic toxicity followed the descending hierarchy of polyethylene > polystyrene > polyvinyl chloride. Bulb nutritional quality metrics displayed monotonic declines across increasing microplastic concentrations. When exposed to 1 000 mg · kg-1 microplastics, garlic bulb dry matter fell to 9.65% compared to 14.80% in control plants, while starch declined from 5.51% to 4.68%. Soluble protein and free amino acids also dropped significantly from 2.89% to 2.25% and 2 057.21 mg · kg-1 to 1 678.03 mg · kg-1, respectively, illustrating disrupted metabolic assimilation in storage sinks.

Foliar gas exchange and chlorophyll fluorescence metrics clarified the physiological mechanisms underlying yield suppression. Functional leaves under 10 mg · kg-1 microplastic additions exhibited transient enhancements in net photosynthetic rate (Pn = 19.39 μmol · m-2 · s-1), stomatal conductance (Gs = 534.67 mmol · m-2 · s-1), and transpiration rate (Tr = 5.66 mmol · m-2 · s-1). - Polyethylene induced the lowest net photosynthetic rate across polymers at 15.63 μmol · m-2 · s-1.

## Experimental Boundaries and Agricultural Transferability

This investigation utilized pot-based split-plot trials with virgin microplastic polymers of uniform 13 μm particle diameter, which may differ from aged, weathered fragments in field soils.

- Tested polymers were restricted to 13 μm spherical particles, omitting the morphology of irregular microplastic films and fibers prevalent in mulched fields.

- The pot trial evaluated a single garlic cultivar (P196) under controlled container substrate conditions, warranting validation across varied soil textures and field environments.

- Environmental weathering factors like ultraviolet photo-oxidation and co-occurring chemical agrochemical residues were excluded from the exposure matrix.

## 1. Executive Abstract

The accumulation of soil microplastics (MPs) derived from agricultural mulching films poses emerging ecotoxicological risks to agroecosystems, yet empirical evidence regarding their impact on garlic (Allium sativum L.) development remains limited. Here, garlic cultivar 'P196' was cultivated in a split-plot pot trial to evaluate the physiological and agronomic responses to three microplastic types (polyvinyl chloride [PVC], polyethylene [PE], and polystyrene [PS]; particle size 13 μm) across four concentration gradients (0, 10, 100, and 1 000 mg · kg-1). Relative to unamended controls, soil amended with 1 000 mg · kg-1 microplastics decreased pseudostem thickness, root fresh weight, and final yield by 26.94%, 44.65%, and 30.32%, respectively. Conversely, low-level exposure at 10 mg · kg-1 exerted a hormetic stimulatory effect, increasing plant height by 6.80%, leaf fresh weight by 12.66%, and pseudostem fresh weight by 19.00%. - Elevated microplastic levels at 1 000 mg · kg-1 suppressed photosynthetic efficiency, reducing Fv/Fm by 19.23% and Y(II) by 35.90%, while raising NPQ by 54.26%.

## Diurnal Microclimate and Spectral Composition Dynamics

In north-south oriented strip intercropping systems, solar geometry shifts throughout the day induce asymmetrical diurnal illumination regimes between the eastern and western border rows of the shorter companion crop. At 9:00, maize canopies cast heavy lateral shade across eastern soybean rows, depressing photosynthetically active radiation to 163.78-206.02 μmol·m-2·s-1. By 12:00, solar elevation reaches its peak, eliminating lateral interception and restoring irradiance across all rows to peak levels of 2,301.87-2,381.52 μmol·m-2·s-1, which matches monoculture values. By 15:00, western soybean rows experience reciprocal shading from adjacent maize rows, dropping irradiance to 211.39-448.68 μmol·m-2·s-1.

Spectral composition analysis reveals that shading selectively attenuates visible wavelengths while enriching relative proportions of ultraviolet (380-400 nm) and near-infrared/far-red light (700-780 nm). In shaded rows (eastern rows at 9:00 and western rows at 15:00), the red-to-far-red ratio (R:FR) declines sharply to 0.34-0.45 and 0.58-0.89, respectively, compared to 1.22-1.25 in full-sun monoculture. This modified spectral signature acts as an environmental trigger for photomorphogenic shade avoidance.

- Eastern border rows experience peak irradiance deficits at 9:00 with R:FR dropping as low as 0.34 in M4S4.

- Midday canopy irradiance across all intercropped rows equals monoculture levels (2,301.87-2,381.52 μmol·m-2·s-1).

- Western border rows suffer secondary lateral shading at 15:00 with R:FR declining to 0.58-0.89.

Strip intercropping of fresh maize with fresh soybean offers substantial land-use efficiency and economic returns in peri-urban agriculture. However, mutual shading from taller maize canopies suppresses soybean photosynthesis and alters morphological development. This field trial evaluated three intercropping configurations (row ratios 2:4, 4:4, and 4:6) alongside monocultures in Tianjin, quantifying diurnal canopy irradiance, spectral shifts, photosynthetic gas exchange, shade-avoidance morphology, and yield components. Results demonstrate that a 4:4 row ratio mitigates border-row shading deficits, optimizes photosynthetic capacity in interior rows, and delivers the highest land equivalent ratio (1.28) with minimized interspecific competitive stress.

## Photomorphogenic Plasticity and Gas Exchange Compensation

Soybean plants adapt to maize canopy shading by triggering shade-avoidance responses that alter both physical architecture and leaf-level gas exchange. In border rows, mechanical elongation stimulates an increase in the lowest pod clearance height, rising from 4.73 ± 0.11 cm under monoculture to 7.24 ± 0.82 cm in M4S4 border rows and 6.81 ± 0.46 cm in M4S6 border rows. Concurrently, main stem diameter diminishes significantly from 12.71 ± 0.85 mm in monoculture to 8.63-9.74 mm in intercropped border rows, elevating lodging susceptibility.

Despite morphological stem thinning and whole-plant leaf biomass reductions, interior soybean rows demonstrate compensatory photosynthetic resilience. The net photosynthetic rate (Pn), stomatal conductance (Gs), intercellular CO2 concentration (Ci), and transpiration rate (Tr) of top compound leaves in interior rows consistently surpass those of border rows across all intercropped patterns. Interior rows under M2S4, M4S4, and M4S6 exhibit significantly elevated Pn relative to border rows, sustained by localized light penetration and acclimation to moderate red/far-red signaling.

- Bottom pod height increases by up to 53.07% in M4S4 border rows compared to monoculture.

- Stem diameter decreases by 16.21% to 32.09% under intercropping due to etiolation responses.

- Functional leaves in interior rows sustain higher Pn, Gs, Ci, and Tr than border rows across all configurations.

## Yield Component Partitioning and System Productivity

Evaluating reproductive performance reveals that intercropping maintains robust pod fertility, with single-plant effective pod rates exceeding 95% across all configurations. Shading does not trigger pod abortion; rather, it shifts pod structure. Intercropping reduces the proportion of two-seed pods while concurrently increasing the rate of three-seed pods per plant. Monoculture controls record a two-seed pod rate of 45.94% and a three-seed pod rate of 49.81%, whereas M4S4 border rows exhibit a 10.20 percentage point drop in two-seed pods accompanied by elevated three-seed pod frequencies.

Total land-use efficiency underscores the superiority of balanced row-strip architecture. All three intercropping designs achieve land equivalent ratios exceeding unity (LER > 1), confirming net land-sparing benefits. The M4S4 treatment establishes the highest system productivity with an LER of 1.28, outpacing M2S4 (1.24) and M4S6 (1.21). Furthermore, relative competitiveness calculations indicate that while soybean remains the subordinate crop under maize dominance (Asm < 0), competitive suppression is lowest in M4S4 (Asm = -0.86) compared to M2S4 (Asm = -1.65), allowing fresh soybean pod yield to match monoculture levels.

- Single-plant effective pod rates exceed 95% in all experimental treatments without significant pod abortion.

- M4S4 achieves the highest land equivalent ratio (1.28) followed by M2S4 (1.24) and M4S6 (1.21).

- Soybean relative competitiveness is least suppressed under M4S4 (Asm = -0.86) versus M2S4 (Asm = -1.65).

## Geographic Scope and Agronomic Boundary Conditions

This investigation was conducted across a single spring-summer growing season (April to July 2025) on uniform yellow soil in Xiqing District, Tianjin. While the findings provide definitive row-ratio guidance for high-value peri-urban vegetable production, applicability across differing climates and cultivars requires consideration of operational constraints.

- Evaluation was restricted to one maize hybrid ('Meiyu 25') and one vegetable soybean cultivar ('Maodou No.3'); variations in canopy architecture, leaf angle, or shade tolerance among other cultivars may alter inter-row light penetration.

- The north-south row orientation specifically drives the observed morning-east and afternoon-west shade symmetry; alternative orientations such as east-west will modify diurnal shading geometry and canopy microclimates.

- Soil fertility and fertilization regimes were held uniform with base diammonium phosphate at 225 kg·hm-2 and dedicated drip lines; altered nutrient or irrigation management may influence vegetative canopy density and competitive hierarchies.

## Empirical and Pedotransfer Benchmarking Framework

In seasonally frozen soil regimes, phase change processes lower matric suction and surface free energy, preserving unfrozen water at temperatures below 0 deg C. Laboratory freeze-thaw simulations were conducted on Acheng black soil (silty clay loam), Lishu black soil (silty clay), and Siping aeolian sandy soil (silt loam) packed at specific bulk densities in stainless steel columns (height 5.7 cm, diameter 5.7 cm). Liquid water content and temperature dynamics were tracked at 3 min intervals using thermo-TDR sensors across controlled temperature drops from 5 deg C to -20 deg C at a cooling rate of 2.5 deg C/h.

Complementary field evaluations monitored daily mean liquid water content and thermal gradients across depths of 5 cm, 10 cm, 25 cm, and 40 cm in a bare experimental plot at Lishu from October 2016 through April 2017. Seven established mathematical formulations were evaluated: piecewise linear (Jame), piecewise quadratic (Lunardini), continuous exponential (McKenzie et al.), piecewise exponential (Kozlowski), modified Van Genuchten-type formulation (Fu et al.), surface area-dependent pedotransfer formulation (Anderson and Tice), and organic-textural pedotransfer formulation (Schaefer and Jafarov).

- Acheng black soil: 8% sand, 60% silt, 32% clay, specific surface area of 67 m2/g, and organic matter of 30.2 g/kg.

- Lishu black soil: 7% sand, 50% silt, 43% clay, specific surface area of 161 m2/g, and organic matter of 20.9 g/kg.

- Siping aeolian sandy soil: 39% sand, 60% silt, 1% clay, specific surface area of 31 m2/g, and organic matter of 7.5 g/kg.

- In situ Lishu profile: 16% sand, 47% silt, 37% clay, specific surface area of 145 m2/g, and organic matter of 17.7 g/kg.

## Comparative Accuracy and Residual Water Discrepancies

Phase transition kinetics exhibited distinct divergence across soil textures. In coarse Siping aeolian soil, most water crystallized above -0.5 deg C, dropping from initial contents of 0.30 m3/m3 and 0.38 m3/m3 to approximately 0.08 m3/m3, reaching stability near -1 deg C with a final residual water content of 0.04 m3/m3 at -20 deg C. Conversely, Lishu silty clay experienced gradual freezing from 0 deg C to -5 deg C, retaining 0.16 m3/m3 and 0.15 m3/m3 unfrozen water before stabilizing at 0.09 m3/m3 and 0.10 m3/m3 at -20 deg C. In field conditions, minimum temperatures reached approximately -12 deg C at 5 cm and -7 deg C at 40 cm, with all depths retaining liquid water contents above 0.20 m3/m3.

Model evaluations confirmed that the empirical models developed by Kozlowski and Fu et al. provided the closest alignment with experimental measurements across all four soils, maintaining mean MBE values of -0.002 m3/m3 and 0.003 m3/m3 and AIC values of -488 and -469. Conversely, the Anderson and Tice model overestimated early freezing moisture and produced an average MBE of 0.053 m3/m3, whereas the Schaefer and Jafarov formulation systematically underestimated liquid content with an average MBE of -0.072 m3/m3 and positive AIC values.

## Formulation and Validation of the Novel Pedotransfer Function

To eliminate the requirement for labor-intensive laboratory calibration of empirical fitting parameters, a new pedotransfer function was formulated by linking residual water content to specific surface area and bulk density, while expressing transition parameters as functions of sand fraction and clay fraction. Calibrated via least squares regression on the experimental dataset, the model coefficients were resolved as a1 = 0.073, b1 = -0.266, a2 = -10.6, b2 = -16.7, a3 = 0.55, b3 = 1.46, a4 = -1585, and b4 = 208.

The resulting formulation yielded individual RMSE values of 0.030 m3/m3 for Acheng black soil, 0.022 m3/m3 for Lishu black soil, 0.023 m3/m3 for Siping aeolian soil, and 0.023 m3/m3 for the in situ Lishu profile. With an overall average RMSE of 0.025 m3/m3, an average MBE of -0.001 m3/m3, and an average AIC of -179, the proposed model significantly outperformed preexisting pedotransfer models, providing an analytical approach for cold-region hydrological and erosion modeling.

Accurate characterization of the soil freezing characteristic curve (SFCC) governs hydro-thermal-solute transport modeling in seasonally frozen landscapes. This study bench-tested five empirical fitting models and two conventional pedotransfer functions across three Northeast China soil types under varied initial moisture contents and along an in situ black soil profile from 5 cm to 40 cm depths. Empirical models accounting for initial and residual water content achieved root mean square error (RMSE) values near 0.018 m3/m3, whereas existing basic pedotransfer functions exhibited significant discrepancies exceeding 0.08 m3/m3. A newly formulated pedotransfer function integrating specific surface area, bulk density, and sand and clay fractions improved the simulated SFCC accuracy to an average RMSE of 0.025 m3/m3 and an average AIC of -179.

## Boundary Conditions and Parameter Generalization Constraints

The empirical and pedotransfer models were evaluated under specific agricultural and pedological conditions characteristic of Northeast China black soil regions.

- The newly established pedotransfer function was calibrated using four regional soil datasets and requires further verification across varying soil salinity, organic matter fractions, and external mechanical overburden stresses.

- Laboratory testing utilized controlled cooling rates of 2.5 deg C/h down to -20 deg C; field freezing processes occur under non-uniform meteorological gradients that may modify boundary water redistribution.

- The empirical models exhibiting the lowest RMSE (0.018 m3/m3) require explicit experimental SFCC measurement for parameter optimization, limiting direct uncalibrated regional implementation.

# Evaluation of Different Freezing Characteristic Curve Models with Black Soils of Northeast China

---

**DOI:** `10.13758/j.cnki.tr.202412040485` | **Journal:** Soils (土壤) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** WANG Li, TIAN Zhengchao, YI Ceng, REN Tusheng  
**Affiliation:** College of Land Science and Technology, China Agricultural University, Beijing 100093, China

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

The black soil region in Northeast China experiences intense seasonal freeze-thaw cycles that profoundly influence soil structure, hydraulic conductivity, and freeze-thaw erosion. The soil freezing characteristic curve (SFCC) defines the thermodynamic equilibrium between subzero soil temperature and liquid unfrozen water content. In this study, SFCCs of three representative Northeast soils were determined in the laboratory across multiple initial water contents using a thermo-TDR sensor apparatus, and field-scale seasonal dynamic SFCCs were tracked in situ across a bare-soil profile in Lishu. Seven existing SFCC formulations were benchmarked against measured datasets, identifying structural limitations in classical empirical and pedotransfer models. Empirical fitting formulations incorporating initial and residual unfrozen water contents demonstrated superior performance, yielding an average root mean square error (RMSE) around 0.018 m3/m3 with negative Akaike information criterion (AIC) values. Conversely, existing pedotransfer functions that omit initial moisture or bulk density exhibited substantial prediction errors, with RMSE exceeding 0.08 m3/m3. To overcome parameter calibration dependency, a novel pedotransfer function was established by parameterizing residual water content and freezing curve coefficients via soil specific surface area, bulk density, and sand and clay fractions. The proposed formulation reliably predicted SFCC trajectories across all four evaluated soils, yielding an average RMSE of 0.025 m3/m3 and an average AIC of -179, thereby offering robust analytical parameterization for regional water and thermal flux simulations.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Fine-textured Lishu black clay maintained substantial unfrozen liquid water contents exceeding 0.20 m3/m3 under deep field freezing conditions.
- Nonlinear empirical fitting models by Kozlowski and Fu achieved the lowest average RMSE of 0.018 m3/m3 with negative AIC values across tested soils.
- Conventional pedotransfer models by Anderson-Tice and Schaefer-Jafarov produced high prediction errors, averaging RMSE values of 0.166 m3/m3 and 0.082 m3/m3, respectively.
- The newly established pedotransfer function incorporating specific surface area, bulk density, sand, and clay fractions reduced the average RMSE to 0.025 m3/m3 with an average AIC of -179.

abstract_en: This study evaluated the effects of dietary mixed Chinese herbs on production performance, egg quality, and oviduct health in laying hens. A single-factor completely randomized design was conducted using 480 45-week-old Lohmann Pink laying hens with an initial laying rate of (95.10 ± 3.61)%, divided into six treatment groups (eight replicates of ten hens each). Hens were fed either a corn-soybean meal basal diet (control, CON) or the basal diet supplemented with 1000 mg/kg of herbal mixtures with varying compatibility ratios of dandelion, mugwort leaf, Hedyotis diffusa, Herba leonuri, and honeysuckle: 1:1:1:1:1 (MCH1), 6:1:1:1:1 (MCH2), 1:6:1:1:1 (MCH3), 1:1:6:1:1 (MCH4), and 1:1:1:6:1 (MCH5). Following a 1-week adaptation, the formal trial lasted 8 weeks. Dietary herbal mixtures maintained overall laying performance while significantly reducing average daily feed intake in MCH5 from weeks 5 to 8 (P < 0.05). analysis_markdown_en:
In post-antibiotic poultry production, salpingitis impairs layer productivity and reproductive tract integrity during mid-to-late laying phases. This study evaluated dietary supplementation with 1000 mg/kg of five distinct mixed Chinese herb formulations comprising dandelion, mugwort leaf, Hedyotis diffusa, Herba leonuri, and honeysuckle in 480 Lohmann Pink laying hens over an 8-week trial. The mugwort leaf-dominated formulation (MCH3, 1:6:1:1:1) demonstrated the highest therapeutic efficacy, markedly attenuating systemic and oviductal pro-inflammatory cytokines while elevating antioxidant enzyme defenses. These outcomes establish specific botanical compatibility strategies to sustain oviduct health without compromising baseline egg production.

## Experimental Architecture and Herbal Compatibility Ratios

In modern poultry housing, oviduct inflammation represents a persistent pathology leading to declining eggshell structure and premature cessation of laying. Following national bans on non-therapeutic feed antibiotics, botanical mixtures rich in polyphenols, flavonoids, organic acids, and alkaloids offer viable protective interventions. The experimental formulation tested five traditional medicinal plants: dandelion (Taraxacum mongolicum), mugwort leaf (Artemisia argyi), Hedyotis diffusa, Herba leonuri (Leonurus japonicus), and honeysuckle (Lonicera japonica).

A total of 480 45-week-old Lohmann Pink laying hens with an initial laying rate of (95.10 ± 3.61)% were allocated into six treatment cohorts: an unsupplemented corn-soybean meal control group (CON) and five herbal intervention groups (MCH1 through MCH5) each receiving 1000 mg/kg total mixture. The herbal compatibility ratios for dandelion, mugwort leaf, Hedyotis diffusa, Herba leonuri, and honeysuckle were established as 1:1:1:1:1 (MCH1), 6:1:1:1:1 (MCH2), 1:6:1:1:1 (MCH3), 1:1:6:1:1 (MCH4), and 1:1:1:6:1 (MCH5). Each cohort possessed eight replicates containing ten caged layers subjected to controlled photoperiods (16 hours light : 8 hours dark) and temperature regulation (20 to 22 degrees Celsius) across 8 test weeks following 1 adaptation week.

- Metabolomic assay verified flavonoid concentrations of 38.42 mg/g in dandelion, 62.15 mg/g in mugwort leaf, 35.77 mg/g in Hedyotis diffusa, 34.71 mg/g in Herba leonuri, and 21.38 mg/g in honeysuckle.

- Organic acid concentrations reached 161.12 mg/g in dandelion, 60.60 mg/g in mugwort leaf, 57.64 mg/g in Hedyotis diffusa, 36.46 mg/g in Herba leonuri, and 86.77 mg/g in honeysuckle.

## Production Parameters and Eggshell Biomechanical Dynamics

Supplementation at 1000 mg/kg did not impair long-term laying performance across the full 8-week duration. The average laying rate across weeks 1 to 8 was 93.79% in CON, 94.06% in MCH1, 93.85% in MCH2, 94.73% in MCH3, 92.90% in MCH4, and 94.93% in MCH5. Feed-to-egg ratios over weeks 1 to 8 ranged from 1.92 to 2.01 without statistical disparity.

During weeks 5 to 8, average daily feed intake was significantly reduced in MCH5 to 112.86 g compared to 116.92 g in CON (P < 0.05), whereas earlier intake was unaffected. Physical eggshell quality reflected notable benefits at week 4: eggshell strength reached 5.31 kg/cm3 in MCH1 and 5.01 kg/cm3 in MCH5 compared to 4.59 kg/cm3 in CON (P < 0.05). Albumen height at week 4 was elevated to 7.45 mm in MCH1 compared to 6.79 mm in CON, indicating enhanced magnum secretory output.

- Eggshell thickness remained uniform across groups at week 4 (0.34 mm to 0.36 mm) and week 8 (0.35 mm to 0.37 mm).

- Dark spot scores evaluated after 5 days of storage remained unchanged at week 4 (96.96 to 98.38) and week 8 (67.23 to 73.88).
