## Oviductal Cytokine Modulation and Regional Antioxidant Defenses

The anatomical integrity of avian egg formation relies on sequential oviductal segments: the protein-secreting magnum, membrane-forming isthmus, and calcifying uterus (eggshell gland). Chronic inflammatory signaling in these segments causes structural degeneration. Dietary herbal mixtures consistently curbed inflammatory mediators. In the magnum, TNF-alpha decreased significantly across all herbal groups compared to CON (565.26 ng/L), reaching 522.21 ng/L in MCH1, 539.66 ng/L in MCH2, 502.48 ng/L in MCH3, 509.27 ng/L in MCH4, and 524.81 ng/L in MCH5 (P < 0.05). In the isthmus, IL-1beta dropped from 61.19 ng/L in CON to 56.01 ng/L in MCH2 and 55.45 ng/L in MCH3.

Enzymatic antioxidant profiles demonstrated substantial tissue protection against lipid peroxidation. In the isthmus, SOD activity surged from 17.21 U/mg prot in CON to 25.27 U/mg prot in MCH1, 34.56 U/mg prot in MCH2, 56.99 U/mg prot in MCH3, 25.48 U/mg prot in MCH4, and 21.45 U/mg prot in MCH5 (P < 0.05). Similarly, isthmus CAT activity expanded from 9.31 U/mg prot in CON to 59.87 U/mg prot in MCH3. In the uterus, MDA accumulation dropped from 2.94 nmol/mg prot in CON to 1.71 nmol/mg prot in MCH3 (P < 0.05), proving that mugwort leaf dominance optimizes regional mucosal defense.

- Hepatic SOD activity rose from 649.24 U/mg prot in CON to 730.09 U/mg prot in MCH4, while liver MDA decreased from 1.18 nmol/mg prot to 0.71 nmol/mg prot in MCH5.

- Uterine IL-6 concentrations decreased from 27.33 ng/L in CON to 24.93 ng/L in MCH3 and 24.20 ng/L in MCH4 (P < 0.05).

## Formulation Disparities and Physiological Boundary Conditions

While multi-herb supplementation conferred distinct anti-inflammatory and antioxidant benefits, biological outcomes varied substantially depending on the dominant herb. Formulation MCH5 reduced feed intake without anti-inflammatory advantages, while histological tracking was omitted.

- In formulation MCH5 (dominated by Herba leonuri at 1:1:1:6:1), average daily feed intake dropped significantly to 112.86 g during weeks 5 to 8, while serum TNF-alpha rose to 835.86 ng/L and IL-6 to 36.10 ng/L, highlighting potential toxicity or palatability issues with disproportionate Herba leonuri.

- The experiment evaluated a single inclusion dose of 1000 mg/kg in 45-week-old Lohmann Pink hens over an 8-week period, leaving dose-response dynamics and late-phase layers older than 65 weeks unexamined.

**Affiliation:** Animal Nutrition Institute, Sichuan Agricultural University, Chengdu 611130, China

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

This study evaluated the effects of dietary mixed Chinese herbs on production performance, egg quality, and oviduct health in laying hens. A single-factor completely randomized design was conducted using 480 45-week-old Lohmann Pink laying hens with an initial laying rate of (95.10 ± 3.61)%, divided into six treatment groups (eight replicates of ten hens each). Hens were fed either a corn-soybean meal basal diet (control, CON) or the basal diet supplemented with 1000 mg/kg of herbal mixtures with varying compatibility ratios of dandelion, mugwort leaf, Hedyotis diffusa, Herba leonuri, and honeysuckle: 1:1:1:1:1 (MCH1), 6:1:1:1:1 (MCH2), 1:6:1:1:1 (MCH3), 1:1:6:1:1 (MCH4), and 1:1:1:6:1 (MCH5). Following a 1-week adaptation, the formal trial lasted 8 weeks. Dietary herbal mixtures maintained overall laying performance while significantly reducing average daily feed intake in MCH5 from weeks 5 to 8 (P < 0.05). In week 4, MCH1 and MCH5 significantly improved eggshell strength (P < 0.05). Across the oviduct, MCH3 exerted the strongest anti-inflammatory and antioxidant actions, significantly lowering magnum IL-1beta and IL-6, isthmus IL-1beta, and uterus TNF-alpha, while driving isthmus SOD and CAT activities to peak levels (P < 0.05) and minimizing uterus MDA content. An appropriate 1000 mg/kg herbal mixture, especially MCH3 dominated by mugwort leaf, effectively protects oviduct mucosal health and mitigates reproductive inflammation.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Laying performance remained stable across groups from weeks 1 to 8, with laying rates ranging between 92.90% and 94.93% and average daily feed intake from 111.62 g to 114.22 g.

- Oviductal antioxidant defenses peaked under MCH3, which elevated isthmus SOD to 56.99 U/mg prot and CAT to 59.87 U/mg prot while reducing uterus MDA to 1.71 nmol/mg prot.

## Biomass Allocation and Underground Organ Partitioning

In strongly acidic red soils derived from Quaternary red clay (pH 4.99), peanut vegetative and reproductive biomass responds divergently to medium and micronutrient supply. Under conventional baseline fertilization (135 kg·hm-2 N, 81 kg·hm-2 P2O5, and 135 kg·hm-2 K2O), peanut plants accumulated only 142.1 kg·hm-2 of root biomass and 2985.3 kg·hm-2 of total underground dry matter. Incorporating boron individually or combined with calcium stimulated root proliferation, reaching 328.8 kg·hm-2 in the B treatment and 339.0 kg·hm-2 in Ca+B, representing increases of 131.39% and 138.56% respectively over CK.

Factor analysis identified two distinct regulatory components accounting for total phenotypic variation. The first principal factor (F1) loaded strongly on subterranean organs, showing positive loadings of 0.884 on roots, 0.630 on shells, 0.880 on kernels, and 0.954 on total underground biomass. The B and Ca+B treatments scored highest along the F1 axis, driving kernel biomass to 2941.1 kg·hm-2 and underground biomass to 4450.1 kg·hm-2. In contrast, molybdenum-containing treatments clustered along the second principal factor (F2), which loaded primarily on leaves (0.894) and stems (0.641). Maximum aboveground vegetative mass occurred under Ca+Mo (2579.9 kg·hm-2), indicating that molybdenum shifts structural photosynthate allocation into vegetative shoots rather than reproductive sink tissues.

- Ca+B achieved the highest total plant biomass at 6712.5 kg·hm-2, outperforming the CK control level of 4676.8 kg·hm-2 by 43.53%.

- Kernel dry matter under Ca+B expanded to 2941.1 kg·hm-2 versus 1939.4 kg·hm-2 in CK, an increase of 51.65%.

- Molybdenum supplementation increased leaf biomass up to 808.5 kg·hm-2 in Ca+B+Mo, a 52.66% rise above CK.

In subtropical red soil uplands characterized by strong acidity and secondary micronutrient deficiencies, conventional nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium regimens fail to meet high-yield peanut requirements. This two-year field study evaluates single and combined applications of calcium, boron, and molybdenum across eight treatments. Combined calcium and boron supplementation produced the highest agronomic and financial performance, increasing pod yield by 44.59% and net profit by 50.83% over baseline fertilization. Conversely, molybdenum stimulated vegetative shoot growth while boron drove subterranean pod development, triggering a pronounced physiological antagonism and yield suppression when combined.

## Pod Yield Response and Micronutrient Antagonism

Two-year pod harvesting confirmed that all medium and micronutrient amendments increased pod yield over the unsupplemented control (2843.2 kg·hm-2), with yield gains spanning 14.70% to 44.59%. The Ca+B treatment established the maximum pod yield at 4111.1 kg·hm-2, followed by the sole B treatment at 3888.9 kg·hm-2. Calcium amendment ameliorates soil acidity, mitigates aluminum and manganese toxicity, and promotes pod wall calcification, while boron stimulates pollen tube elongation, fertilization success, and carbohydrate translocation into pods.

Crucially, multi-factor analysis of variance demonstrated that combining boron and molybdenum creates a significant antagonistic interaction (F = 143.37, P < 0.01), as did the Ca+Mo interaction (F = 15.79, P < 0.01). While solo application of B delivered a 36.8% yield gain and Mo provided 22.6%, their combination in B+Mo yielded only 3414.8 kg·hm-2 (20.1% gain). Similarly, the ternary mixture Ca+B+Mo dropped yield to 3323.4 kg·hm-2 (16.9% gain), with harvest index declining from 62.0% in CK down to 59.5%. This competitive inhibition stems from shared transport channels (such as NIP5;1 boric acid channels) and competitive uptake between phosphate and molybdate anions under elevated soil pH.

- Kernel shelling percentage reached 71.5% in Ca+B and 71.7% in B, compared with 68.2% in CK.

- Harvest index was reduced in all molybdenum treatments, dropping to 56.4% in Ca+Mo and 58.3% in Mo.

- The three-way Ca+B+Mo interaction proved non-significant (F = 0.22, P = 0.64), failing to enhance yield beyond binary treatments.

## Production Economics and Optimal Nutrient Regimens

Evaluating total input costs against gross crop revenue verified the economic feasibility of targeted micronutrient management. Basal operational costs for CK totaled 3561.0 Yuan·hm-2, generating 17912.2 Yuan·hm-2 in revenue and 14351.2 Yuan·hm-2 in net profit. Supplementing with lime (1200 kg·hm-2 at 360 Yuan·hm-2) and borax (10 kg·hm-2 at 333.3 Yuan·hm-2) raised total expenditure to 4254.3 Yuan·hm-2 under Ca+B, but expanded total revenue to 25900.0 Yuan·hm-2.

Net profit under Ca+B reached 21645.7 Yuan·hm-2, representing a 50.83% net gain over conventional fertilization. The single B treatment generated 20605.7 Yuan·hm-2 in profit, achieving the highest benefit-to-cost ratio (profit/input) of 5.29 due to low material costs. Ternary fertilization (Ca+B+Mo) lowered profit to 16676.8 Yuan·hm-2 and dropped the profit/input ratio to 3.91, below the CK control baseline of 4.03. Therefore, agronomic efficiency and gross margin dictate omitting molybdenum in red soils when calcium and boron are co-applied.

- Ca+B delivered the absolute highest net profit at 21645.7 Yuan·hm-2, outperforming CK by 7294.5 Yuan·hm-2.

- The benefit-to-cost ratio reached 5.29 in B, 5.15 in Mo, and 5.09 in Ca+B, compared with 4.03 in CK.

- Ternary Ca+B+Mo fertilization degraded profitability, resulting in the lowest profit/input ratio of 3.91 across all treatments.

## Soil Baseline Boundaries and Agronomic Transferability Constraints

This study was conducted on a specific Quaternary red clay site in Jiangxi Province across two consecutive cropping cycles, with initial exchangeable calcium of 703.17 mg·kg-1, available boron of 0.62 mg·kg-1, and available molybdenum of 0.18 mg·kg-1 at pH 4.99.

- Initial exchangeable soil calcium (703.17 mg·kg-1) exceeded the severe deficiency threshold (250 mg·kg-1) though remaining below the 800 mg·kg-1 optimum, which explains the relatively muted yield gain of solo calcium (14.70%).

- Results are directly calibrated for the Spanish-type cultivar Yueyou 256 under subtropical conditions (mean temperature 26.3 degrees C, total seasonal rainfall 2092.8 mm) and require local calibration in coarse sandy soils or higher-pH regions.

- Fixed material pricing (lime at 360 Yuan·hm-2, borax at 333.3 Yuan·hm-2, peanut purchase price at 6.3 Yuan·kg-1) reflects local market conditions and may shift benefit-cost ratios under price volatility.

abstract_en: Given the challenges of water scarcity and abundant light resources in the arid northwest region, this study investigates the relationship between farmland soil moisture and crop photosynthesis to improve comprehensive resource utilization and establish a complementary soil moisture-light mechanism. From 2019 to 2021, multi-year field experiments were conducted across three experimental sites in the Yellow River irrigation area of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. Using full irrigation as the control (CK), drip irrigation treatments were established across varying soil moisture lower limits: M1 (90% FC), M2 (80% FC), M3 (70% FC), M4 (60% FC), and M5 (50% FC). Drip irrigation regimes were benchmarked against full irrigation by constraining soil moisture lower thresholds between 50% and 90% of field capacity. ## Phenological Dynamics of Leaf Photosynthesis and Gas Exchange

In arid and semi-arid environments, soil moisture availability governs carbon assimilation by directly regulating stomatal conductance and transpirational cooling. Diurnal monitoring revealed a distinct bimodal curve in leaf net photosynthetic rate across all irrigation regimes, with primary and secondary peaks appearing at approximately 11:00 and 15:00, separated by midday photosynthetic depression at 13:00. Net photosynthetic rate tracked soil moisture availability across all growing seasons, following the consistent hierarchy CK>M1>M2>M3>M4>M5. Photosynthetic capacity reached its seasonal maximum at the booting stage before declining to its lowest point during the milk-ripe phase.

Under severe deficit conditions (M5), the net photosynthetic rate at the booting stage dropped by 26.6%, 26.3%, and 21.0% in 2019, 2020, and 2021, respectively, while milk-ripe reductions reached 32.2%, 46.9%, and 25.1%. Booting-stage transpiration under M5 fell by 14.4%, 12.3%, and 16.8% across the three consecutive seasons, driven by organic osmolyte accumulation and adaptive stomatal closure designed to mitigate physiological dehydration.

- Photosynthetic midday depression occurred regularly at 13:00 across all drip irrigation gradients.

- Transpiration rate reductions under severe stress reached 40.7% at the seedling stage in 2021.

- Stomatal constriction limited internal carbon dioxide diffusion, suppressing photosynthetic enzyme activity.

## Agronomic Yield Components and Biomass Allocation Disparity

Deficit irrigation exerted pronounced inhibitory effects on dryland rice vegetative development and reproductive sink capacity. Plant height accumulation diverged progressively after early vegetative development, establishing highly significant differences across treatments (P<0.001) by late season. Relative to full irrigation, final plant height reductions across the stress gradient spanned 4.8%-24.3% in 2019, 3.7%-19.6% in 2020, and 2.2%-20.0% in 2021. Straw height and straw dry mass exhibited proportional declines, decreasing by 0.3%-12.6% and 0.8%-11.6% across the multi-year trials due to suppressed cell elongation and slower dry matter translocation.

Grain productivity tracked the severity of soil moisture limitation. Final yield under full irrigation surpassed deficit treatments by 10.6%-55.8% in 2019, 2.3%-31.0% in 2020, and 9.5%-71.5% in 2021. Seed setting and grain filling were also sensitive to water deficits, with filled grain rate contracting by 0.5%-7.9% under stress. In contrast, 1000-grain weight demonstrated greater stability, recording minimal decreases between 0.3% and 1.5% under mild to moderate deficits, before dropping by 9.2% under extreme drought in 2021.

- Filled grain rate decreased by up to 7.9% under the most severe moisture deficit treatment (M5).

- Straw dry weight reductions reached 4.4% in 2019, 5.4% in 2020, and 11.6% in 2021 under M5.

- Final grain yield suppression intensified under high evaporative demand, reaching a 71.5% deficit in 2021.

## Multi-Criteria Decision Evaluation and Deficit Irrigation Optimization

Total crop evapotranspiration and water consumption decreased monotonically with expanding deficit severity. Across the experimental cycle, seasonal water consumption under deficit treatments dropped by 7.8%-63.5% relative to the fully irrigated control. Consumption was concentrated predominantly within two critical phenological windows: the seedling phase and the jointing-booting stage, whereas water extraction dropped to minimal levels at the milk-ripe stage. Polynomial functions fitted to field capacity thresholds confirmed that excessive moisture supplies induced high vegetative transpiration without commensurate harvest gains.

To identify the optimal operational boundary, comprehensive multi-criteria decision analysis was executed using the TOPSIS model integrated with the information value method and entropy weight method. Across all three years, the M1 treatment (soil moisture lower limit maintained at 90% of field capacity) achieved top-tier relative closeness scores (0.645-0.722 under entropy weighting; 0.654-0.696 under the information value method), outranking full irrigation in 2019 and 2021 under entropy weighting. - Single-leaf water use efficiency under M1 declined modestly by 2.1%-6.8% across seasons.

- TOPSIS closeness scores established the 90%-100% field capacity range as the optimal irrigation threshold.

## Regional Boundary Conditions and Precision Control Constraints

This study establishes soil moisture thresholds for dryland rice cultivated under drip irrigation in the arid Yellow River basin, subject to specific environmental and infrastructural considerations.

- Field trials were conducted across three typical sites within the Yellow River irrigation area of Ningxia, where light radiation is abundant but ambient atmospheric humidity is low, potentially altering transpiration ratios compared to humid rice-producing zones.

- Maintaining soil moisture limits precisely at 90%-100% of field capacity requires high-frequency soil moisture sensing and automated drip delivery systems, which may present operational hurdles in broad-acre smallholder farming contexts.

## Synergistic Electro-Hydration Protocols and Response Surface Modeling

Carrot seeds possess a cutinized pericarp rich in volatile oils, resulting in poor water permeability, protracted germination cycles, and erratic emergence that impede mechanized precision sowing. While standalone hydropriming minimizes chemical residues, extended soaking durations increase pathogen susceptibility. Conversely, high-voltage electrostatic fields rapidly stimulate cellular metabolism but suffer from transient post-treatment retention. HEHP combines both interventions by exposing seeds imbibed in ultrapure water at 20 °C for 6 h to an electrostatic field generated by a BM-201 apparatus, followed by 48 h humidity maintenance at 98% relative humidity and 12 h controlled redrying at 25 °C and 60% relative humidity.

To model multi-parameter interactions, a central composite design tested electric field intensities from 0.1 to 3.9 kV · cm-1 and durations from 30 to 150 s. Nine physiological indicators—including daily germination rates from day 1 to day 5, seedling fresh weight, germination index, vigor index, and mean germination time—were compressed via principal component analysis into a single composite PCA score explaining 91.81% of total variance. The resulting response surface quadratic model was highly significant (P = 0.003 3), identifying an optimal coordinate of 2.05 kV · cm-1 and 81.4 s with a peak predicted PCA score of 2.09.

- Imbibition of carrot seeds at 20 °C for 6 h heightened embryonic sensitivity to electrostatic polarization.

- Response surface quadratic modeling verified that overexposure beyond 2.05 kV · cm-1 or 90 s introduced physiological threshold inhibition.

Mechanical sowing of carrot (Daucus carota L.) is severely impeded by poor seed coat permeability, slow germination, and non-uniform emergence. To overcome these constraints, this study integrates hydropriming (HYD) with high-voltage electrostatic field (EF) stimulation into a unified hydro-electro hybrid priming (HEHP) protocol. Using a central composite design and principal component analysis (PCA), response surface models established optimal electrostatic parameters of 2.05 kV · cm-1 and 81.4 s. The optimized HEHP treatment achieved a 90.0% germination rate and a vigor index of 4.63, maintaining substantial biological enhancement over an 8-month post-treatment storage period.

## Longitudinal Storage Timeliness and Vigor Decay Dynamics

A critical bottleneck restricting the commercial deployment of primed seeds is shelf-life viability following dehydration. A 12-month longitudinal storage trial at 5 °C and 35% relative humidity monitored physiological degradation at 60 d intervals. Seeds treated with optimized HEHP parameters exhibited a gradual decline in immediate germination capacity, with 1 d germination dropping by 13.5 percentage points between month 0 (20.5 ± 3.0%) and month 12 (7.0 ± 2.6%). However, the cumulative 5 d germination rate showed strong resilience, decreasing by only 7.5 percentage points from 90.0 ± 1.6% to 82.5 ± 1.9%.

Non-linear regression modeling characterized vigor index trajectories over storage time (x in months) as y = -0.001x 3 + 0.001x 2 - 0.029x + 4.601 for HEHP (R 2 = 0.970) and y = -0.001x 3 + 0.008x 2 - 0.050x + 3.379 for HYD (R 2 = 0.979). Both primed cohorts preserved high vigor stability through 6 months of storage, experienced marked degradation at 8 to 10 months, yet remained significantly superior to untreated controls across the full 12-month evaluation.

- HEHP biological efficacy persists stably for approximately 8 months, matching commercial planting operational windows.

- Control seed vigor remained static and low across 12 months, whereas HEHP preserved enhanced final germination even after 1 year.

## Cultivar Specificity and Physiological Operational Constraints

The optimized hydro-electro hybrid priming parameters demonstrate strong biological efficacy for 'Nais' carrot seeds, but deployment across diverse agricultural settings must account for physiological thresholds and structural variations in seed coats.

- Electric field stimulation exhibits strict threshold kinetics: exceeding 2.05 kV · cm-1 or extending duration beyond 90 s reduces seed vigor, as evidenced by HEHP8 (150 s) dropping to a vigor index of 5.54 ± 0.12.

- The biological enhancement degrades after 8 months of storage under 5 °C and 35% relative humidity, requiring operational sowing within this window.

- Parameter validation was conducted exclusively on the 'Nais' cultivar; variations in pericarp cutinization, pericarp volatile oil profiles, and baseline germination rates across other carrot cultivars necessitate re-calibration.

## Soil Hydrothermal and Organic Dynamics Under Mulched Deficit Irrigation

In arid agroecosystems like Xinjiang, where agricultural water consumption represents 90.40% of total allocation, optimizing soil moisture retention and organic matter storage is essential. The field evaluation revealed that reducing irrigation volumes from 4 500 m3/hm2 (W1) to 3 825 m3/hm2 (W2) and 3 150 m3/hm2 (W3) induced significant declines in soil water storage (SWS) and soil organic matter (SOM). Across the 0-80 cm soil profile, SWS variations exhibited distinct phenological phase dependencies. During the seedling and budding stages, fulvic acid application (45 kg/hm2, F2) exerted a significant positive main effect (P<0.05), raising SWS by 4.68% to 6.06% compared to the F1 control.

However, this trend reversed during peak vegetative and reproductive growth. During the flowering and boll-forming stage as well as the boll-opening stage, fulvic acid addition reduced SWS by 6.51% to 10.70% (P<0.01), driven by enhanced plant transpiration and accelerated vegetative canopy expansion. For example, under identical management, W1O1F2 decreased flowering-stage SWS by 18.94% relative to W1O1F1, while W3O2F2 dropped by 22.01% compared to W3O2F1. Concurrently, SOM in the 0-40 cm root zone exhibited strong three-factor interactions (P<0.001). Under moderate deficit (W2), fulvic acid application combined with chemical nitrogen (W2O1F2) elevated end-of-season 0-20 cm SOM to 8.68±0.11%, an increase of 146.20% over W2O1F1 (3.52±0.22%) and 43.04% over the full-irrigation baseline W1O1F1 (6.07±0.11%). Under severe deficit (W3), however, fulvic acid failed to prevent organic carbon depletion in low-organic-substitution regimes.

- Main-effect irrigation curtailment from W1 to W2 and W3 reduced flowering-stage soil water storage by 9.29% and 8.76%, respectively.

- Fulvic acid improved 0-20 cm topsoil organic matter across W1 (+30.30%) and W2 (+80.40%), but registered a -17.68% decrease under severe deficit W3.

- At the 20-40 cm subsoil depth, organic substitution without fulvic acid under W1 lowered SOM by 35.27% (O2) and 30.48% (O3) relative to pure chemical fertilization.

This study evaluates the agronomic and edaphic impacts of coupling deficit irrigation, organic fertilizer substitution, and fulvic acid supplementation in an arid oasis cotton agroecosystem. Conducting an 18-treatment factorial field experiment under mulched drip irrigation in Xinjiang during 2024, researchers tracked soil water storage across four growth stages, 0-40 cm soil organic matter profiles, biomass partitioning, lint quality, and crop yield. The findings identify non-linear three-factor threshold dynamics across deficit regimes: while fulvic acid enhanced seedling water retention and topsoil organic matter under moderate deficit, extreme water restriction combined with excessive organic substitution led to performance trade-offs.

## Phenological Dry Matter Partitioning and Agronomic Yield Responses

Dry matter accumulation during the critical flowering and boll-forming stage directly dictated final economic yield. Across the 18 treatment combinations, the interaction between deficit irrigation, organic substitution, and fulvic acid significantly affected stem dry matter (P<0.001), leaf dry matter (P<0.05), boll dry matter (P<0.05), and total population dry matter (P<0.01). The W2O2F2 treatment recorded the highest individual aboveground biomass, producing 4 704.60±199.53 kg/hm2 stem dry matter, 2 747.40±36.50 kg/hm2 leaf dry matter, and 3 481.97±142.98 kg/hm2 boll dry matter, totaling 10 933.97±300.56 kg/hm2 population dry matter.

The interaction of organic substitution with fulvic acid governed reproductive sink capacity. In the O1 and O2 regimes, fulvic acid increased boll dry matter by 22.51% and 23.69%, whereas in the high substitution regime (O3), it suppressed boll dry matter by -25.57%. Under severe deficit (W3), however, heavy organic replacement without fulvic acid (W3O3F1) exhibited remarkable drought buffering, yielding 4 098.77±358.53 kg/hm2 in boll biomass and a total population dry matter of 9 930.47±737.73 kg/hm2. Final harvest data confirmed that seed cotton yield was highest in W1O2F2 (6 833.33±256.54 kg/hm2), while severe deficit combined with unbuffered organic substitution (W2O3F1 and W3O3F2) yielded the lowest outputs at 3 816.67±299.34 kg/hm2 and 3 886.67±444.56 kg/hm2, respectively.

- Under 15% organic substitution (O2), fulvic acid addition increased plant height by 4.30% under W1 and 6.49% under W2 relative to F1.

- Stem diameter peaked under W3O2F1 followed by W1O2F2, exhibiting increases of 15.74% and 12.24% over the W1O1F1 baseline.

- F2 overall increased cotton yield by 6.90%, irrigation water use efficiency by 8.43%, and partial nitrogen productivity by 7.11% (P<0.05).

## Multi-Criteria Decision Modeling for Irrigation and Nutrient Scheduling

Balancing agronomic productivity against water scarcity requires rigorous multi-attribute optimization. Using the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS), four key agronomic criteria were synthesized with equal weighting: seed cotton yield, the fiber quality index (FQI), irrigation water use efficiency (IWUE), and partial factor productivity of nitrogen (PFP). Proximity to the positive ideal solution (C value) ranged from 0.106 to 0.726 across the experimental treatments. Treatment W1O2F2 secured the top ranking (C = 0.726, D+ = 0.122, D- = 0.323), offering the optimal balance when irrigation water is unconstrained.

For arid and semi-arid deployment where water quotas are strictly constrained, the analysis identified distinct operational strategies. The deficit regime W3O3F1 ranked second overall (C = 0.696, D+ = 0.147, D- = 0.336), delivering a high seed cotton yield of 6 033.33±379.66 kg/hm2, an IWUE of 1.26±0.08 kg/m3, and a PFP of 28.73±1.81 kg/kg under the lowest irrigation quota of 3 150 m3/hm2. Under moderate deficit (W2, 3 825 m3/hm2), treatments W2O3F2 (C = 0.604, rank 6), W2O1F2 (C = 0.589, rank 7), and W2O2F2 (C = 0.578, rank 8) sustained stable productivity while maintaining fiber quality indices between 16 029.08 and 18 373.55.

- W2O1F2 attained the highest fiber quality index (18 373.55±615.31), outperforming W1O1F1 by 14.13%.

- W3O3F1 achieved the maximum IWUE (1.26±0.08 kg/m3) and highest PFP (28.73±1.81 kg/kg) under deficit irrigation.

- Treatment W2O3F1 yielded the lowest overall TOPSIS closeness (C = 0.106, rank 18) due to slow early-stage nutrient release.

## Pedoclimatic Boundary Conditions and Management Constraints

This study was conducted during a single 148 d growing season in 2024 on an arid grey desert loam in Xinjiang with 198 mm annual precipitation and 1.58 g/cm3 bulk density under mulched drip irrigation.

- Field trials were restricted to medium loam soils with 18.78% field capacity, meaning that percolation dynamics and water retention under sandy or heavy clay profiles remain unverified.

- High organic substitution (30%, O3) under moderate irrigation without fulvic acid caused nutrient lag that reduced yield to 3 816.67±299.34 kg/hm2.

- Adding 45 kg/hm2 fulvic acid under severe deficit combined with 30% organic replacement (W3O3F2) caused an antagonistic depression in yield to 3 886.67±444.56 kg/hm2 and closeness to 0.116.

# Effects of Combined Application of Organic and Inorganic Fertilizers and Fulvic Acid on Cotton Yield, Quality and Soil Fertility under Deficit Irrigation

---

**DOI:** `10.11975/j.issn.1002-6819.202506037` | **Journal:** Transactions of the Chinese Society of Agricultural Engineering (农业工程学报) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** HE Xinji, PEI Dongjie, WANG Zhenhua, ZHANG Jinzhu, YE Hanchun, LI Wenhao, WEN Yue  
**Affiliation:** College of Water Conservancy and Architectural Engineering, Shihezi University

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

This study aims to explore the three-factor interaction of irrigation amount, combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers, and fulvic acid on soil fertility and cotton growth under drip irrigation. A field experiment was conducted under mulch in Xinjiang in 2024. A three-factor randomized experiment consisted of 18 treatments in total. Three irrigation levels were set: 4 500 m3/hm2 (W1), 3 825 m3/hm2 (W2), and 3 150 m3/hm2 (W3). Three levels of combined organic-inorganic fertilizer application with equal nitrogen content were established: no organic fertilizer + 600 kg/hm2 urea (O1), 2 000 kg/hm2 organic fertilizer + 510 kg/hm2 urea (O2), and 4 000 kg/hm2 organic fertilizer + 420 kg/hm2 urea (O3). Two levels of fulvic acid were included: no fulvic acid addition (F1) and 45 kg/hm2 fulvic acid addition (F2). Soil water and nutrient parameters, crop growth, yield and quality, as well as water and fertilizer use efficiency were evaluated. The results showed that fulvic acid addition increased soil water storage at the seedling stage under identical irrigation and fertilizer regimes compared to non-addition treatments, while declining during the flowering and boll-forming stage. Multi-criteria TOPSIS evaluation identified W1O2F2 as optimum for yield maximization (closeness degree 0.726), while W2O1F2, W2O2F2, and W3O3F1 achieved water conservation, stable yield, and resource efficiency in arid zones.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- At the budding stage, adding fulvic acid altered soil water storage by 7.83% under W1 and 18.02% under W2, but decreased storage by -6.32% under severe deficit W3.
- End-of-season soil organic matter in the 0-20 cm layer increased by 30.30% under W1 and 80.40% under W2 with fulvic acid addition, yet declined by -17.68% under W3.
- Boll dry matter responded biphasically to organic substitution and fulvic acid, shifting by 22.51% under O1 and 23.69% under O2, but dropping by -25.57% under O3.
- Peak seed cotton yield reached 6 833.33±256.54 kg/hm2 under W1O2F2, achieving an irrigation water use efficiency of 1.12±0.04 kg/m3 and partial nitrogen productivity of 26.80±1.01 kg/kg.
- Comprehensive TOPSIS analysis ranked W1O2F2 first with a closeness degree of 0.726, followed by W3O3F1 at 0.696 and W1O2F1 at 0.669.

abstract_en: To optimize the cultivation techniques of flue-cured tobacco cultivar 'Yunyan 116' in Shuangjiang, Yunnan, an orthogonal field experiment L9(3^4) was conducted to address recurring production issues including difficult yellowing at maturity, strong green off-odor, and unbalanced internal chemical composition. Four factors at three levels were investigated: nitrogen application rates (99, 111, and 123 kg/hm2), planting densities (1200 mm x 500 mm, 1100 mm x 500 mm, and 1000 mm x 500 mm), topping periods (bud stage, early flowering, and full flowering), and leaf retention counts (18, 20, and 22 leaves). Agronomic traits, secondary and trace mineral elements, cured leaf chemical constituents, sensory quality scores, and aroma-causing volatile compounds were determined. Plant height, stem circumference, and pitch expanded with rising nitrogen application, whereas maximum leaf length and width peaked with early topping and lower leaf retention. Nitrogen application predominantly governed plant height, pitch, maximum leaf length, and sensory quality. Planting density exerted primary control over total sugar, reducing sugar, total alkaloids, potassium oxide, and major aroma groups. To promote leaf maturity and rectify green impurity, the combination of 111 kg/hm2 nitrogen, bud-stage topping, and 20 retained leaves provides ideal morphological and metabolic balance.

analysis_markdown_en:
In the Shuangjiang tobacco production area of Yunnan, the flue-cured cultivar 'Yunyan 116' frequently exhibits delayed yellowing at maturity, pronounced green residual impurities, and unbalanced chemical composition. To resolve these agronomic constraints, an orthogonal experimental design L9(3^4) was executed evaluating nitrogen application rate, planting density, topping period, and retained leaf count. Agronomic dimensions, mineral nutrition, key chemical constituents, sensory performance, and volatile aroma profiles were systematically quantified. Results establish that balanced intermediate nitrogen combined with bud-stage topping and 20 retained leaves resolves leaf opening and yellowing limitations, while targeted adjustments enable directional optimization for either intensified aroma or harmonious sensory smoothness.

## Orthogonal Agronomic Trait Modulation and Canopy Dynamics

In the hot subtropical ecological environment of Shuangjiang County, Yunnan, field evaluations at an elevation of 992.34 m demonstrated substantial phenotypic sensitivity in 'Yunyan 116' across nitrogen, spacing, topping timing, and leaf retention treatments. Nitrogen fertilization operated as the primary driver of vertical expansion, increasing average plant height from 79.77 cm at 99 kg/hm2 to 92.95 cm at 123 kg/hm2, with a maximum individual treatment height of 99.36 cm observed in T7. However, high nitrogen fertilization exacerbated carbon-nitrogen metabolic competition, leading to leaf narrowing, as evidenced by a length-to-width ratio of 2.28 in T9.

Topping timing and leaf retention acted as direct modulators of lamina expansion and apical dominance suppression. Removing the apical flower bud at the visible bud stage increased the maximum leaf width mean to 35.17 cm and leaf length to 68.06 cm, whereas full-flowering topping restricted leaf width to 32.16 cm. Combining bud-stage topping with a moderate plant spacing of 1000 mm x 500 mm in T6 achieved peak lamina expansion with a leaf width of 37.12 cm and length of 68.18 cm, demonstrating that moderate canopy density in high-radiation regions optimizes light distribution without causing severe mutual shading.

- Stem circumference ranged from 10.12 cm in T2 to 11.08 cm in T9, mainly influenced by plant density and topping stage.

- Pitch expanded progressively across nitrogen levels from 3.75 cm at level 2 to 4.07 cm at level 3, reaching a peak of 4.20 cm in T9.

- Leaf retention of 18 leaves yielded the highest average leaf length of 68.15 cm, compared to 65.89 cm when retaining 22 leaves.

## Tri-Dimensional Information Propagation and Dynamic Prompt Formulation

In agricultural product reviews, consumers routinely state vivid opinions without explicitly repeating the target aspect noun. For instance, statements describing fruit as sweet or sour implicitly target taste, whereas descriptions of berries being small target physical size. Traditional pipeline and unified ABSA models fail to link these implicit pairs, while general large language models struggle with multi-character colloquial Chinese phrasing and suffer from high operational latency.

To capture hierarchical dependencies, DMP-BTL-DA constructs parallel sequence decoding streams governed by a dual-channel attention module. The architecture couples linear attention for global representation with self-attention for local feature interactions. This mechanism executes progressive tri-dimensional information passing across aspect terms, opinion terms, and sentiment polarities. Concurrently, dynamic prompt templates generate explicit and implicit target guidance prompts that are prepended to token embeddings, enabling pre-trained BERT layers to anchor domain-specific agricultural vocabulary before conditional random field sequence decoding.

- Dynamic prompt templates explicitly query explicit targets, implicit targets, and opinion expressions.

- Linear attention channels reduce computation while preserving global sentence dependencies.

- Conditional random field layers enforce sequence labeling constraints across multi-character spans.

## Domain-Specific Consumer Sentiment Distribution Across Product Attributes

Granular parsing of the grape corpus revealed distinct consumer focus distributions across product dimensions. Taste constituted the dominant attribute, accounting for 28.85% of all extracted aspect entities (11 559 mentions), of which 8 280 were identified as implicit aspect mentions. Overall, taste received overwhelmingly favorable feedback, with 84.48% positive sentiment and only 13.51% negative sentiment.

In contrast, quality was the second most frequent attribute, comprising 16.08% of total mentions (6 444 terms, including 4 984 implicit mentions). However, quality generated 57.68% negative feedback (3 717 negative mentions) and only 41.03% positive feedback, primarily driven by spoilage and freshness decay during transit. Similarly, weight accounted for 2% of mentions but exhibited a 53.42% negative rate, signaling that deviations in package mass immediately trigger customer complaints. Attributes like packaging (90.37% positive) and cost-performance (87.01% positive) exhibited strong customer satisfaction.

- Taste is the primary commercial driver, representing 28.85% of all extracted aspect terms.

- Quality and weight are the primary negative drivers, exceeding 50% negative sentiment ratios.

- Packaging achieved the highest positive polarity rate at 90.37% across 3 344 mentions.

This study introduces DMP-BTL-DA, a specialized deep learning architecture designed for aspect-based sentiment analysis on agricultural e-commerce text. Standard sequence models and general large language models struggle when consumer reviews omit explicit aspect targets or deploy diverse multi-character agricultural descriptors. Evaluated on a curated corpus of 18 984 Chinese grape e-commerce reviews, DMP-BTL-DA integrates BERT vector representations, a dual-encoding layer combining 1D convolution and recurrent convolutional neural networks, dual-channel attention for progressive tri-dimensional feature transfer, dynamic prompt templates, and conditional random fields. It achieves F1 scores of 89.3% for aspect extraction, 87.3% for opinion extraction, and 86.3% for sentiment polarity classification.

## Operational Boundary Conditions and Annotation Scope Constraints

While DMP-BTL-DA demonstrates superior aspect-opinion extraction precision on fresh produce text, its operational framework relies on specific boundary conditions and manual labeling configurations.

- The dataset of 18 984 reviews is restricted to domestic Chinese e-commerce platforms and grape cultivars, requiring transfer testing before generalization to broader agricultural categories.

- The dynamic prompting mechanism depends on predefined template archetypes, which require domain re-calibration when adapting to commodities with distinct attribute vocabularies.

- The 8:2 train-test partition presupposes high-quality token-level manual BIO annotations, which are labor-intensive to establish for emerging agricultural product categories.

analysis_markdown_en:
Conventional gas exchange photosynthetic rate measurement requires 3 to 5 minutes waiting for chamber carbon dioxide to establish an equilibrium steady state. To accelerate this latency-constrained workflow, researchers designed DBE-TSNet, a dual-branch time-series network trained with a Gaussian negative log-likelihood loss to jointly predict steady-state concentration and predictive uncertainty. Implemented on a time-shared single-sensor gas exchange architecture across eight plant species under three illumination tiers, DBE-TSNet cut measurement latency by an average of 128.87 s (51% cycle reduction) while keeping error below 1 μmol/mol.

## Dual-Branch Differential Network Architecture and Gaussian Loss

Single-sensor photosynthetic measurement devices switch gas circuits alternately between leaf assimilation chambers and reference ambient channels. This produces biphasic transient signals characterized by a descending concentration curve during leaf photosynthesis and an ascending recovery curve upon switching back to reference airflow. To handle these non-stationary trajectories without mutual feature corruption, DBE-TSNet adopts a symmetrical dual-branch feature encoding pipeline. Each branch takes a six-dimensional vector comprising carbon dioxide concentration, sensor temperature, leaf chamber temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and volumetric flow rate.

Input tensors first pass through a Differential Enhancement module that executes first-order numerical differencing across time steps and concatenates the resulting temporal derivatives with original physical quantities into a twelve-channel tensor. The feature map then passes through four cascaded Across-Channel Convolution and Linear Channel Transform stages. The convolutional block compresses channel redundancy through a narrow-to-wide bottleneck, while the linear transform compresses sequence length by half at each tier without blending cross-channel semantics. Global average pooling condenses features before an aggregation multi-layer perceptron predicts a four-dimensional vector containing steady-state values and corresponding uncertainty variances.

To balance parameter updates despite Bernoulli random masking applied to ascending sequences during augmentation, the network is optimized with an amplified Gaussian negative log-likelihood loss function incorporating a residual scale multiplier k=20 and an ascending-stage weighting coefficient of 2.

- Diff module doubles temporal input dimensionality from 6 to 12 channels by appending instantaneous derivative dynamics.

- Stacked across-channel convolutions extract localized transient patterns while linear channel transforms halve temporal lengths per layer.

- Joint optimization balances prediction precision against calibrated uncertainty estimation via heteroscedastic likelihood minimization.

## Empirical Benchmarking and Comparative Ablation Evaluation

Model evaluation was conducted on an experimental dataset of 960 time-series profiles gathered from eight plant species including Zea mays, Solanum tuberosum, Raphanus sativus, Brassica rapa subsp. chinensis, Lactuca sativa, Eriobotrya japonica, Citrus reticulata, and Broussonetia papyrifera across low, medium, and high photosynthetically active radiation regimes. Baseline comparisons against standard time-series architectures confirmed the superiority of DBE-TSNet across all statistical metrics. Standard recurrent architectures such as LSTM and GRU required 17.85 and 52.59 GFLOPS respectively, while DBE-TSNet required only 0.80 GFLOPS.

Linear baseline D-Linear and inverted Transformer i-Transformer struggled on the short, highly non-linear saturation curves, yielding higher descending-phase MAE values of 3.77 μmol/mol and 7.15 μmol/mol respectively. Ablation testing demonstrated that omitting differential enhancement, cross-channel convolution, or linear transforms degrades predictive stability. Specifically, removing linear channel transforms caused ascending-phase MAE to spike from 2.07 μmol/mol to 11.07 μmol/mol, underscoring the necessity of structured temporal downsampling.

- DBE-TSNet attained optimal descending root mean square error of 2.43 μmol/mol and ascending root mean square error of 3.95 μmol/mol.

- Baseline i-Transformer suffered severe over-fitting on short sequences, recording ascending RMSE of 15.64 μmol/mol and R2 of 0.755.

- Computational complexity remained at 0.80 GFLOPS, facilitating direct deployment onto embedded edge controllers.

## Uncertainty-Driven Early Termination and Dynamic Latency Truncation

Empirical calibration across partitioned uncertainty deciles revealed a strictly monotonic relationship between network uncertainty and residual error. When predictive uncertainty falls into lower intervals, absolute errors consistently remain within tight physiological tolerances. Selecting stopping thresholds of 0.026 7 for descending stages and 0.014 6 for ascending stages ensures that downstream assimilation rate calculations operate with errors below 1 μmol/mol.

During live execution, input sequence length is expanded step-by-step from an initial measurement point until predicted uncertainty drops below threshold. Under this operational policy, descending measurements terminated after an average input duration of 54.14 s (40% of standard baseline sampling), saving 77.81 s. Ascending measurements terminated after 71.54 s (61% of baseline duration), saving 51.06 s. In total, the system required only 125.68 s of sensor recording, conserving 128.87 s per full cycle and demonstrating stable generalization across divergent leaf morphologies and illumination levels.

- Descending sequence requirements dropped from full equilibrium length down to an average sampling duration of 54.14 s.

- Ascending sequence requirements settled at an average of 71.54 s, representing an input segment ratio of 0.61.

- Total measurement time was reduced by 128.87 s per plant sample, achieving an overall cycle duration reduction of approximately 51%.

## Hardware Coupling and Gas Path Transferability Constraints

DBE-TSNet relies on temporal trajectory signatures that reflect both leaf biological response and chamber pneumatic characteristics. Alterations in mechanical chambers or sensing modules require targeted recalibration.

- Model inference parameters are intrinsically conditioned on specific pneumatic hardware geometries, chamber mixing volumes, and sensor lag profiles.

- Transferring the framework across differing instrument designs necessitates supplementary baseline collection, transfer learning, or fine-tuning to realign trajectory representations.

- Current implementations evaluate terminal gas concentrations; joint multi-task estimation of simultaneous transpiration and stomatal conductance remains an open research direction.

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

analysis_markdown_en:
## Field Trial Architecture and Soil Interaction Dynamics

In southern China, acidic red soils pose severe production constraints for peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) due to high acidity, depleted organic reserves, and acute exchangeable calcium deficiencies. Excessive nitrogen application frequently exacerbates soil acidification and inhibits rhizobial nodulation, whereas calcium deficiency promotes empty pods, rotten kernels, and blackened embryos. To identify sustainable nutrient combinations under chemical fertilizer reduction targets, a split-plot randomized block experiment was instituted in 2023 across two acidic paddy-derived red soil locations: Jinxian, Nanchang (28°35'N, 116°17'E) and Linchuan, Fuzhou (27°98'N, 115°43'E).

The experimental framework evaluated twelve factorial treatment combinations formed by three nitrogen levels—conventional N1 (120 kg/hm2), 20% reduction N2 (96 kg/hm2), and 40% reduction N3 (72 kg/hm2)—crossed with four slaked lime application rates: C1 (0 kg/hm2), C2 (300 kg/hm2), C3 (600 kg/hm2), and C4 (900 kg/hm2). Basal fertilization supplied 70% of urea and 70% of potassium chloride alongside full doses of calcium magnesium phosphate and slaked lime, while remaining nitrogen and potassium were topdressed at the flowering and pegging stages to support reproductive development.

- Field sites featured acidic red soils cultivated with cultivar Qianyou No. 1 at a planting density of 300000 plants/hm2.

- Slaked lime purity was verified at 90% with a calcium oxide equivalent of 68% applied as broadcast base fertilizer.

- Phosphorus was standardized across all subplots at 90 kg/hm2 P2O5, and potassium was maintained at 120 kg/hm2 K2O.

This study evaluates the agronomic and physiological interactions between nitrogen fertilizer reduction and calcium supplementation in peanut (cultivar Qianyou No. 1) across two typical red soil sites in Jiangxi Province (Jinxian and Linchuan). Testing three nitrogen levels (120 kg/hm2, 96 kg/hm2, and 72 kg/hm2) and four calcium levels (0, 300, 600, and 900 kg/hm2 as slaked lime), researchers quantified dry matter accumulation, organ-specific nutrient partitioning, and final pod yields. Applying 900 kg/hm2 calcium markedly compensated for nitrogen reductions, lifting average yields by 4.73% under 20% reduced nitrogen compared to conventional nitrogen without calcium.

## Biomass Accumulation and Yield Component Synergy

Dry matter accumulation at maturity responded strongly to both nitrogen availability and lime supplementation, ranking in organ biomass as seed > stem > leaf > shell > root. Across both experimental sites, average total dry matter spanned from 10697.99 kg/hm2 in the N2C1 treatment to 13804.92 kg/hm2 under N1C4. Conventional nitrogen N1 increased root dry matter accumulation by 9.11% and 12.17% relative to N2 and N3, establishing robust belowground infrastructure for nutrient interception.

Yield component analysis revealed that nitrogen-calcium interaction lifted 100-pod weight and 100-kernel weight by 5.44% and 3.70% over uncalcified controls. Although conventional N1 achieved 2.57% and 3.98% higher yields than N2 and N3 across all lime levels, calcium additions compensated for lower nitrogen inputs. Specifically, under 20% nitrogen reduction, N2C3 and N2C4 generated 4.73% higher average yield than N1C1. Under 40% reduction, N3C3 and N3C4 produced a 3.46% yield surplus over N1C1, demonstrating the agronomic viability of lime-assisted nitrogen conservation.

## Differential Nitrogen and Calcium Translocation Hierarchies

Elemental accumulation profiles diverged sharply between macronutrient nitrogen and secondary nutrient calcium. Total nitrogen uptake ranged from 205.91 kg/hm2 in N2C1 to 274.39 kg/hm2 in N1C4. Across organs, nitrogen followed the hierarchy seed > leaf > stem > shell > root, with average allocation proportions of 64.84% in seed, 16.56% in leaf, 8.20% in stem, 7.64% in shell, and 2.91% in root. Highest total nitrogen accumulation occurred under N1, exceeding N2 and N3 by 11.52% and 1.95%. Lime inputs exerted an undeniable priming effect: C4 augmented total nitrogen accumulation by 4.52%, 10.77%, and 20.66% over C3, C2, and C1.

Conversely, calcium accumulated predominantly in vegetative sinks: leaf > stem > shell > seed > root. Mean calcium distribution rates were 58.01% in leaves, 27.68% in stems, 5.78% in shells, 5.36% in seeds, and 3.17% in roots. Total calcium uptake reached 188.13 kg/hm2 in N1C4, representing a 31.90% enhancement over C1. Because calcium translocates via transpirational xylem flow, foliage served as the dominant terminal reservoir, while pod-zone calcium directly bolstered shell integrity and suppressed pod blanking.

- Foliar calcium accumulation reached 101.48 kg/hm2 under N1, surpassing N2 by 15.50% and N3 by 8.19%.

- Seed nitrogen allocation peaked at 71.38% under specific nitrogen-calcium combinations, confirming active remobilization during seed filling.

- Average calcium accumulation under nitrogen-calcium interaction increased by 23.42% compared with treatments lacking lime.

## Regional Boundary Conditions and Single-Season Evaluation Constraints

This investigation provides robust empirical verification for lime-assisted nitrogen reduction in southern red soils, but its conclusions are bounded by temporal, environmental, and varietal limitations.

- The empirical dataset derives from a single cropping season (2023), requiring multi-year weather cycle validation before establishing generalized regional fertilization guidelines.

- Field trials exclusively utilized the cultivar Qianyou No. 1; varying genotypes with divergent nodulation capacities or calcium absorption efficiencies may exhibit differing optimal thresholds.

- Soil properties were limited to acidic paddy-derived red soils in Jiangxi Province, which limits direct extrapolation to neutral or calcareous soils.

# Effects of Nitrogen Fertilizer Reduction and Calcium Interaction on Nitrogen and Calcium Accumulation, Distribution, and Yield in Peanuts

---

**DOI:** `10.19802/j.issn.1007-9084.2025109` | **Journal:** Chinese Journal of Oil Crop Sciences (中国油料作物学报) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** LI Ya-zhen, HAN De-peng, WU Hao, HUANG Tian-bao, XIONG Wen, CHENG Ye-wei, ZHANG Mei-wei, XIAO Xiao-jun, CHEN Ming, YU Xi-chu, RAO Wen-ping, CHEN Rong-hua, ZHENG Wei  
**Affiliation:** Jiangxi Institute of Red Soil and Genetic Resource/Key Laboratory of Arable Land Improvement and Quality Improvement of Jiangxi Province, Nanchang 330046, China

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

To investigate the effects of nitrogen reduction and calcium fertilizer application rates on peanut nutrient accumulation and yield, a field experiment was conducted using cultivar Qianyou No. 1 at two red soil sites in Jiangxi Province: Jinxian, Nanchang and Linchuan, Fuzhou. Treatments integrated three nitrogen levels (N1: 120 kg/hm2 conventional rate, N2: 96 kg/hm2 or 20% reduction, N3: 72 kg/hm2 or 40% reduction) and four calcium levels (C1: 0 kg/hm2 control, C2: 300 kg/hm2, C3: 600 kg/hm2, C4: 900 kg/hm2 as slaked lime). Results demonstrated that nitrogen-calcium interaction increased 100-pod weight and 100-kernel weight by 5.44% and 3.70% on average compared to C1. At maturity, dry matter accumulation under C4, C3, and C2 increased by 2381.57 kg/hm2, 1721.916 kg/hm2, and 1270.08 kg/hm2 over C1. Nitrogen accumulation across organs followed the hierarchy seed > leaf > stem > shell > root, with seed allocation averaging 64.84%. Conversely, calcium accumulation followed leaf > stem > shell > seed > root, with leaf allocation averaging 58.01%. Under 20% nitrogen reduction, combined treatments N2C3 and N2C4 boosted average yields by 4.73% relative to N1C1, demonstrating that calcium supplementation effectively mitigates yield losses from nitrogen reduction in acidic red soil cultivation.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Nitrogen-calcium interaction enhanced average 100-pod weight by 5.44% and 100-kernel weight by 3.70% compared to no calcium application (C1).
- Total dry matter at maturity increased under C4, C3, and C2 by 2381.57 kg/hm2, 1721.916 kg/hm2, and 1270.08 kg/hm2, respectively, relative to C1.

## Microtopographic Modification and Population Tiller Dynamics

In semi-arid winter wheat production regions, structural field redesign such as furrow sowing modifies micro-environmental parameters, including localized thermal retention and soil water redistribution. During the wintering phase of the 2020-2021 season, furrow sowing (P1) produced 591.11×104 plants/hm2, surpassing flat planting (P3, 444.44×104 plants/hm2) by 33.0%. This accelerated early canopy development is attributed to sheltered furrow geometry, which mitigates winter desiccating winds and concentrates topsoil moisture.

However, late-spring freeze events during the jointing window imposed thermal stress on advanced tillers. While P1 maintained elevated tiller counts at jointing (1360.01×104 plants/hm2 under P1S60), subsequent tiller mortality resulted in converged anthesis population densities between P1 and P3. Conversely, ridge sowing (P2) exhibited depressed tiller populations across jointing (817.78×104 to 1044.45×104 plants/hm2) and maturity (326.33×104 to 346.45×104 plants/hm2). The elevated ridge profile accelerated moisture drainage away from critical rooting horizons, forcing excessive tiller abortion that restricted final ear bearing capacity.

- Wintering tiller densities peaked under furrow sowing at 591.11×104 plants/hm2 compared to 493.33×104 in ridge sowing and 444.44×104 in flat planting.

- Jointing populations peaked under P1S60 at 1360.01×104 plants/hm2 before stabilizing through anthesis and grain fill.

- Ridge sowing led to significant spike count depressions of 29.0% and 25.2% across consecutive experimental years.

Agricultural sustainability across semi-arid winter wheat production regions faces acute challenges from declining groundwater reserves and inefficient traditional flood irrigation. This two-year field investigation evaluated the physiological and agronomic synergy of pairing micro-topographical planting geometries (furrow sowing, ridge sowing, and flat planting) with precision supplemental irrigation targeted to 0-40 cm or 0-60 cm soil profiles based on real-time moisture deficits. Furrow sowing paired with 0-60 cm supplemental irrigation maintained high tiller counts and biomass via border-row edge effects while slashing irrigation volume by 34.5% and lifting irrigation water use efficiency by 79.5%.

Targeted replenishment based on pre-irrigation profile moisture measurements markedly reduced non-productive deep percolation. By restricting water delivery to the active 0-60 cm root zone rather than saturating deeper subsoil strata, P1S60 attained a two-season mean IWUE of 196.25 kg·m-3 in 2020-2021 and 87.60 kg·m-3 in 2021-2022, eclipsing the conventional flood control values of 83.26 kg·m-3 and 74.24 kg·m-3. ## Agronomic Edge Compensations and Production Economics

The agronomic success of furrow sowing hinges upon edge-row compensation mechanisms. While overall planting row spacing in furrow configurations reduces effective inner-row area, border plants benefit from superior microclimate conditions, enhanced incident light interception, and side-slope soil moisture retention. In P1S60, border plants achieved 52.75 grains per spike in 2020-2021, counteracting population trade-offs and delivering a grain yield of 8.83 t·hm-2, outperforming flat flood irrigation (8.27 t·hm-2).

Economic analysis revealed that P1S60 generated the highest gross output value among furrow systems at 26457.32 yuan/hm2, surpassing P3SCK (25638.48 yuan/hm2). Water expenditure dropped from 200.00 yuan/hm2 in flood irrigation to 130.92 yuan/hm2 under S60. However, manual ridge shaping and trench excavation added 3600 yuan/hm2 in labor input, compressing net income to 18226.40 yuan/hm2 compared to 20938.48 yuan/hm2 under flat flood irrigation. Transitioning from manual labor to standardized mechanization remains imperative to unlock the complete financial viability of the P1S60 system.

- Grains per spike under P1S60 reached 52.75 in 2020-2021, significantly exceeding P3SCK at 40.30.

- Total production cost under P1S60 was 8230.92 yuan/hm2, driven by 3600 yuan/hm2 of manual shaping labor.

- Gross output-to-input ratio reached 3.210 for P1S60 compared to 3.080 for P1SCK and 5.450 for P3SCK.

## Regional Boundary Conditions and Agronomic Constraints

The field trial findings apply primarily to the semi-arid, irrigated Loess Plateau and Guanzhong Plain conditions featuring silt loam soils and semi-humid drought-prone climates.

- Economic returns are heavily penalized by manual labor expenditure (3600 yuan/hm2) for trenching and ridge formation, necessitating regional mechanization to realize commercial profitability.

- Supplemental irrigation restricted strictly to 0-40 cm (S40) provoked yield depressions of 8.0% and 2.4% relative to flood irrigation due to insufficient root zone wetting during critical reproductive phases.

- Extreme climatic events such as late-spring cold snaps during the jointing period can accelerate the mortality of early tillers in sheltered furrow environments.

- The agronomic evaluations were benchmarked using a single winter wheat cultivar, Xinong 20, requiring further multi-genotype validation across contrasting soil textures.

Establishing suitable soilless substrate regimes assists in mitigating root-zone thermal stress and bolstering plant resilience. Although T1 accumulated higher soluble sugars and starches across vegetative and reproductive tissues, T2 yielded 18 862 g per 0.5 m2, outperforming T1 by 43.59%. Consequently, all-perlite soilless cultivation offers robust physiological buffering for commercial over-summer protected cucumber production.

## Agronomic Trait Differentiation and Thermal Canopy Dynamics

In southern subtropical production zones, high ambient greenhouse temperatures ranging between 30 deg C and 33 deg C impose chronic stress on climbing fruit cucumber crops. Evaluating canopy architecture over a 48-day cycle demonstrated divergent structural allocation between coconut coir-based blends and pure perlite media. The composite organic blend (T1) fostered rapid apical dominance, driving plant height to 380.67 cm at day 48 compared to 336.00 cm in pure perlite (T2).

In contrast, plants established in all-perlite media directed resources toward structural girth and leaf area expansion. By day 48, T2 maintained a stem diameter of 9.43 mm, representing a 9.65% increase over T1. Maximal leaf length and width under T2 reached 36.33 cm and 32.16 cm, outperforming T1 by 14.71% and 16.22% respectively. This robust vegetative framework provided enhanced physical support and photosynthetic interception under high radiation loads.

- Perlite media exhibit lower water and nutrient retention capacity relative to organic coir, requiring continuous automated fertigation to prevent rapid desiccation.

## Phenotypic Growth Recovery Across Divergent Nodulation Phenotypes

Nitrogen deficiency imposes severe morphological restrictions on young soybean seedlings, which exhibit limited biological nitrogen fixation capacity prior to the establishment of functional root nodules. In this study, sand-cultured near-isogenic lines (WT and MT) exposed to a nitrogen level of 2.11 mmol·L⁻¹ exhibited pronounced stunting compared to seedlings under 7.31 mmol·L⁻¹ nitrogen. Low nitrogen stunted shoot height, narrowed stem caliper, restricted total foliar expansion, and curtailed primary root elongation and root volume development.

Supplying 5 mmol·L⁻¹ GABA for 3 consecutive days at the V2 stage substantially reversed low nitrogen growth inhibition across both genotypes. Over sampling points at 20 and 30 days post-treatment, nodulating MT seedlings under LN+GABA achieved average increases of 95.73% in plant height, 36.36% in stem diameter, 80.99% in total leaf area, 37.19% in root length, and 105.78% in root volume relative to LN alone. The non-nodulating WT exhibited average improvements of 53.59% in plant height, 47.24% in stem diameter, 110.65% in leaf area, 39.61% in root length, and 99.18% in root volume, demonstrating strong systemic responsiveness to exogenous GABA intervention.

- Nodulating MT leaf dry weight increased by 42.77%, stem dry weight by 94.78%, and root dry weight by 46.63% under LN+GABA relative to LN.

- Non-nodulating WT demonstrated dry matter gains of 104.05% in leaves, 123.43% in stems, and 74.46% in roots following GABA drenching.

This investigation assesses the physiological mechanisms by which exogenous gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) alleviates low nitrogen stress in soybean seedlings. Utilizing a pair of near-isogenic lines with divergent nodulation phenotypes (non-nodulating WT and nodulating MT), seedlings were evaluated under normal nitrogen (7.31 mmol·L⁻¹), low nitrogen stress (2.11 mmol·L⁻¹), and low nitrogen supplemented with 5 mmol·L⁻¹ GABA. Exogenous GABA substantially stimulated vegetative growth, root elongation, and dry matter accumulation. It coordinated enhanced antioxidant enzyme activity with elevated sucrose, fructose, and soluble sugar pools, demonstrating a dual role in ROS scavenging and carbon metabolic reprogramming.

## Antioxidant Enzymatic Reinforcement and Reactive Oxygen Scavenging

Nitrogen limitation disrupts cellular redox equilibrium, accelerating the generation of reactive oxygen species that cause membrane lipid peroxidation and organelle dysfunction. Seedlings subjected to low nitrogen exhibited higher baseline superoxide anion generation rates and increased hydrogen peroxide accumulation than normal nitrogen controls. Although stress alone stimulated endogenous antioxidant activity, the response was insufficient to halt oxidative stress.

Application of exogenous GABA systematically elevated the catalytic activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), catalase (CAT), and ascorbate peroxidase (APX) in both foliar and radical tissues across days 5, 10, 20, and 30. In MT root tissues, activities rose by 9.78% for SOD, 18.14% for POD, 24.87% for CAT, and 20.24% for APX, driving down root O2- generation rate and H2O2 content by 8.25% and 10.50%, respectively. In WT roots, antioxidant gains were even more pronounced, with SOD, POD, CAT, and APX surging by 16.88%, 33.09%, 29.89%, and 16.07%, accompanying reductions of 10.75% in O2- production rate and 5.96% in H2O2 content.

- Foliar CAT activity in non-nodulating WT seedlings increased by 36.12% under LN+GABA treatment compared to LN alone.

- Foliar H2O2 concentration in non-nodulating WT seedlings decreased by 13.12% under exogenous GABA treatment.

## Sucrose Metabolic Reprogramming and Carbon Allocation Dynamics

Nitrogen deficiency restricts photosynthetic carbon assimilation and alters sucrose transport and partitioning between source leaves and sink organs. Seedlings exposed to low nitrogen displayed lower sucrose concentrations alongside elevated levels of fructose and total soluble sugars, reflecting altered source-sink relationships. Drenching with 5 mmol·L⁻¹ GABA counteracted this imbalance by significantly enhancing sucrose, fructose, and soluble sugar pools in both leaves and roots.

Key enzymatic regulators of sucrose synthesis and breakdown responded robustly to GABA treatment. In MT leaves and roots, sucrose synthase (SUS), sucrose phosphate synthase (SPS), acid invertase (AI), and neutral invertase (NI) activities increased by mean values ranging from 9.27% to 24.28%. In non-nodulating WT, where biological fixation cannot supply reduced nitrogen, invertase activities exhibited pronounced increases: leaf AI and NI increased by 16.75% and 15.02%, while root AI and NI rose by 18.37% and 18.59%. This enzymatic induction facilitated accelerated sucrose hydrolysis to yield carbon skeletons and energy currency required for stress adaptation.

- Foliar sucrose, fructose, and soluble sugar pools in MT seedlings increased by 40.84%, 19.09%, and 17.09% following GABA application.

- Mantel analysis confirmed that antioxidant enzymes, ROS markers, and sucrose metabolic enzymes correlated positively with plant morphology and biomass accumulation.

## Methodological Constraints and Agronomic Applicability

This investigation evaluated sand-cultured soybean seedlings under controlled rain-sheltered conditions with nutrient solutions supplied at 7.31 mmol·L⁻¹ and 2.11 mmol·L⁻¹ nitrogen. While exogenous 5 mmol·L⁻¹ GABA markedly improved growth metrics, values remained below normal nitrogen controls, and field soil buffering effects remain unexamined.

- Growth and physiological parameters under 5 mmol·L⁻¹ GABA did not fully restore seedling performance to normal nitrogen levels (7.31 mmol·L⁻¹).

- Trials were conducted in washed sand within rain shelters; soil mineral dynamics, microbial competition, and field leaching remain uncharacterized.

- Treatments were applied via daily root irrigation of 500 mL per pot across 3 consecutive days at the V2 stage, requiring calibration for commercial foliar or fertigation regimes.

analysis_markdown_en:
This study analyzes 28,530 dairy herd improvement records from 3,042 lactating dual-purpose Simmental cows in Shandong Province from 2021 to 2024. Using mixed linear models and Wood incomplete gamma curves, the authors evaluated how parity, testing season, calving season, lactation stage, and parity-by-calving season interactions regulate milk yield, milk components, and somatic cell scores. The population averaged 22.77 kg/d milk yield with a somatic cell score of 1.97. High-parity cows calved in summer suffered significant production and udder health penalties, whereas spring calving yielded the highest peak milk yield across parities.

## Phenotypic Variation and Main Non-Genetic Effects

In commercial loose-housing systems within the Huang-Huai-Hai agricultural zone, dual-purpose Simmental cattle exhibited an average daily milk production of 22.77 kg·d-1 across 26,428 validated test records, ranging from 2.10 kg·d-1 to 58.10 kg·d-1. Compositional constituents demonstrated tight biological regulation, with milk fat percentage averaging 4.12% (SD 0.82%, CV 19.83%), milk protein percentage averaging 3.54% (SD 0.35%, CV 9.80%), and total solids averaging 14.07% (SD 1.18%, CV 8.39%). In contrast, somatic cell score exhibited wide phenotypic dispersion with a mean of 1.97 (SD 1.46, CV 73.95%), remaining well below the clinical threshold of 4.0 and reflecting robust herd-level mammary health.

Mixed linear model evaluation indicated that parity, testing season, and lactation stage exerted statistically significant impacts across all assessed lactation parameters (P<0.01). Milk production scaled directly with parity progression, climbing from 18.49±0.15 kg·d-1 in first parity to 26.92±0.16 kg·d-1 in cows of parity 3 and above, alongside an elevation in somatic cell score from 1.93±0.03 to 2.15±0.03. Testing season introduced environmental variations: winter testing corresponded to lowest daily yield (21.98±0.16 kg·d-1) but peak milk fat (4.36±0.01%), total solids (14.44±0.02%), and lowest somatic cell score (1.89±0.03), driven by nutritional concentration and reduced thermal load.

- Milk yield expanded by 45.59% from parity 1 (18.49±0.15 kg·d-1) to parity 3 and above (26.92±0.16 kg·d-1).

- Peak lactation stage (36 to 100 days in milk) generated 26.05±0.15 kg·d-1 milk yield, compared to 17.74±0.16 kg·d-1 in late lactation (201 to 305 days in milk).

- Calving season significantly affected all parameters (P<0.01) except the fat-to-protein ratio (P=0.84).

## Parity and Calving Season Interaction Dynamics

Analysis of parity-by-calving season interaction revealed significant regulatory effects across 8 lactation traits (P<0.05), with the fat-to-protein ratio representing the sole non-significant metric. Low-parity cows (parities 1 and 2) displayed minor susceptibility to calving season shifts, whereas cows at parity 3 and above exhibited severe vulnerability to summer calving. High-parity cows calving during summer experienced pronounced depressions in milk yield, milk fat percentage, fat yield, and protein yield relative to cohorts calving in spring, autumn, or winter.

Concurrently, summer-calving cows in the third and higher parities recorded elevated somatic cell scores compared to those calving in spring and winter. This selective sensitivity in mature cows aligns with the cumulative physiological wear of prolonged lactation cycles and the compound metabolic strain of elevated temperature-humidity index during periparturient periods. Younger primiparous cows maintained greater stress resilience during summer calving, underscoring divergent management requirements across herd age cohorts.

- Significant parity-by-calving season interaction occurred for daily milk yield, fat percentage, fat yield, protein percentage, protein yield, lactose percentage, total solids, and somatic cell score (P<0.05).

- Summer-calving cows of parity >=3 experienced a concurrent decline in milk fat percentage and increase in somatic cell score.

- Fat-to-protein ratio remained unaffected by the interaction term across all parities.

## Mathematical Fitting of Incomplete Gamma Lactation Curves

Lactation dynamics fitted with Wood incomplete gamma functions demonstrated standard single-peak trajectories with peak lactation consolidating within 30 to 100 days in milk across all cohort strata. Curve parameter estimation revealed that advancing parity systematically advanced the timing of peak lactation day across all four calving seasons. In parity 1, lactation peak occurred at 75.8261 days for spring calving, 60.4406 days for summer calving, 60.5637 days for autumn calving, and 76.1118 days for winter calving.

By parity 3 and above, the peak lactation day shifted earlier to 46.4512 days for spring calving, 29.1366 days for summer calving, 42.0846 days for autumn calving, and 49.0618 days for winter calving. Across all parities, spring calving achieved the greatest peak yield (23.4912 kg·d-1 in parity 1; 30.7703 kg·d-1 in parity 2; 34.9125 kg·d-1 in parity >=3). Lactation persistency was lowest in summer calving groups (6.8538 in parity 1; 6.5382 in parity 2; 6.3338 in parity >=3), confirming spring as the optimal calving window in this region.

- Peak lactation day accelerated from 75.8261 d in parity 1 spring to 46.4512 d in parity >=3 spring.

- Peak yield reached a maximum of 34.9125 kg·d-1 in parity >=3 spring-calving cows.

- Summer-calving cows across all parities recorded the lowest persistency values, dropping to 6.3338 in parity >=3.

## Methodological Scope and Regional Environmental Constraints

This study derives its empirical data from a single intensive commercial dairy operation in Shandong Province, reflecting management conditions of the temperate Huang-Huai-Hai farming basin under total mixed ration feeding.

- Records were sourced from 3 042 cows within one large-scale facility in Shandong Province, which may not capture environmental variations found in pastoral grazing systems of Northwest or Northeast China.

- Cows of parity 3 and above were consolidated into a single group due to smaller sample sizes in later parities, precluding granular evaluations of parity 4 through 7.

- The dataset was restricted to milk production records between 5 and 305 days in milk with at least 3 test records per cow, excluding extended lactation curves beyond 305 days.

**Affiliation:** College of Animal Science and Technology, China Agricultural University, Beijing 100193, China

## 1. Executive Abstract

This study evaluated the effects and interaction mechanisms of non-genetic factors on milk production traits in Chinese dual-purpose Simmental cattle. Based on a large-scale commercial dairy farm in Shandong Province, a total of 28 530 DHI records were collected from 3 042 lactating adult Simmental cows from 2021 to 2024. After data quality control, a mixed linear model was adopted to analyze the effects of non-genetic factors, including parity, testing season, calving season, and lactation stage, on key milk production traits, such as milk yield, milk fat percentage, milk protein percentage, and somatic cell score (SCS). Meanwhile, the Wood model was used to fit lactation curves of cows grouped by different parities nested within calving seasons. The average milk yield of this population was 22.77 kg·d-1 with a coefficient of variation of 39.07%. The coefficient of variation of SCS was relatively high at 73.95%, while other milk composition traits showed stable performance. Parity, testing season, and lactation stage exerted significant effects on all milk production traits (P<0.05). Calving season had significant effects on all traits except the fat-to-protein ratio. The interaction between parity and calving season significantly affected eight indicators excluding fat-to-protein ratio. Lactation peak was concentrated at 30 to 100 days in milk, peak day advanced with increasing parity, and spring-calving cows achieved the highest peak yield.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Mean test-day milk yield was 22.77 kg·d-1 with a coefficient of variation of 39.07%, while somatic cell score averaged 1.97 with a variation coefficient of 73.95%.
- Milk yield increased across parity from 18.49±0.15 kg·d-1 in parity 1 to 23.45±0.15 kg·d-1 in parity 2 and 26.92±0.16 kg·d-1 in parity 3 and higher.
- Interaction between parity and calving season significantly influenced 8 production traits (P<0.05), with summer-calving cows of parity >=3 experiencing the steepest drops in milk yield, fat yield, and protein yield.
- Lactation curves fitted via the Wood model demonstrated that lactation peak occurred between 30 and 100 days in milk, with peak day advancing as parity increased.
- Spring-calving cows achieved the highest peak milk yield across parities, reaching 23.4912 kg·d-1 in parity 1, 30.7703 kg·d-1 in parity 2, and 34.9125 kg·d-1 in parity 3 and above.

abstract_en: To clarify the regulatory effects of the synergistic interaction between ARC microbial inoculant and nitrogen fertilizer on peanut yield, and to provide a theoretical basis for green and high-yield peanut cultivation, this study investigated the responses of photosynthetic characteristics in peanut varieties with contrasting nodulation traits to combined inoculant and nitrogen application. A two-year field pot experiment (2023-2024) was conducted using a highly nodulating cultivar Xianghua 11 (XH11) and a non-nodulating line DH9, with two ARC inoculant rates (0 kg·hm⁻², T0; 30 kg·hm⁻², T1) and two nitrogen application levels (0 kg·hm⁻², N0; 75 kg·hm⁻² pure N, N1). Results showed that the combined application of ARC inoculant and nitrogen fertilizer significantly improved photosynthetic efficiency, promoted dry matter accumulation, and optimized yield components compared with single-factor treatments. Specifically, the T1N1 treatment (30 kg·hm⁻² ARC + 75 kg·hm⁻² N) significantly increased main stem height, lateral branch length, leaf chlorophyll content, net photosynthetic rate, evaporation rate, and stomatal conductance in both peanut genotypes. For XH11, two-year average dry matter accumulation under T1N1 was 13.90% and 28.86% higher than that under T1 and N1 alone, respectively, accompanied by increases of 20.79% and 18.29% in pod number per plant, 16.73% and 23.85% in filled pod number, and 13.58% and 8.77% in kernel yield per plant. For DH9, T1N1 increased dry matter accumulation by 8.81% and 22.32%, pod number by 18.14% and 7.95%, filled pod number by 26.78% and 17.95%, and kernel yield by 12.50% and 12.75% compared with T1 and N1 alone, respectively. These findings indicate that the synergistic effect of ARC inoculant and nitrogen fertilizer in T1N1 treatment is superior to single-factor applications, providing a viable strategy for high-efficiency cultivation.
