## Root Morphological Remodeling and Vegetative Architecture Expansion

The co-application of ARC microbial inoculant and chemical nitrogen fertilizer markedly stimulated aboveground canopy development and belowground root architecture in both peanut genotypes across the 2023 and 2024 growing seasons. Across all experimental configurations, main stem height and lateral branch length followed the hierarchical order of T1N1 > T1N0 > T0N1 > T0N0. In the non-nodulating line DH9, T1N1 produced average increases of 12.50%, 6.94%, and 14.77% in main stem height, alongside gains of 12.84%, 8.62%, and 14.55% in lateral branch length, reflecting a higher relative responsiveness than that observed in the nodulating cultivar XH11.

Root scanning revealed consistent structural improvements under synergistic treatment. Total root length peaked at the pod-setting stage, where T1N1 expanded root length relative to T0N0 by 24.43% and 22.03% in XH11 during 2023 and 2024, respectively, compared to 36.79% and 24.21% in DH9. Root surface area exhibited maximum increases of 30.28% in XH11 and 45.20% in DH9. The amplified root proliferation in DH9 suggests that non-nodulating lines compensate for absent symbiotic nitrogen fixation through greater root exploration when stimulated by plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria.

- DH9 showed greater percentage increases in stem height and lateral branch length than XH11 under T1N1.

- Root surface area expansion was pronounced in DH9, reaching a 45.20% maximum increase over T0N0.

- Both cultivars achieved maximum total root length during the pod-setting stage.

This two-year outdoor pot study examines the synergistic interaction of ARC microbial inoculant (30 kg·hm⁻²) and chemical nitrogen fertilizer (75 kg·hm⁻² pure N) on peanut genotypes with contrasting nodulation capacities: high-nodulating Xianghua 11 (XH11) and non-nodulating DH9. Combined application (T1N1) consistently outperformed single-factor applications across both genotypes, markedly stimulating vegetative growth, root elongation, leaf chlorophyll synthesis, and stomatal gas exchange. Consequently, T1N1 augmented dry matter accumulation and single-plant pod productivity while reducing dependency on excess mineral nitrogen, establishing a viable biological approach for resource-efficient crop management.

## Photosynthetic Gas Exchange and Pigment Concentration Dynamics

Leaf pigment synthesis was systematically enhanced by the interaction of nitrogen and ARC inoculant. In both test years, total chlorophyll (chlorophyll a+b) levels were consistently higher in DH9 than in XH11, with T1N1 maintaining peak pigment concentrations through the pegging and pod-setting stages. During the pegging stage across 2023-2024, DH9 reached maximum chlorophyll a+b values of 2.49 mg·g⁻¹ and 2.57 mg·g⁻¹ under T1N1, outperforming all single-input and control treatments.

## Dry Matter Partitioning and Pod Yield Component Optimization

Dry matter accumulation increased steadily across developmental stages, culminating at pod-setting. Across both years, total dry matter followed T1N1 > T1N0 > T0N1 > T0N0. - XH11 produced single plant yields of 53.33±3.30 g in 2023 and 55.57±1.92 g in 2024 under T1N1.

- Yield correlated positively with main stem length, branch length, and dry matter accumulation in both genotypes.

## Experimental Scope and Agronomic Boundary Conditions

This study was conducted under outdoor pot culture conditions in Shenyang using brown earth soil across two seasons, testing fixed dosages of 30 kg·hm⁻² ARC inoculant and 75 kg·hm⁻² nitrogen. While providing detailed physiological insights into nodulating and non-nodulating lines, verification under large-scale mechanized field conditions across diverse soil types and varying climatic gradients is necessary before universal agronomic deployment.

- Evaluations were restricted to outdoor pots containing 30 kg soil rather than open-field agronomic microplots.

- The dosage framework tested only two binary levels for inoculant (0 and 30 kg·hm⁻²) and nitrogen (0 and 75 kg·hm⁻²), precluding continuous response surface modeling.

- Soil properties were limited to brown earth soil featuring alkaline hydrolysis nitrogen of 117.7 mg·kg⁻¹ (2023) and 119.1 mg·kg⁻¹ (2024).

analysis_markdown_en:
Automated selective harvesting of roses requires discriminating subtle morphological stages under complex field illumination, occlusion, and scale divergence. This study introduces YOLOv8n-dy, an edge-oriented detector tailored for bud, full bloom, and withered stages. The architecture replaces standard C2f blocks with C2f5_dyconv featuring dynamic snake convolutions and 5x5 grouped convolutions, integrates an Efficient Layer Attention module, adds a 160x160x128 shallow detection head, adopts WIOUv3 boundary loss, and optimizes training via Adamax. YOLOv8n-dy achieves 79.2% precision, 71.3% recall, and 77.3% mAP0.5 with 9.8 GFLOPs and a 6.0 MB footprint, matching YOLOv9 accuracy while requiring only 4.22% of its parameter weight.

## Architectural Reconfiguration and Dynamic Snake Convolution

In natural rose cultivation, automated selective harvesting demands distinct actions depending on physiological maturity: bud stages are harvested for cut flowers, full bloom flowers are gathered for essential oil extraction, and withered flowers require pruning for disease suppression. Standard one-stage detectors struggle with bud detection because green sepals blend seamlessly with foliage backgrounds, while distant viewpoints render buds as diminutive targets. To overcome these morphological challenges, the C2f backbone blocks are upgraded to C2f5_dyconv modules. The C2f5_dyconv module splits input channels into dual parallel pathways: one pathway applies standard 3x3 convolutions coupled with 1x1 convolutions for core detail retention, whereas the complementary pathway executes parallel 5x5 grouped convolutions and dynamic snake convolutions.

Dynamic snake convolution introduces learnable offsets constrained along linear axes to trace meandering petal contours and slender pedicels without losing spatial continuity. By expanding the effective receptive field from 3x3 to 9x9 via bilinear interpolation of continuous coordinate offsets, the module successfully covers irregular boundaries of compact buds. Furthermore, to retain fine-grained spatial cues lost during successive downsampling, the feature fusion network alters its starting resolution from the default 80x80x256 tensor to a high-resolution 160x160x128 feature map. This addition of a specialized small-target detection layer, paired with parameter reduction across parallel convolutional pathways, trims total model parameter count down to 2.71 M compared to 3.01 M in vanilla YOLOv8n.

- Dynamic snake convolution applies continuous kernel coordinate offsets with bilinear interpolation to maintain contiguous receptive coverage across meandering floral pedicels and sepals.

- Channel splitting and grouped 5x5 convolution reduce the parameter count of the upgraded convolutional block by approximately 7.15% relative to the standard C2f module.

- Extending the multi-scale feature pyramid network to 160x160x128 feature maps prevents the erosion of subtle bud textures prior to deep feature propagation.

## Attention Decoupling and Dynamic Boundary Regression Optimization

Deep convolutional networks frequently suffer from channel degradation where prominent floral heads suppress weak activation signals originating from smaller buds. To counter this without imposing prohibitive computational burdens, an Efficient Layer Attention (ELA) block is inserted at layer 7 of the backbone. ELA decouples the 2D spatial feature map into two 1D parallel feature vectors along horizontal and vertical axes using 1D average pooling, 1D convolution, and group normalization. This directional decomposition preserves exact coordinate sensitivity across long-range spatial dependencies while utilizing cross-weight multiplication to enhance discriminative petal color patterns and suppress overlapping foliage distractors.

Bounding box regression is simultaneously stabilized by substituting standard CIOU with WIOUv3. While CIOU penalizes aspect ratio discrepancies, it exhibits low sensitivity toward tiny targets and suffers from gradient imbalance when encountering blurry background noise. WIOUv3 applies a dynamic non-monotonic focusing mechanism that assigns lower outlier penalties to high-quality anchor boxes, establishing a smooth gradient profile that shields backpropagation from harmful outliers. Coupled with the Adamax optimizer, which regulates first-order directional momentum and second-order step limits to prevent convergence into sub-optimal local minima, the network attains rapid convergence within the initial 50 epochs.

- ELA strips away 2D computational redundancy by performing 1D pooling and grouped normalization across horizontal and vertical spatial dimensions.

- WIOUv3 dynamic focusing assigns balanced outlier scores across bounding boxes, lifting bud stage mAP0.5 to 71.6% compared to 64.4% for GIOU and 67.5% for DIOU.

- Adamax adaptive optimization accelerates early loss descent, eliminating plateau oscillations observed under standard SGD solvers.

## Empirical Edge Validation and In-Field Robotic Prototyping

A rigorous field dataset comprising 1 562 augmented training images, 235 test images, and 233 validation images captured under variable sunny and cloudy conditions at 30~50 cm distances served as the benchmark. Across comparative evaluations against thirteen YOLO family detectors, YOLOv8n-dy established a dominant performance-to-complexity trade-off. It matched the detection accuracy of YOLOv9 (77.3% vs. 77.2% mAP0.5) while operating at 9.8 GFLOPs versus 313.4 GFLOPs, reducing model size from 142.1 MB to 6.0 MB and cutting parameter weight by 95.78%. Compared to larger medium variants such as YOLOv8s and YOLOv10s, YOLOv8n-dy improved mAP0.5 by 1.4 and 2.4 percentage points while using roughly 23.3% of the parameter volume of YOLOv8s.

Grad-CAM++ visual interpretability heatmaps confirm that YOLOv8n-dy concentrates attention directly onto perimeter petal contours and structural flower stems rather than over-focusing on interior textures. When deployed onto an intelligent mobile platform equipped with an industrial camera, onboard power supply, and host controller running ONNX Runtime with CUDA acceleration, the system converted video streams into normalized 640x640 BGR tensors, executing real-time multi-stage flowering identification at 30 frames/s average detection frame rate and 58 frames/s inference speed.

- Outperforms lightweight baselines YOLOv5n, YOLOv8n, and YOLOv10n in mAP0.5 by 7.9, 6.1, and 6.6 percentage points, respectively.

- Maintains 0.71 confidence on moderately occluded blooming blossoms and achieves 0.96 confidence on withered targets against complex soil backgrounds.

- Delivers 58 frames/s inference throughput under ONNX Runtime, satisfying operational thresholds for real-time robotic harvesting end-effectors.

## Geographic Sample Boundaries and Robotic Integration Scope

While YOLOv8n-dy establishes high precision and lightweight efficiency across multiple rose growth stages, several operational boundaries constrain direct generalized deployment across all commercial settings.

- Dataset samples originate exclusively from regional rose production bases in Anning and Kunming, Yunnan Province, limiting phenotypic variability across non-regional cultivars and distinct greenhouse trellising systems.

- The training set relies on 781 manually annotated source images expanded to 1 562 frames, presenting opportunities for semi-supervised expansion to mitigate labeling overhead for rare color cultivars.

- In crowded clusters where buds and full blossoms coexist, the model exhibited 2 missed bud detections due to high overlap densities.

- Field tests validated visual frame rates on a mobile cart, but physical grasping dynamics, robotic arm hand-eye calibration, and end-effector vibration remain uncoupled from current visual evaluations.

analysis_markdown_en:
Coastal saline-alkali soils restrict cotton productivity through high salinity, alkaline pH, and degraded soil structure. Based on a long-term field experiment initiated in 2012 in Binzhou, Shandong, this study evaluated the agronomic impacts of combining annual cotton stubble returning with triennial subsoiling to a depth of 38 cm (RS treatment) compared with conventional shallow rotary tillage (CK), isolated subsoiling (S), and isolated stubble return (R). Across 2023 and 2024 evaluations, the combined RS practice decreased topsoil salinity by 21.2%-26.1% and pH by 6.6%-7.7%, elevated organic carbon and nitrogen availability, and enhanced full-bloom net photosynthetic rate, stomatal conductance, and canopy light interception, culminating in a 56.2% two-year average increase in lint yield.

## Pedological Desalinization and Edaphic Nutrient Enrichment Dynamics

Coastal saline-alkali environments present adverse edaphic constraints characterized by elevated sodium ion saturation, high alkalinity, dense bulk density, and impoverished organic matter reserves. In this multi-year trial established in 2012, rotary tillage to 20 cm (CK) perpetuated surface salt accumulation and physical compaction. Combining annual full-quantity cotton stalk shredding (3-5 cm lengths incorporated via rotary tillage) with triennial subsoiling to 38 cm depth (RS) altered profile chemistry across both the 0-20 cm and 20-40 cm strata.

Over the 2023 and 2024 monitoring seasons, RS lowered 0-20 cm soil pH from 8.39-8.40 in CK down to 7.75-7.78, while suppressing salt content from 4.16 g kg-1 to 3.27-3.28 g kg-1. The organic carbon pool within 0-20 cm expanded from 4.57-4.59 g kg-1 under CK to 8.14-8.18 g kg-1 under RS, accompanied by an increase in total nitrogen from 0.49-0.51 g kg-1 to 0.79-0.81 g kg-1. Available phosphorus and potassium in the topsoil also increased under RS, reaching 17.43-18.35 mg kg-1 and 215.65-223.42 mg kg-1, respectively.

The underlying mechanism stems from the organic acids released during stalk decomposition, which neutralize soil alkalinity, and the formation of humic colloidal complexes that adsorb sodium ions. Concurrently, subsoiling fractures the subsurface plow pan, enhancing hydraulic conductivity, accelerating downward salt leaching, and facilitating deep root exploration into subsoil layers.

- 0-20 cm topsoil salt content dropped from 4.16 g kg-1 (CK) to 3.28 g kg-1 (2023) and 3.27 g kg-1 (2024) under RS.

- 0-20 cm soil organic carbon rose by up to 78.2% in RS compared to CK, reaching 8.18 g kg-1 in 2023.

- Available potassium in the 20-40 cm subsoil reached 106.15 mg kg-1 in 2023 under RS, compared to 45.86 mg kg-1 under CK.

## Photosynthetic Apparatus Optimization and Canopy Light Interception

Photosynthetic capacity serves as the foundational driver for dry matter synthesis and lint formation. Under saline stress, stomatal closure and chlorophyll degradation typically depress gas exchange. In this study, the alleviation of edaphic constraints under RS significantly promoted leaf and canopy photosynthetic traits, particularly during the critical full bloom and boll-setting stage.

In 2023, RS increased full-bloom net photosynthetic rate (Pn) by 13.6% over CK, while in 2024 S and RS increased Pn by 9.1% and 18.6%, respectively. Stomatal conductance (Gs) under RS exceeded CK by 35.0% to 50.7%, enabling greater carbon dioxide influx to support assimilation. Conversely, intercellular carbon dioxide concentration (Ci) at full bloom decreased relative to vegetative stages, indicating heightened enzymatic carboxylation efficiency. Transpiration rate (Tr) and SPAD chlorophyll indices also exhibited substantial enhancements under RS.

At the canopy scale, photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) absorption ranged between 858.62 and 1305.13 μmol m-2 s-1, with light interception (PARin) spanning 75% to 93%. RS increased leaf area index (LAI) across all three growth stages by 25.8% to 58.7% over CK without causing canopy lodging or light starvation in lower strata, maintaining PARin improvements up to 17.0% during boll opening.

- Full-bloom leaf Pn increased by a two-year average of 15.9%, alongside a 42.9% mean surge in stomatal conductance Gs.

- Canopy light interception rate (PARin) during the 2024 boll-opening stage increased by 17.0% under RS compared to CK.

- Chlorophyll relative content (SPAD) under RS was consistently higher than CK, S, and R across all developmental checkpoints.

## Biomass Translocation Sink Dynamics and Lint Yield Determination

Cotton yield formation relies on the coordinated partitioning of photoassimilates and absorbed mineral nitrogen from vegetative organs toward reproductive structures. Early in the season (squaring stage), dry matter and nitrogen were predominantly partitioned into leaves and stems. As development progressed toward boll opening, reproductive organs became the primary sink.

Under RS, enhanced root foraging and improved rhizosphere nutrient availability translated into dramatic biomass gains. By the boll-opening period, whole-plant dry matter accumulation and nitrogen accumulation under RS increased by 59.8% and 72.0% (two-year averages) compared to CK. In 2024, RS dry matter accumulation at boll opening exceeded CK by 76.6%, with nitrogen accumulation in stems, leaves, and reproductive bolls exceeding CK by 55.2% to 277.3%.

Lint yield reflected these physiological enhancements. In 2023, lint yield reached 1661 kg hm-2 under RS versus 1010 kg hm-2 under CK (a 64.5% increase). In 2024, RS yielded 1720 kg hm-2 compared to 1163 kg hm-2 in CK (a 47.9% increase). Boll density was the principal yield component explaining this gain, rising from 60.1-65.0 x 10^4 hm-2 in CK to 84.3-86.3 x 10^4 hm-2 in RS, whereas lint percentage remained stable around 39.2% to 42.5%.

- 2023 lint yield increased from 1010 kg hm-2 in CK to 1661 kg hm-2 in RS (P < 0.05).

- 2024 lint yield reached 1720 kg hm-2 in RS, surpassing CK (1163 kg hm-2) and S (1353 kg hm-2).

- Boll density under RS reached 84.3 x 10^4 hm-2 (2023) and 86.3 x 10^4 hm-2 (2024), demonstrating reproductive sink dominance.

## Regional Scope, Mechanical Requirements, and Longitudinal Boundaries

This study evaluates the agronomic and physiological responses of cotton cultivar Lumianyan 37 under specific temperate monsoon coastal saline-alkali conditions in northern Shandong, utilizing a fixed triennial subsoiling schedule and annual stalk crushing protocol.

- Field trials were conducted in a single coastal agroecological zone in Binzhou, Shandong (mean annual precipitation 570 mm, mean temperature 14.4 degrees Celsius), which may differ from inland arid saline regions.

- The subsoiling treatment requires high-horsepower tractors capable of reaching 38 cm working depth, demanding appropriate mechanical infrastructure.

- The experimental site had undergone continuous stubble returning and subsoiling since 2012, indicating that the observed magnitude of soil improvements reflects cumulative decadal effects rather than single-season conversions.

- Evaluations focused exclusively on continuous monoculture cotton (one crop per year) managed under plastic mulch and specific fertilizer dosages (120 kg hm-2 N, 132 kg hm-2 P2O5, 36 kg hm-2 K2O).

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

## 1. Executive Abstract

Stubble returning and subsoiling represent key agronomic practices for ameliorating coastal saline-alkali lands, yet the physiological mechanisms governing cotton photosynthetic enhancement and dry matter allocation under long-term conservation tillage remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a long-term field platform established in 2012 on coastal saline-alkali soil in Binzhou, Shandong Province, was examined over the 2023 and 2024 growing seasons under four tillage regimes: conventional tillage (CK, rotary tillage to 20 cm), subsoiling (S, 38 cm triennial subsoiling), stubble return (R, annual stalk chopping and rotary incorporation), and integrated stubble return with subsoiling (RS). These results demonstrate that synergistic stubble returning and subsoiling remediate coastal soil saline stress and drive robust reproductive sink growth.

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Integrated stubble returning and subsoiling (RS) significantly reduced soil pH by 6.6%-7.7% and soil salt content by 21.2%-26.1% (P < 0.01) relative to conventional tillage.

abstract_en: High temperature severely constrains soybean growth and development, leading to significant yield losses. The development of heat-tolerant cultivars necessitates the identification of elite germplasm with stable field tolerance. In this study, comparative field experiments were conducted under natural conditions across two ecological sites—Hefei (high-temperature group) and Xuzhou (control group)—over three consecutive seasons from 2018 to 2020. A total of 608 soybean germplasm accessions (484 domestic and 124 foreign) were systematically evaluated for phenotypic variation across plant height, bottom pod height, main stem node number, effective branch number, pod number per plant, seed weight per plant, and 100-seed weight. Variance and linear mixed model analyses demonstrated that temperature differences between locations served as the primary driver of agronomic variance. Under high temperature, main stem node number increased significantly, whereas bottom pod height, effective branch number, pod number per plant, seed weight per plant, and 100-seed weight decreased significantly. Six core heat-responsive traits were transformed via principal component analysis into three principal components explaining a cumulative variance of 74.23%. Based on comprehensive T-values derived from fuzzy membership functions, cluster analysis classified the 608 accessions into five response tiers: extremely sensitive (9), slightly sensitive (123), moderately sensitive (309), mildly sensitive (158), and non-sensitive (9). Elite heat-insensitive foreign germplasms, notably Kanto 102, Suzumaru, Bedford, and PI80828-1, demonstrated exceptional reproductive resilience under heat stress.

## Multi-Environment Natural Heat Stress Characterization

Rising summer temperatures across the Huang-Huai-Hai plain and southern China present acute challenges to soybean reproductive development and yield stability. While controlled-environment phytotrons allow uniform heat stress application, artificial simulations frequently diverge from field dynamics where diurnal temperature swings, humidity fluctuations, and radiation interact. To capture authentic agronomic responses, this investigation conducted systematic comparative field trials across 608 soybean accessions between 2018 and 2020 at two distinct agro-ecological sites: Hefei (Anhui Province, designated as the high-temperature treatment group) and Xuzhou (Jiangsu Province, designated as the control group). The accession panel comprised 484 domestic varieties spanning Northern, Huang-Huai-Hai, and Southern ecotypes alongside 124 international lines sourced from the National Crop Genebank of China.

Microclimatic tracking verified pronounced thermal divergence between the two sites. Over the entire growing duration, Hefei exhibited an average temperature of 27.22°C (0.95°C higher than Xuzhou) and recorded 20.99 days with daily maximum temperatures exceeding the 35°C critical threshold, which was 8.99 days more than Xuzhou. Cumulative effective thermal accumulations in Hefei reached 1723.02 d·°C across the full cycle, 203.52 d·°C during flowering, and 330.60 d·°C during pod filling, exceeding Xuzhou by 165.38 d·°C, 9.63 d·°C, and 42.75 d·°C, respectively. Linear mixed models showed that temperature differences between locations served as the dominant main effect impacting effective branch number (F=116.79**), 100-seed weight (F=81.24**), and seed weight per plant (F=46.95**).

- Field trials paired high-heat Hefei against temperate Xuzhou across three full summer cropping cycles.

- Hefei recorded 20.99 days above 35°C compared to 12.00 days in Xuzhou, establishing sustained natural heat stress.

- Best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) was implemented to isolate intrinsic genetic sensitivity from confounding meteorological covariates.

Under escalating summer heat stress across major soybean production zones, identifying germplasm with stable heat tolerance under natural field conditions remains essential. This study conducted three-year paired field trials from 2018 to 2020 in Hefei (high-temperature treatment) and Xuzhou (control) across 608 soybean accessions. Utilizing linear mixed models and best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP), the authors verified that temperature drove major trait variations. By calculating high-temperature response coefficients (HTRC) and integrating principal component analysis with fuzzy membership functions, accessions were clustered into five distinct sensitivity classes, identifying elite non-sensitive foreign accessions including Kanto 102, Suzumaru, Bedford, and PI80828-1.

## Multivariate Dissection of High Temperature Response Coefficients

To isolate intrinsic physiological heat responses from background soil and microclimatic variability, best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) was implemented across accessions and years. Analysis of variance on BLUP values demonstrated that plant height remained invariant across environments (F=0.002), whereas reproductive and yield-determining traits underwent sharp phenotypic alterations under elevated temperatures. Specifically, bottom pod height declined by 4.15% (F=14.715**), effective branch number dropped by 19.00% (F=437.693**), pod number per plant decreased by 4.79% (F=27.657**), seed weight per plant shrank by 17.82% (F=740.117**), and 100-seed weight declined by 4.97% (F=13.061**). Conversely, main stem node number exhibited an increase of 5.68% (F=45.807**), reflecting heat-induced vegetative elongation compensations.

High-temperature response coefficients (HTRC), calculated as the ratio of trait expressions under heat stress to control conditions, spanned from 0.33 to 2.08 across the panel. Effective branch number exhibited the lowest mean HTRC (0.81±0.15, CV=18.96%), indicating extreme sensitivity to heat-induced lateral bud suppression. Principal component analysis on standardized HTRC values compressed the six responsive traits into three orthogonal dimensions explaining 74.23% of total variance. Principal component 1 (35.92% contribution) was governed by seed weight per plant (0.87), pod number per plant (0.87), and effective branch number (0.57). Principal component 2 (20.36%) captured bottom pod height architecture (0.88), while principal component 3 (17.95%) was dominated by 100-seed weight (0.91).

- Branching capacity and individual seed yield exhibited the highest vulnerability to natural thermal stress.

- Principal components cleanly decoupled yield sink capacity, plant structural architecture, and single-seed mass filling.

- Composite heat tolerance T-values were generated through fuzzy membership transformation weighted by component eigenvalues.

## Germplasm Clustering and Identification of Elite Donors

Using Euclidean distance group linkage clustering at a threshold distance of 10.0, the composite heat response index (T-value) separated the 608 accessions into five distinct sensitivity categories. The distribution of T-values conformed to normality with skewness of 0.16 and kurtosis of 0.69.

Phenotypic contrast between Level I and Level V revealed fundamentally divergent developmental trajectories under stress. In Level I accessions, heat stress induced severe drops in bottom pod height (F=18.15**), effective branch number (F=34.95**), pod number per plant (F=7.78*), and seed weight per plant (F=84.40**), with seed weight crashing from 20.84±2.18 g to 12.78±1.48 g. Strikingly, the four highest-ranking heat-insensitive accessions were all foreign germplasms: Kanto 102 (WDD02286, T=0.655), Suzumaru (WDD02152, T=0.604), Bedford (WDD00698, T=0.595), and PI80828-1 (WDD00623, T=0.585). Regional cultivars in the Huang-Huai-Hai zone exhibited intermediate sensitivity, demonstrating that exotic introductions provide critical allelic diversity for breeding climate-resilient cultivars.

- All top four heat-insensitive germplasms were foreign introductions, highlighting an essential source for broadening genetic diversity.

- Cultivated Huang-Huai-Hai varieties showed moderate susceptibility, underscoring the urgent need to introduce exotic tolerance alleles.

## Methodological Constraints and Breeding Transferability

While natural multi-year field evaluations provide authentic agro-ecological stress exposure, several operational caveats and ecological boundaries condition the applicability of these findings.

- Natural field testing inevitably superimposes secondary environmental covariates, such as rainfall distribution and relative humidity, although mixed models verified temperature as the primary driver.

- The 608 evaluated accessions were deliberately filtered to align in maturity with Huang-Huai-Hai ecotypes, limiting direct extrapolation to ultra-short-season northern or tropical late-maturity groups.

- Top-performing insensitive donors such as Kanto 102 and Bedford require pre-breeding hybridization to eliminate potential linkage drag before incorporation into high-yielding domestic elite backgrounds.

**Affiliation:** College of Life Sciences, Yangtze University

## 1. Executive Abstract

High temperature severely constrains soybean growth and development, leading to significant yield losses. The development of heat-tolerant cultivars necessitates the identification of elite germplasm with stable field tolerance. In this study, comparative field experiments were conducted under natural conditions across two ecological sites—Hefei (high-temperature group) and Xuzhou (control group)—over three consecutive seasons from 2018 to 2020. A total of 608 soybean germplasm accessions (484 domestic and 124 foreign) were systematically evaluated for phenotypic variation across plant height, bottom pod height, main stem node number, effective branch number, pod number per plant, seed weight per plant, and 100-seed weight. Variance and linear mixed model analyses demonstrated that temperature differences between locations served as the primary driver of agronomic variance. Under high temperature, main stem node number increased significantly, whereas bottom pod height, effective branch number, pod number per plant, seed weight per plant, and 100-seed weight decreased significantly. Six core heat-responsive traits were transformed via principal component analysis into three principal components explaining a cumulative variance of 74.23%. Based on comprehensive T-values derived from fuzzy membership functions, cluster analysis classified the 608 accessions into five response tiers: extremely sensitive (9), slightly sensitive (123), moderately sensitive (309), mildly sensitive (158), and non-sensitive (9). Elite heat-insensitive foreign germplasms, notably Kanto 102, Suzumaru, Bedford, and PI80828-1, demonstrated exceptional reproductive resilience under heat stress.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Thermal divergence between Hefei and Xuzhou served as the primary driver of trait shifts, with effective branch number (F=116.79**) and 100-seed weight (F=81.24**) exhibiting marked temperature sensitivity.

- Principal component analysis of six standardized high-temperature response coefficients compressed trait variations into three components capturing a cumulative contribution rate of 74.23%.
- Cluster analysis classified 608 accessions into five sensitivity tiers: Level I extremely sensitive (9 accessions), Level II slightly sensitive (123), Level III moderately sensitive (309), Level IV mildly sensitive (158), and Level V non-sensitive (9).
- Elite foreign accessions Kanto 102 (T=0.655), Suzumaru (T=0.604), Bedford (T=0.595), and PI80828-1 (T=0.585) exhibited superior heat insensitivity, maintaining seed weight and significantly increasing pod number per plant under stress.

analysis_markdown_en:
Pre-harvest sprouting (PHS) inflicts severe yield and end-use quality penalties on wheat production across humid agro-ecological zones. In this comprehensive two-year investigation, researchers evaluated 1069 diverse wheat accessions using a simulated rainfall chamber protocol to quantify spike germination rates alongside nine agronomic characteristics. The germplasm exhibited pronounced susceptibility overall, with 52.9% categorized as highly susceptible and only 1.3% demonstrating high resistance. Red-grained accessions and historical landraces exhibited significantly superior resistance compared to white-grained lines and modern cultivars. Regional divergence closely aligned with precipitation gradients during grain filling, while agronomic associations revealed significant yet weak trade-offs with grain dimensions and plant architecture.

## Phenotypic Diversity and Germplasm Class Discrepancies

A panel of 1069 wheat accessions—comprising 871 domestic accessions (744 landraces and 127 cultivars) and 198 international introductions—was evaluated under controlled misting conditions across the 2022-2023 and 2023-2024 cropping cycles at the Ezhou experimental station. Spike germination rate (SGR) displayed broad phenotypic variation across the panel, spanning from 0.39% to 99.44% in both experimental years. Mean SGR shifted from 50.71% with a coefficient of variation of 49.02% in 2023 to 45.56% with a coefficient of variation of 60.87% in 2024, reflecting wide phenotypic plasticity and rich genetic variability within the assembled diversity panel.

Categorization by grain coat pigmentation confirmed substantial disparities in dormancy maintenance. White-grained accessions demonstrated an average SGR of 63.29% in 2023 and 61.40% in 2024, whereas red-grained accessions averaged 47.91% and 42.03% across corresponding years. Resistance tier classification underscored this vulnerability: 79.5% of white-grained wheat was highly susceptible and zero accessions achieved high resistance. Conversely, red-grained materials maintained a 29.9% resistant fraction (moderate resistance to high resistance). Similarly, historical landraces exhibited an average SGR of 47.86% in 2023 and 42.70% in 2024, significantly outperforming modern bred cultivars (61.84% and 51.69%) and foreign germplasm (54.30% and 52.39%).

- White-grained germplasm: 0.0% high resistance, 1.5% resistance, 4.1% moderate resistance, 14.9% susceptibility, and 79.5% high susceptibility.

- Red-grained germplasm: 29.9% aggregate resistant proportion with 47.0% high susceptibility.

- Landraces: 29.7% resistant accessions compared to approximately half that rate in cultivars and foreign germplasms.

## Agro-Ecological Climatological Selection and Regional Distribution

Evaluation across distinct Chinese agro-ecological wheat production zones revealed that PHS resistance frequencies mirror regional rainfall patterns during the pre-harvest ripening window. In the Middle and Lower Yangtze Valley Winter Wheat Region (annual rainfall 830-1870 mm, concentrated during April-June) and the South China Winter Wheat Region (annual rainfall exceeding 1500 mm), resistant germplasm proportions reached 39.6% to 40.0%, representing the highest regional resistance levels across the country.

In contrast, arid and semi-arid production zones where harvest coincides with dry periods exhibited high vulnerability due to relaxed evolutionary selection pressure. The Qinghai-Tibet Spring-Winter Wheat Region (annual precipitation 300-500 mm) and Xinjiang Winter-Spring Wheat Region (annual mean precipitation 145 mm) were dominated by susceptible and highly susceptible materials, with highly susceptible accessions accounting for 76.7% and 61.5% respectively, and resistant lines representing merely 10.5% and 7.6%. Intermediate frequencies were detected in the Southwest Winter Wheat Region and Huang-Huai Winter Wheat Region, where resistant accessions exceeded 30%.

- High resistance accessions were detected exclusively in the Qinghai-Tibet, Huang-Huai, Northeast Spring, and Middle/Lower Yangtze Valley zones (1.6% to 2.6%).

- Northwest Spring Wheat Region accessions possessed no resistant or highly resistant materials, exhibiting 20.0% moderate resistance and 51.1% high susceptibility.

- Northern Winter Wheat Region accessions (sample size 6) consisted of 1 susceptible and 5 highly susceptible accessions.

## Agronomic Trait Associations and Breeding Implications

Bivariate correlation analyses between SGR and agronomic features demonstrated statistically significant links, although the magnitude of every detected association remained low to moderate (|r|<=0.39). SGR was negatively correlated with plant height (r = -0.30 to -0.17, P<0.001) and grain color score (r = -0.27 to -0.24, P<0.001), indicating that taller plants and red caryopses correlate with lower germination and higher PHS tolerance. In contrast, SGR displayed positive correlations with grain length, grain width, and thousand grain weight (r = 0.11 to 0.23, P<0.001), showing that larger, heavier kernels are slightly more prone to premature sprouting.

Phenological traits—including days from sowing to heading and days from sowing to maturity—exhibited environment-dependent correlations with SGR, shifting from negative coefficients in 2023 (r = -0.39 to -0.24) to positive coefficients in 2024 (r = 0.12 to 0.34). Among all accessions, 11 red-grained lines maintained high resistance across both seasons, characterized by taller canopies (111.8 to 144.8 cm) and lower thousand grain weight (20.98 to 36.73 g). Crucially, 3 white-grained accessions demonstrated stable resistance, offering parental germplasm for white wheat breeding without requiring extensive linkage drag mitigation.

- Plant height and grain color score showed consistent negative correlations with SGR across testing environments.

- Grain dimension metrics (length, width, thousand grain weight) exhibited consistent positive correlations with SGR.

- Identified elite resistant donors include 11 red-grained highly resistant and 3 white-grained resistant accessions.

## Experimental Scope and Methodological Constraints

This study conducted phenotypic characterization in a uniform ecological environment over two consecutive seasons, revealing specific methodological boundaries regarding regional sample coverage and secondary dormancy dynamics.

- The Northern Winter Wheat Region included only 6 accessions, an insufficient sample size (0.6% of total panel) that precludes authoritative regional conclusions.

- Spikes were dried indoors for 7 d and preserved at -20 degrees Celsius prior to misting, which maintains primary dormancy but does not capture post-harvest dormancy decay curves under ambient storage.

- Identified highly resistant accessions possess tall plant heights (111.8 to 144.8 cm) and low thousand grain weights (20.98 to 36.73 g), necessitating backcrossing to eliminate unfavorable agronomic linkages in commercial breeding.

## Non-Visible Spectral Modulation and Reproductive Phenology

In solar greenhouse environments throughout northern China, natural solar irradiance is constrained during winter and early spring by low solar altitude angles and greenhouse structural shading. Supplementing visible red and blue wavelengths is known to drive core photosynthesis, but modulating non-visible wavebands—specifically far-red (FR, 700-800 nm) and near-ultraviolet (UVA, 315-400 nm)—acts directly on morphogenetic signaling pathways. Far-red photon addition alters the phytochrome photostationary state, stimulating shade-avoidance traits that reconfigure plant architecture for optimized canopy photon capture.

Empirical evaluation demonstrated that adding 25-30 μmol·m-2·s-1 of FR to a 9:1 red/blue background (at 270-290 μmol·m-2·s-1 total canopy PPFD) significantly accelerated reproductive development. Red/Blue 9/1+FR generated 30.3±1.4 total flower buds per plant across three successive inflorescences, compared to 19.5±0.8 in the unsupplemented control. Moreover, flowering duration required to reach anthesis was reduced to 111.8±4.6 hours compared to 139.0±7.0 hours in the control, and fruit set reached 38±1%, driving a single-plant fruit count of 9.9±0.5.

In contrast, integrating 15-20 μmol·m-2·s-1 of UVA radiation into a white spectrum induced vegetative biomass accumulation while impairing reproductive success. Although White light+UVA produced substantial aboveground dry weight (20.5±1.3 g) and elongated petiole length (22.3±0.6 cm), its maximum net photosynthetic rate declined by 29.5% relative to white light alone. Consequently, fruit set dropped to 26±1% and total flower bud formation declined to 22.9±1.0, demonstrating that continuous UVA supplementation at this intensity imposes photo-inhibitory pressure on the photosynthetic apparatus of Fragaria ananassa.

- FR integration maintained compact petiole lengths (15.0±0.6 cm) while maximizing leaf number (29.3±0.6) and reproductive output.

- UVA enrichment restricted total flower bud formation and depressed single-plant fruit yield to levels indistinguishable from unsupplemented controls.

This study evaluated supplemental LED lighting strategies for elevated substrate-cultivated 'Red Face' strawberry in a northern Chinese solar greenhouse during the winter-spring season. Testing spectral variations (Red/Blue 9/1, Red/Blue 9/1+FR, White light, White light+UVA) and photoperiod durations (10 h versus 16 h) under automated threshold-based control, the findings show that supplementing far-red light (25-30 μmol·m-2·s-1) alongside red/blue light increased yield by 45.0% over unsupplemented controls and elevated electrical energy use efficiency to 39.7 g·kWh-1. Conversely, near-ultraviolet UVA supplementation suppressed photosynthetic capacity and reproductive transition, while extending photoperiod to 16 h promoted biomass and flower bud numbers.

## Photoperiod Extension Dynamics and Energy Utilization Efficiency

Photoperiod regulation serves as an environmental cue directing assimilate partitioning between vegetative sinks and floral primordia. Extending the active photoperiod from a standard 10 h diurnal schedule (8:00-18:00) to an extended 16 h regime (8:00-24:00) using white LED fixtures dramatically transformed canopy structure. Plants under the 16 h photoperiod exhibited prominent elongation, reaching a petiole length of 28.0±0.6 cm and a total leaf area of 1769±148 cm2, compared to 18.2±1.0 cm and 1284±77 cm2 under the 10 h photoperiod.

Floral organogenesis responded strongly to daylength prolongation: the 16 h treatment accumulated 41.1±1.8 total flower buds across inflorescences, representing a 110.7% elevation over control and a 60.6% increase over the 10 h treatment. This stimulated continuous fruit set that yielded 10.3±0.6 fruits per plant, producing an overall yield expansion of 60.2% over control and 45.6% over the 10 h schedule.

From an engineering and operational expenditure perspective, electrical energy use efficiency (EUE) is the critical determinant of supplemental lighting viability. Although the 16 h lighting regime increased cumulative power consumption by 85.6% relative to the 10 h treatment, its disproportionate yield gain achieved an EUE of 32.5 g·kWh-1, representing a 142.5% improvement over the 10 h baseline. Among spectral treatments, Red/Blue 9/1+FR delivered the highest system EUE at 39.7 g·kWh-1, whereas White light+UVA registered an inefficient 3.4 g·kWh-1.

- The 16 h photoperiod generated 13.1±0.6 first, 13.9±1.3 second, and 12.4±0.9 third inflorescence flower buds.

- Automated sensor thresholds (<300 μmol·m-2·s-1 on, >500 μmol·m-2·s-1 off) ensured LED activation strictly compensated for ambient deficit periods.

## Metabolic Fruit Quality Profiles and Sugar-Acid Balance

Fruit organoleptic quality in elevated substrate strawberry depends directly on the balance of soluble sugars, titratable acids, and soluble proteins. Supplemental lighting treatments elevated titratable acid contents above the control level of 7.9±0.1 mg·g-1, reaching 10.9±0.1 mg·g-1 under Red/Blue 9/1+FR, 9.8±0.2 mg·g-1 under White light, and 9.7±0.1 mg·g-1 under the 16 h photoperiod. Soluble protein content simultaneously increased from 0.5±0.0 mg·g-1 in the unsupplemented control to 0.6±0.0 mg·g-1 across all supplemental lighting treatments.

Soluble sugar accumulation exhibited marked spectral sensitivity. Red/Blue 9/1 and Red/Blue 9/1+FR produced soluble sugar concentrations of 67.6±3.0 mg·g-1 and 66.5±1.9 mg·g-1, respectively, outperforming control (56.9±1.1 mg·g-1), white light (55.6±2.7 mg·g-1), and White light+UVA (56.6±5.1 mg·g-1). Consequently, narrow-band red and blue photons, with or without far-red supplementation, optimize carbon assimilation and sucrose translocational fluxes into ripening receptacles.

- Red/Blue 9/1 secured the highest sugar-acid ratio at 7.6±0.3, followed by control at 7.1±0.2 and Red/Blue 9/1+FR at 6.3±0.2.

- Fruit moisture remained stable across treatments, spanning 89.4±1.6% to 91.1±1.0%.

## Operational Boundary Conditions and Agronomic Constraints

The experimental outcomes apply specifically to elevated substrate cultivation of short-day strawberry cultivars under automated greenhouse supplemental lighting regimens. Transferability depends on environmental solar thresholds and fixture positioning.

- Trials were conducted exclusively on the cultivar 'Red Face' ('Hongyan') using elevated substrate troughs in a Beijing solar greenhouse, which may exhibit cultivar-specific photoperiod and phytochrome sensitivities distinct from day-neutral varieties.

- Supplemental fixtures were positioned 20 cm above the canopy with an automated operational logic triggering at ambient PPFD <300 μmol·m-2·s-1 and shutting off at >500 μmol·m-2·s-1; altering fixture distance or threshold values will shift canopy PPFD and energy consumption profiles.

- UVA addition was assessed at a specific dosage of 15-20 μmol·m-2·s-1 alongside white light; lower intermittent dosages or alternative wavebands within the UV-A spectrum were not evaluated.

# Effects of Light Quality and Photoperiod on Growth, Yield, and Quality of Substrate-Cultivated Strawberry in a Chinese Solar Greenhouse

---

**DOI:** `10.3864/j.issn.0578-1752.2026.20.008` | **Journal:** Scientia Agricultura Sinica (中国农业科学) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** ZHANG Han, LI JingLai, ZHANG YuQi, GUO Jian, LI Xing, LI Tao  
**Affiliation:** Institute of Environment and Sustainable Development in Agriculture, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Beijing 100081

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

This study investigated the effects of non-visible wavebands, specifically far-red light (FR) and near-ultraviolet light (UVA), as well as photoperiod duration on the growth, yield, and fruit quality of substrate-cultivated strawberry in a solar greenhouse, aiming to develop an efficient supplemental lighting strategy for winter-spring production in China. Using the cultivar Red Face in an elevated substrate cultivation system from September 2024 to February 2025 in Beijing, LED supplementary lighting was deployed at early flower bud differentiation with canopy photosynthetic photon flux density maintained at 270-290 μmol·m-2·s-1. Treatments encompassed Red/Blue 9/1, Red/Blue 9/1+FR (FR at 25-30 μmol·m-2·s-1), White light, White light+UVA (UVA at 15-20 μmol·m-2·s-1), and two photoperiods (10 h and 16 h), dynamically governed by solar sensors. Red/Blue 9/1+FR improved plant architecture, increased flower bud differentiation, elevated yield by 45.0% over the unsupplemented control and by 11.8% over Red/Blue 9/1, while achieving the highest electrical energy use efficiency of 39.7 g·kWh-1. Conversely, White light+UVA stimulated vegetative elongation but reduced maximum net photosynthetic rate by 29.5%, total flower buds by 15.0%, and fruit set rate by 21.2% relative to white light alone. Extending photoperiod to 16 h triggered shade-avoidance responses, enhancing total flower buds by 110.7% and total yield by 60.2% over control.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Red/Blue 9/1+FR increased total fruit yield by 45.0% over control and 11.8% over Red/Blue 9/1, boosting electrical energy use efficiency by 51.5% to 39.7 g·kWh-1.
- White light+UVA increased aboveground dry weight by 144% and total leaf area by 112% over control, but reduced maximum net photosynthetic rate by 29.5% and yield by 23.2% compared to white light.
- Extending photoperiod from 10 h to 16 h increased total flower bud differentiation by 110.7% and fruit yield by 60.2% relative to the unsupplemented control.
- Fruit soluble sugar concentration reached 67.6±3.0 mg·g-1 under Red/Blue 9/1 and 66.5±1.9 mg·g-1 under Red/Blue 9/1+FR, significantly outperforming white light treatments.
- Automated dynamic LED operation engaged when natural greenhouse PPFD fell below 300 μmol·m-2·s-1 and extinguished when ambient levels exceeded 500 μmol·m-2·s-1.

abstract_en: The aim of this trial was to investigate the amino acid limiting sequence of corn-miscellaneous-meal-type low protein diet in medium-growing yellow-feathered broilers aged 61-85 days by using the partial amino acid deletion method. A total of 756 sixty-one-day-old female medium-growing yellow-feathered broilers (Mahuang) were randomly allotted into nine groups (six repetitions per group and 14 chicks per repetition), which were fed a normal-protein diet and eight low-protein diets, respectively. The Control (NP) group was fed the normal-protein diet (crude protein 16%). The low-protein control (LP) group was fed the low-protein diet (crude protein, 14%) with the amino acid content meeting the requirement of the yellow-feathered broilers. The low-protein low-lysine (LP-Lys), low-methionine (LP-Met), low-threonine (LP-Thr), low-isoleucine (LP-Ile), low-valine (LP-Val), low-arginine (LP-Arg), and low-tryptophan (LP-Trp) groups were formulated by reducing the levels of true available Lys, Met, Thr, Ile, Val, Arg, and Trp by 20% from LP group, respectively; amino acids that did not reach the 20% reduction threshold were adjusted based on actual deficiency values. The trial duration was 25 days. The results showed no significant differences in growth performance and body quality among all groups (P>0.05). When using optimal feed/gain as the evaluation index, the amino acid restriction order was Met>Lys>Val>Ile>Arg>Thr>Trp, with a proper ratio of 100:46:64:67:80:107:17. For optimal jejunal villus height to crypt depth ratio, the sequence was Thr>Arg>Met>Val>Ile>Trp>Lys (100:45:78:72:86:118:19). For optimal serum immunoglobulin A level, the sequence was Ile>Thr>Arg>Met>Trp>Lys>Val (100:43:81:80:63:124:19).

analysis_markdown_en:
This study evaluated the limiting amino acid sequence and ideal dietary ratios in 61 to 85-day-old female medium-growing yellow-feathered broilers (Mahuang) fed net-energy-formulated corn-miscellaneous-meal diets. Reducing crude protein from 16% to 14% with essential amino acid supplementation preserved growth performance and carcass traits while tending to improve serum albumin and jejunal morphology. Deletion trials revealed that the limiting amino acid sequence varies across physiological target endpoints: methionine is primary for feed-to-gain ratio, threonine dominates mucosal structural integrity, and isoleucine governs systemic humoral immunity.

## Dietary Formulation Dynamics and Growth Preservation

In response to escalating volatile soybean meal prices and rigorous agricultural nitrogen abatement mandates, the formulation of poultry rations has increasingly transitioned toward net energy systems utilizing non-conventional miscellaneous oilseed meals. In this experimental assessment, a baseline crude protein reduction of 2 percentage points (from 16% in the NP group to 14% in the LP group) was engineered on a constant net energy plane of 2.063 Mcal/kg by integrating corn germ meal (11.000%), rapeseed meal (8.000%), and cottonseed meal (3.000%) with targeted crystalline amino acid supplementation. Across the 25-day feeding trial spanning 61 to 85 days of age, medium-growing female Mahuang broilers demonstrated remarkable physiological buffering capacity.

Overall growth metrics indicated that the reduction of dietary protein did not compromise systemic deposition. The LP cohort achieved an average daily gain of 35.43 g and an average daily feed intake of 167.97 g, resulting in a feed-to-gain ratio of 4.75, which was statistically indistinguishable from the NP baseline (average daily gain 33.09 g, feed intake 163.29 g, feed-to-gain ratio 4.94). Carcass yields confirmed that commercial carcass grading parameters remained unaffected by the dietary modifications.

- Net energy formulation maintained dietary energy density at 2.063 Mcal/kg across all nine experimental treatments.

- Dressing percentage (90.65% in NP vs 90.82% in LP) and abdominal fat percentage (6.26% in NP vs 6.41% in LP) exhibited zero negative divergence.

- Only methionine deficiency induced an adverse trend in feed utilization efficiency (P=0.080).

## Intestinal Mucosal Architecture and Antioxidant Responses

Intestinal mucosal morphology serves as a primary determinant of systemic nutrient absorption and functional gut integrity. Under standard balanced low-protein feeding, the LP cohort showed a notable trend toward enhanced jejunal villus height to crypt depth ratio (9.13 vs 7.67 in NP, P=0.075), alongside an elevation in serum albumin (15.62 g/L vs 13.69 g/L in NP, P=0.077). This structural improvement was critically undermined when specific essential amino acids were withdrawn from the basal low-protein ration.

Specific amino acid deletions exposed divergent physiological vulnerabilities. Removal of threonine, methionine, isoleucine, valine, or arginine resulted in significant reductions in the jejunal villus height to crypt depth ratio (P<0.05), with threonine deficiency depressing this structural index to 7.51. In parallel, systemic redox markers exhibited adaptive compensations: serum total antioxidant capacity and glutathione peroxidase activities were significantly stimulated under threonine, isoleucine, valine, and arginine deficiencies, reflecting an active metabolic compensation to sub-optimal amino acid balances.

- Villus height to crypt depth ratio decreased from 9.13 in LP controls to 7.51 in LP-Thr, 8.15 in LP-Met, and 8.30 in LP-Ile.

- Serum glutathione peroxidase activity increased significantly from 75.07 U/mL in LP to 123.30 U/mL in LP-Thr and 126.93 U/mL in LP-Val.

- Serum immunoglobulin A was depressed under threonine deficiency (18.53 ug/mL) and isoleucine deficiency (28.50 ug/mL) relative to LP controls (69.25 ug/mL).

## Divergent Multi-Criteria Limiting Amino Acid Hierarchies

Employing the classical partial amino acid deletion approach demonstrated that the limiting sequence of essential amino acids in poultry nutrition cannot be described by a single static ranking. Because physiological compartments exhibit distinct operational dependencies on specific amino acid substrates, the calculated limiting hierarchies bifurcated sharply across productive, morphological, and immunological performance criteria.

When optimizing feed conversion efficiency, the requirement sequence resolved as Met>Lys>Val>Ile>Arg>Thr>Trp, confirming methionine as the rate-limiting driver of systemic energetic efficiency. In sharp contrast, maintaining jejunal epithelial architecture elevated threonine and arginine above methionine (Thr>Arg>Met>Val>Ile>Trp>Lys), reflecting the heavy mucosal demand for threonine in mucin synthesis. analysis_markdown_en:
A decadal macro-ecological field survey conducted across the Huang-Huai-Hai winter wheat zone compared weed communities between 2013 and 2023 across thousands of field plots. The investigation tracked five key grass weed species: Aegilops tauschii, Bromus japonicus, Lolium multiflorum, Alopecurus myosuroides, and Avena fatua. Findings document a marked expansion of Aegilops tauschii and Bromus japonicus into ubiquitous regional threats, while Lolium multiflorum and Alopecurus myosuroides evolved from localized occurrences into coalescing regional belts. Driven by conservation shallow tillage, cross-regional combine harvesting, and persistent herbicide selection pressure, the results define critical intervention points for region-specific weed management.

## Regional Weed Community Shifts and Relative Abundance Dynamics

Systematic field inventories executed in 2013 and 2023 quantified dramatic decadal shifts within winter wheat agroecosystems across the Huang-Huai-Hai plain. In 2013, the grass weed community was predominantly anchored by a dual-dominant pattern consisting of Bromus japonicus (8.30%) and Aegilops tauschii (7.18%), which collectively accounted for more than 15% of regional relative abundance. Avena fatua occupied third position at 2.51%, while invasive grass taxa including Lolium multiflorum and Alopecurus myosuroides remained minor elements below 2.5%.

By 2023, the agroecological landscape evolved into a multi-dominant infestation regime. Aegilops tauschii advanced to primary regional dominance at 11.66%, recording increases between 0.02% and 8.72% across seven administrative divisions. Concurrently, Bromus japonicus expanded to 11.22%, exhibiting increases spanning 0.43% to 10.44%. Lolium multiflorum underwent aggressive proliferation, elevating regional relative abundance to 2.88% and displacing Avena fatua as the third most prevalent species.

- Aegilops tauschii emerged as the dominant weed species across Anhui, Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, and Shaanxi.

- Bromus japonicus retained primary dominance in Hebei, Tianjin, and Jiangsu.

- Lolium multiflorum showed prominent rank advancements in Henan, Shaanxi, Hebei, and Shanxi.

## Spatiotemporal Trajectories and Geographical Gradient Correlations

Spatial dispersion patterns revealed substantial geographic migration of weed populations. Aegilops tauschii and Bromus japonicus migrated from historical strongholds in western and northern sectors toward eastern and southern agricultural basins, establishing stable communities in previously uninfested zones including Huaibei in Anhui and Jiangsu, as well as Tianjin. Lolium multiflorum transformed rapidly from isolated points into an extensive belt concentrated in southern territories while dispersing regionally, establishing dense zones across central-southern Henan, northern Anhui, northern Jiangsu, and the Guanzhong Plain.

Geographical coordinate correlation models highlighted evolving ecological vectors. In 2013, Aegilops tauschii abundance correlated negatively with longitude, whereas by 2023 it established a significant positive correlation with latitude, reflecting a transitioned north-south gradient. Bromus japonicus demonstrated highly significant positive correlations with latitude in both surveys and developed a significant positive correlation with longitude in 2023. In contrast, Lolium multiflorum and Avena fatua exhibited negative correlations with both latitude and longitude.

- Alopecurus myosuroides evolved from isolated points into continuous patches across the Guanzhong Plain and central-southern Hebei.

- Avena fatua retreated from northern regions, demonstrating a southward contraction pattern.

## Agronomic Drivers and Integrated Weed Management Protocols

The accelerating succession of pernicious grass weeds is closely coupled with shifts in cultivation practices and chemical selection pressure. The widespread adoption of conservation tillage, reduced tillage, and straw retention maintains moisture in upper soil layers while leaving seeds within the 10 cm germination zone. Concurrently, long-term reliance on single-site herbicides such as fenoxaprop-P-ethyl and mesosulfuron-methyl has selected for resistant biotypes across multiple modes of action, while cross-regional combine harvester operations facilitate long-distance dispersal.

Mitigating these infestations requires structural agronomic interventions. Recommendations include rotational deep plowing to bury weed seeds below germination thresholds, systematic rotation of herbicide mechanisms incorporating pre-emergence soil-applied residuals alongside post-emergence treatments, and stringent sanitation protocols for custom-harvest machinery operating across provincial boundaries.

- Rotational deep tillage disrupts shallow seed banks accumulated under continuous no-till practices.

- Diversifying chemical targets limits cross-resistance development against ACCase and ALS inhibitors.

- Machine cleaning mandates reduce seed vectoring along national combine harvesting routes.

## Methodological Constraints and Ecological Boundaries

While the survey provides extensive macro-level coverage across two distinct decadal time points, several sampling and temporal constraints influence resolution.

- Field investigations were conducted specifically at the winter wheat tillering stage in November and December, potentially underrepresenting late-emerging cohorts.

- Certain prefectural jurisdictions had restricted sample point coverage, which may contribute to localized overestimation of specific weed abundances.

- The ten-year survey interval cannot capture annual community perturbations induced by extreme seasonal weather anomalies or transient herbicide adoption trends.

## Comparative Gas Kinetics and Hydrogen Sink Dynamics

Enteric fermentation in ruminants relies on an intricate syntrophic microbial consortium wherein primary fermenters hydrolyze structural polysaccharides into volatile fatty acids, carbon dioxide, and molecular hydrogen. Methanogenic archaea subsequently utilize carbon dioxide and free hydrogen to generate methane via the hydrogenotrophic reduction pathway mediated by methyl-coenzyme M reductase. In this in vitro evaluation, supplementation of 2 mmol·L-1 garlic organosulfides yielded starkly divergent gas emission profiles correlated with the sulfur chain density of each molecule.

While alliin (C6H11NO3S) generated gas kinetics virtually indistinguishable from the control (30.69 mL total gas and 2.11 mL CH4), allicin (C6H10OS2) and DATS (C6H10S3) exerted potent antimethanogenic effects. Total gas volume dropped to 23.66 mL in the allicin group and 18.48 mL in the DATS group. Methane generation was curtailed by more than 86% under allicin (0.30 mL) and by over 99% under DATS (0.02 mL). Because methanogenesis serves as the primary electron sink in the rumen, its interruption caused dissolved dihydrogen accumulation, surging from 0.03 mL in the control to 0.48 mL for allicin and 0.31 mL for DATS.

- Batch in vitro systems lack continuous ruminal clearance, endogenous buffering, and microbial adaptation mechanisms, requiring in vivo feeding trials to assess persistent efficacy and avoid ruminal dysbiosis.

Enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP) provides eco-friendly biocementation, yet brittle matrix cracking often limits its erosion resistance under overland scouring. In this study, natural palm fibers (0.1% mass ratio) were integrated into EICP-treated purple soil subjected to four cementation solution concentrations (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 mol/L) across six curing durations (1, 7, 15, 30, 60, and 120 d). This investigation examines the synergistic reinforcement of enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP) and natural palm fibers in suppressing the soil detachment capacity of loose purple soil from the Three Gorges Reservoir Area. Utilizing custom flume scouring experiments across variable cementation solution concentrations (0.5 to 2.0 mol/L) and curing durations (1 to 120 d), the findings demonstrate that adding 0.1% palm fiber enhances apparent cohesion by an additional 16.50% and calcium carbonate deposition by 16.01%, driving a further 25.81% reduction in soil detachment capacity beyond pure EICP bio-cementation. The experimental soil was sampled from Zigui County within the Three Gorges Reservoir Area (30°38'N to 31°11'N, 110°18'E to 111°0'E). Mechanical characterization classified the substrate as cohesive purple soil consisting of 45.06% sand (2.00 to 0.05 mm), 38.44% silt (0.05 to 0.002 mm), and 16.50% clay (<0.002 mm), with a dry density of 1.30 g/cm3, initial moisture content of 4.78%, liquid limit of 33.70%, plastic limit of 19.70%, plasticity index of 14.00, pH of 6.73, and organic matter content of 7.15 g/kg. ## Microstructural Reinforcement Architecture and Non-Linear Regression Mechanics

Scanning electron microscopy revealed that untreated purple soil exhibits large interparticle macropores and weak cohesion bridges. In pure fiber treatments, the flexible filaments bridge inter-aggregate voids but maintain minimal chemical interfacial bonding. In unreinforced EICP systems, rhombohedral calcite precipitates aggregate into isolated clusters or spot-welded contact bridges between soil grains, leaving unbonded shear planes vulnerable to brittle hydraulic fracture.

In contrast, the combined fiber-EICP matrix exhibits dense calcite crystal agglomerations directly nucleated and anchored along the porous outer walls of the palm fibers. The hydrophilic surface of the vegetable fiber concentrates aqueous calcium and carbonate ions, forming a continuous soil-fiber-calcium carbonate composite skeleton. Non-linear fitting established that soil detachment capacity follows an exponential decay relative to apparent cohesion (y = 31.43e^-0.44x, R2 = 0.85, P < 0.01) and calcium carbonate mass content (y = 15.56e^-0.96x, R2 = 0.91, P < 0.01), demonstrating that bio-mineralized crystal mass functions as the governing physical barrier to hydrodynamic detachment.

## Operational Boundary Conditions and Agronomic Constraints

While palm fiber inclusion significantly enhances bio-cementation and mitigates matrix brittleness, several operational boundary factors govern real-world slope installations.

- Enzyme-induced hydrolysis is suppressed at cementation solution concentrations exceeding 1.5 mol/L due to osmotic and ionic inhibition of soybean urease activity.

- The empirical trials were constrained to a single 0.1% fiber mass dosage and a simulated hydraulic shear stress of 12.08 Pa on a 38.39% flume gradient.

- Although reducing cementation concentration to 0.5 mol/L with fiber limits chemical salt toxicity toward revegetation, prolonged biochemical decay of natural plant fibers under field weathering remains unquantified.

Purple soil within the Three Gorges Reservoir Area exhibits high susceptibility to hydraulic erosion due to loose grain aggregation, low shear resistance, and rapid structural disintegration on steep gradients. Enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP) provides eco-friendly biocementation, yet brittle matrix cracking often limits its erosion resistance under overland scouring. In this study, natural palm fibers (0.1% mass ratio) were integrated into EICP-treated purple soil subjected to four cementation solution concentrations (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 mol/L) across six curing durations (1, 7, 15, 30, 60, and 120 d). Simulated runoff flume trials at a 38.39% slope and 45 L/min discharge (hydraulic shear stress of 12.08 Pa) revealed that EICP alone reduced average soil detachment capacity by 58.63% relative to unamended control soil, whereas palm fiber incorporation achieved a further 25.81% reduction. Concurrently, fiber inclusion increased average apparent cohesion and calcium carbonate precipitation by 16.50% and 16.01%, respectively. Optimal anti-erosion performance occurred at 1.5 mol/L cementation after 7 d curing. Microstructural scanning electron microscopy confirmed that palm fibers provide multi-point nucleation sites that anchor dispersed calcite crystals into a cohesive soil-fiber-calcium carbonate spatial lattice, allowing lower cementation concentrations to achieve superior slope-stabilization benchmarks.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Relative to unamended purple soil (CK), standard EICP reduces soil detachment capacity by an average of 58.63%, and adding 0.1% palm fiber delivers an additional 25.81% reduction.
- Palm fiber integration elevates apparent cohesion by an average of 16.50% and increases precipitated calcium carbonate content by 16.01% across curing regimes.
- The 0.1% palm fiber composite paired with 0.5 mol/L cementation solution yields an erosion reduction equivalent to pure 1.5 mol/L EICP (62.30% versus 64.31% average reduction).
- Soil detachment capacity exhibits highly significant negative exponential relationships with both apparent cohesion (R2=0.85, P<0.01) and calcium carbonate content (R2=0.91, P<0.01).
- Scanning electron microscopy reveals that palm fiber filaments serve as crystal nucleation templates, interlocking soil grains and calcite aggregates into a cohesive three-dimensional network.

analysis_markdown_en:
This study resolves the complex fungal etiology of destructive valsa canker afflicting endangered wild apple (Malus sieversii) populations in the Tianshan mountain forests of Xinjiang. From 217 diseased branch samples collected across Xinyuan County natural stands and germplasm repositories, researchers isolated 419 fungal strains spanning six Cytospora species verified through morphological taxonomy and multi-locus phylogeny (ITS, ACT, TEF, TUB). Cytospora parasitica proved dominant with a 63.87% isolation frequency, while Cytospora ambiens and Cytospora hoffmannii were identified as novel canker pathogens on M. sieversii. In vitro profiling defined optimal vegetative growth parameters across culture media, temperature gradients, pH, nutrient sources, and photoperiod regimes.

## Multilocus Phylogenetic Delineation and Morphological Identification of Cytospora Pathogens

Field surveys across natural wild apple forests and ex situ germplasm repositories in Xinyuan County revealed severe shoot dieback symptoms, primarily localized to 1-2 year-old twigs under 1 cm diameter. Diseased cortical tissues initially developed moist, reddish-brown swollen lesions that rapidly desiccated, contracted, and formed sunken necrotic patches filled with black stromata. From 217 sampled branches, 419 isolates belonging to the genus Cytospora were purified and categorized into six morphological groups based on stromatic locule architecture, conidial dimensions, and colony pigmentation.

Genomic validation utilizing multi-gene sequence alignment encompassing internal transcribed spacer (ITS, ~600 bp), translation elongation factor 1-alpha (TEF, ~280 bp), actin (ACT, ~250 bp), and beta-tubulin (TUB, ~520 bp) resolved species boundaries using Diaporthe vaccinii (CBS 160.32) as an outgroup. Neighbor-joining phylogenetic inference placed representative strains F02, F04, F06, F07, F10, and F12 into monophyletic clades corresponding to Cytospora parasitica (268 isolates, 63.87%), C. mali (97 isolates, 23.10%), C. ambiens (24 isolates, 5.71%), C. leucostoma (13 isolates, 3.09%), C. hoffmannii (11 isolates, 2.62%), and C. pruinopsis (6 isolates, 1.43%), each supported by bootstrap values above 95%.

## Koch Postulate Inoculation Dynamics and Necrotic Lesion Progression in Excised Shoots

Pathogenicity validation performed on scalded 15 cm healthy excised dormant twigs verified Koch's postulates for all six representative strains. Initial oval, reddish-brown sunken necrotic lesions appeared 5-7 d post-inoculation. Within 10 d, lesion expansion girdled infected twigs, softening and rotting the phloem while creating sharp margins between healthy and diseased tissues.

By 20 d post-inoculation, black pycnidia erupted through the periderm, discharging coiled yellowish gelatinous spore horns (cirri). Re-isolation from lesion margins confirmed 100% concordance with original inocula, whereas wounded paraffin-sealed controls remained symptomless, verifying the primary pathogenicity of all six Cytospora taxa on M. sieversii woody tissue.

## Thermotolerance Profiles and Mycelial Growth Responses to Culture Media and pH

Vegetative growth profiling demonstrated distinct environmental niches among the six Cytospora taxa. Tested on five culture substrates, potato dextrose agar (PDA) supported optimal mycelial expansion across all six species, while potato sucrose agar (PSA) and potato malt agar (PMA) sustained comparable growth for C. mali and C. hoffmannii. Synthetic Czapek agar consistently yielded minimal colony development, ranging from 7.24 mm in C. leucostoma to 25.05 mm in C. ambiens.

Thermal gradient screening revealed broad vegetative viability from 5 to 40 deg C, but maximum radial expansion was strictly centered at 25-28 deg C, with C. mali peaking at 28 deg C (83.83 mm) and C. ambiens, C. leucostoma, C. parasitica, and C. pruinopsis peaking at 25 deg C. Hydrogen ion tolerance assays indicated that all strains grew between pH 4.0 and 11.0, with optimal radial expansion concentrated between pH 6.0 and 8.0.

## Nutritional Carbon and Nitrogen Assimilation and Photoperiodic Sensitivity

Nutritional assays using modified Czapek media revealed divergent metabolic capacities across Cytospora species. All strains produced significantly larger colony diameters on carbohydrate-amended media relative to carbon-free controls. Glucose functioned as the optimal carbon source for C. mali (16.77 mm), C. hoffmannii (30.31 mm), C. ambiens (38.88 mm), C. leucostoma (29.76 mm), and C. parasitica (17.16 mm), whereas C. pruinopsis exhibited superior utilization of sucrose (37.79 mm).

Nitrogen assimilation assays indicated that L-asparagine served as the preferred nitrogen substrate for C. mali (24.40 mm), C. parasitica (26.90 mm), and C. pruinopsis (21.40 mm), while C. ambiens preferred glycine (37.00 mm) and C. leucostoma utilized ammonium sulfate most effectively (9.95 mm). Photoperiod sensitivity varied markedly: continuous 24 h illumination stimulated C. mali and C. ambiens, alternating 12 h light/dark cycles favored C. pruinopsis, and total darkness maximized growth in dominant C. parasitica (47.97 mm).

## Methodological Constraints and Ecological Generalizability Boundaries

This study evaluated 419 fungal isolates sourced exclusively from wild stands and an ex situ repository in Xinyuan County, Ili Prefecture, potentially underrepresenting Cytospora diversity across broader Central Asian wild fruit forest ranges. Pathogenicity assays were conducted on detached dormant twigs rather than living mature trees, and microclimate evaluations were confined to controlled in vitro agar models.

- Pathogen sampling was geographically restricted to Xinyuan County (217 diseased branches), omitting wild apple populations distributed across the broader Ili River Valley and Tacheng regions.

- Inoculation assays utilized detached branch scald wounding, which cannot replicate multi-year systemic tree defense responses, resin barriers, or field-scale microclimatic fluctuations.

- In vitro agar colony assays do not fully capture host bark chemical inhibitors, xylem nutrient availability, or the composite damage inflicted alongside wood-boring pests like Agrilus mali.

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

abstract_en: Vegetable production is frequently associated with high nitrogen fertilizer application and intensive crop rotation, resulting in soil acidification, structural degradation, and proliferation of harmful microorganisms. This study investigated the short-term effects of organic fertilizer, potassium humate, calcium carbonate, and their combinations on soil properties, organic carbon components, and microbial community structure in acidic vegetable fields with an untreated control (CK). Results showed that the sole application of full-dose organic fertilizer significantly increased total nitrogen, available phosphorus, and available potassium in non-rhizosphere soil, while significantly increasing easily oxidizable organic carbon (EOC) in non-rhizosphere (by 22.70%) and rhizosphere (by 9.76%) soils. Sole application of full-dose calcium carbonate significantly raised soil pH but reduced available phosphorus in non-rhizosphere soil and alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen, available potassium, and organic carbon (SOC) in rhizosphere soil. Most notably, the combined application of all three amendments significantly increased soil pH and Chinese cabbage yield compared to CK, while also increasing SOC, EOC, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and the abundance of soil bacteria, fungi, Gram-positive bacteria, Gram-negative bacteria, and actinomycetes. Redundancy analysis indicated that non-rhizosphere microbial communities were primarily driven by alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen, whereas available potassium and DOC governed rhizosphere communities. Structural equation modeling revealed that exchangeable Ca2+, available phosphorus, and alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen exerted significant positive effects on cabbage yield, demonstrating that co-application balances acidity remediation with nutrient retention.
