abstract_en: This experiment investigated the effects of dietary supplementation with biochanin A on lactation performance, serum biochemical indexes, nutrient apparent digestibility, and nitrogen utilization in heat-stressed Holstein dairy cows. A cohort of 300 healthy cows with comparable parity (2 to 3 parities), initial milk yield (34.05±5.40 kg/d), and days in milk (175.02±34.91 d) was randomly divided into three groups of 100 cows each. Animals were fed a total mixed ration supplemented with 0 (control), 2 (low-dose), or 10 g/d (high-dose) biochanin A over a 35-day period, comprising 7 days of adaptation and 28 days of experimental feeding. Throughout the study, the cowshed average daily temperature-humidity index remained above 68, with baseline respiratory rates surpassing 60 breaths/min. Compared with the control group, cows receiving 10 g/d exhibited significantly reduced respiratory rate on day 28 (79.08 vs. 84.92 breaths/min) and lower serum heat shock proteins HSP-27 and HSP-70 (P<0.05). High-dose supplementation significantly improved daily milk yield (37.57 vs. 34.93 kg/d), feed conversion efficiency (1.71 vs. 1.60), and milk protein yield (1018.55 vs. 899.89 g/d). It also increased apparent digestibility of crude protein (68.07% vs. 64.00%) and neutral detergent fiber (51.60% vs. 45.42%). Furthermore, high-dose biochanin A reduced ruminal ammonia nitrogen (7.92 vs. 11.24 mg/dL) and urease activity (111.32 vs. 155.61 U/mL), lowering urinary urea nitrogen while increasing the nitrogen conversion rate (25.86% vs. 22.45%). Overall, 10 g/d biochanin A mitigates thermal distress and enhances production efficiency.

## Thermal Strain Mitigation and Physiological Resilience

During warm summer seasons, high ambient temperatures coupled with elevated relative humidity impose severe environmental stress on lactating ruminants. In this investigation, environmental monitors within the barn recorded a daily average temperature-humidity index exceeding 68 throughout the entire trial period. Under these conditions, baseline respiratory rates exceeded 60 breaths/min across all experimental cohorts, confirming persistent physiological heat stress.

Dietary intervention with purified biochanin A exhibited clear mitigating actions against heat-induced systemic strain. By day 28 of the experimental period, dairy cows receiving the 10 g/d dosage demonstrated a significant reduction in respiratory frequency compared to unsupplemented controls. Furthermore, both low-dose and high-dose regimens attenuated cellular stress markers, producing significant reductions in serum concentrations of heat shock protein-27 and heat shock protein-70. Serum beta-hydroxybutyric acid, a classic diagnostic indicator of negative energy balance and metabolic strain, was also significantly decreased in both supplemented cohorts.

- Average cowshed temperature-humidity index remained above 68 during the 35-day experimental trial.

- Day 28 respiratory rate decreased significantly in the high-dose group compared to the control group.

- Circulating levels of heat shock protein-27 and heat shock protein-70 dropped markedly following isoflavone supplementation.

Thermal stress severely impairs dairy cow welfare, feed utilization, and milk production. This controlled trial evaluated dietary biochanin A, a purified legume isoflavone, in 300 heat-stressed lactating Holstein dairy cows maintained at daily average temperature-humidity index levels exceeding 68. Supplementation with 10 g/d biochanin A significantly alleviated physiological heat stress indicators, lowered respiratory rates, and decreased serum heat shock proteins. In addition, high-dose biochanin A elevated milk production, enhanced crude protein and neutral detergent fiber digestibility, suppressed ruminal urease activity and ammonia nitrogen accumulation, and redirected dietary nitrogen toward milk protein synthesis while decreasing urinary urea nitrogen excretion.

## Lactation Performance and Digestive Efficiency Dynamics

Elevated ambient heat typically suppresses feed intake, compromises ruminal function, and lowers total milk volume. In this study, dry matter intake remained statistically indistinguishable across groups (ranging between 21.70 kg/d and 21.93 kg/d), demonstrating that the observed productive gains did not arise from differential bulk ration consumption. Instead, biochanin A at 10 g/d stimulated significant improvements in overall feed conversion efficiency, driving daily milk yield from 34.93 kg/d to 37.57 kg/d.

This productive enhancement was underpinned by targeted improvements in gastrointestinal nutrient extraction. Measurement of nutrient apparent digestibility revealed that the 10 g/d cohort achieved significantly greater digestibility coefficients for crude protein and neutral detergent fiber. Enhanced fiber breakdown supplied more fermentable energy substrates to support lactation, while improved protein absorption provided adequate circulating precursors for mammary gland milk protein synthesis.

- Milk protein daily output increased from 899.89 g/d in controls to 1018.55 g/d in high-dose cows.

## Ruminal Fermentation Modulation and Nitrogen Partitioning

Ruminant nitrogen balance is dictated by the equilibrium between ruminal microbial proteolysis and hepatic urea recycling. Excessive ruminal microbial urease activity accelerates dietary protein degradation into free ammonia, often surpassing microbial capture capacity and resulting in surplus urea synthesis and urinary nitrogen excretion. In this trial, biochanin A exerted targeted inhibition against ruminal ureolytic activity, reducing ruminal urease from 155.61 U/mL down to 111.32 U/mL in the high-dose group.

As a consequence of suppressed ruminal ureolysis, ruminal ammonia nitrogen levels fell significantly from 11.24 mg/dL to 7.92 mg/dL. This regulated proteolytic environment prevented excessive nitrogen loss into the vascular circulation. Cows supplemented with 10 g/d biochanin A exhibited reduced serum urea and urinary urea nitrogen concentrations, while milk nitrogen yield and overall nitrogen conversion rate increased significantly, documenting an efficient metabolic shift from waste excretion toward milk protein assembly.

- Ruminal urease activity was suppressed by both 2 g/d and 10 g/d supplementation regimens.

- Ruminal ammonia nitrogen concentrations were reduced without compromising total dry matter digestion.

- Whole-body nitrogen conversion rate improved from 22.45% to 25.86%, accompanied by lowered urinary excretion.

## Experimental Boundaries and Production Constraints

This study tested purified biochanin A in mid-lactation Holstein cows under continuous regional heat stress conditions. Practical deployment should consider specific production stages, basal ration composition, and isoflavone delivery forms.

- The experimental duration was restricted to 35 days (7 days adaptation and 28 days feeding), leaving long-term metabolic adaptations across entire lactation cycles uncharacterized.

- The trial evaluated multiparous cows (parities 2 to 3) averaging 175.02±34.91 days in milk; responsiveness in primiparous heifers or transition cows remains to be established.

- Dosing was fixed at 2 g/d and 10 g/d without exploring intermediary titration ranges between 2 g/d and 10 g/d to define the minimal effective threshold.

- Cost and sourcing constraints of highly purified biochanin A versus crude red clover extracts were not addressed within the scope of this feeding trial.

# Effects of Biochanin A on Lactation Performance, Serum Biochemical Indexes, Nutrient Apparent Digestibility and Nitrogen Utilization of Heat-Stressed Dairy Cows

---

**DOI:** `10.12418/CJAN2026.218` | **Journal:** Chinese Journal of Animal Nutrition (动物营养学报) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** TUO Yong, LIU Xiaojun, WANG Xihu, WANG Jun, ZHAO Shengguo, AMAT Guzalnur  
**Affiliation:** Feed Research Institute, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Academy of Animal Husbandry Sciences

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

This experiment investigated the effects of dietary supplementation with biochanin A on lactation performance, serum biochemical indexes, nutrient apparent digestibility, and nitrogen utilization in heat-stressed Holstein dairy cows. A cohort of 300 healthy cows with comparable parity (2 to 3 parities), initial milk yield (34.05±5.40 kg/d), and days in milk (175.02±34.91 d) was randomly divided into three groups of 100 cows each. Animals were fed a total mixed ration supplemented with 0 (control), 2 (low-dose), or 10 g/d (high-dose) biochanin A over a 35-day period, comprising 7 days of adaptation and 28 days of experimental feeding. Throughout the study, the cowshed average daily temperature-humidity index remained above 68, with baseline respiratory rates surpassing 60 breaths/min. Compared with the control group, cows receiving 10 g/d exhibited significantly reduced respiratory rate on day 28 (79.08 vs. 84.92 breaths/min) and lower serum heat shock proteins HSP-27 and HSP-70 (P<0.05). High-dose supplementation significantly improved daily milk yield (37.57 vs. 34.93 kg/d), feed conversion efficiency (1.71 vs. 1.60), and milk protein yield (1018.55 vs. 899.89 g/d). It also increased apparent digestibility of crude protein (68.07% vs. 64.00%) and neutral detergent fiber (51.60% vs. 45.42%). Furthermore, high-dose biochanin A reduced ruminal ammonia nitrogen (7.92 vs. 11.24 mg/dL) and urease activity (111.32 vs. 155.61 U/mL), lowering urinary urea nitrogen while increasing the nitrogen conversion rate (25.86% vs. 22.45%). Overall, 10 g/d biochanin A mitigates thermal distress and enhances production efficiency.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- High-dose biochanin A at 10 g/d increased daily milk yield from 34.93 kg/d to 37.57 kg/d and feed conversion efficiency from 1.60 to 1.71 (P<0.05).
- Supplementation with 10 g/d enhanced apparent digestibility of crude protein from 64.00% to 68.07% and neutral detergent fiber from 45.42% to 51.60% (P<0.05).
- Both low-dose (2 g/d) and high-dose (10 g/d) biochanin A significantly reduced ruminal urease activity from 155.61 U/mL in controls to 120.54 U/mL and 111.32 U/mL, respectively.
- Thermal stress strain was mitigated as day 28 respiratory rate dropped from 84.92 breaths/min in controls to 79.08 breaths/min in the 10 g/d cohort.
- Nitrogen conversion rate improved from 22.45% to 25.86%, coupled with a decline in urinary urea nitrogen from 530.63 mg/dL to 467.01 mg/dL.

### Abstract

This study systematically analyzed the diagnostic horizons and diagnostic characteristics of soils developed from paleo-red clay in Hebei Province to clarify their taxonomic classification and supplement the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (CST). Based on the Third National Soil Census, seven representative soil profiles were selected at the junction of low hills and piedmont plains in the Yanshan and Taihang Mountains. Strictly following CST criteria, the profiles were classified and basic taxonomic units established. The seven profiles exhibited mollic epipedon, ochric epipedon, cambic horizon, argic horizon, and calcic horizon, belonging to three soil orders: Isohumosols, Cambosols, and Argosols. Combined with soil moisture and temperature regimes, they were divided into five suborders: Ustic Isohumosols, Ustic Argosols, Boric Argosols, Udic Argosols, and Ustic Cambosols. Based on diagnostic indices including calcic horizon, surface epipedons, claypan, lithological characteristics of northern red earths, calcaric property, and pH, five soil groups and five subgroups were identified: Calci-Ustic Isohumosols, Hapli-Ustic Argosols, Molli-Boric Argosols, Claypani-Udic Argosols, and Hapli-Ustic Cambosols. Seven soil families were classified by particle size, mineralogical type, acid-base properties, and thermal regime. Comparison with existing soil series, particularly in soil body configuration, red clay layer position, and thickness, led to the establishment of seven new soil series including Dasipeng and Wujiadian. This systematic investigation fills the gap in soil series surveys for paleo-red clay-derived soils in Hebei Province.

## Diagnostic Horizons and Characteristics of Paleo-red Clay-Derived Soils

Seven profiles from Yanshan and Taihang Mountain regions were described and sampled. Diagnostic horizons included mollic epipedon (LP10, 14 cm thick, organic carbon 12.18 g/kg, base saturation 83.24%), ochric epipedon (other profiles, moist value 4–7), cambic horizon (PQ02, ZH03, XH04, KB06, LP10 with weak weathering), argic horizon (PQ02 clay increase 12.70%, XT05 clay ratio 1.83, ZH09 clay ratio 1.24, LP10 clay increase 7.60%), calcic horizon (KB06, 30 cm thick, secondary carbonate 66.30 g/kg higher than parent material), and claypan (ZH09, >10 cm thick, blocky structure, high clay content cemented by Fe-Mn).

Diagnostic characteristics included calcaric property (XH04, XT05, KB06 with CaCO3 >10 g/kg in all sublayers to 50 cm), calcic feature (PQ02 bottom layer CaCO3 65.70 g/kg, 51.30 g/kg higher than overlying), isohumic property (KB06, humus storage ratio Rh 0.39), soil temperature regimes (cold for KB06 at >1400 m, XH04 and LP10 at 800–1000 m; thermic for others), soil moisture regimes (stagnic for ZH09, ustic for others), and northern red earth lithological characteristics (all profiles with 2.5YR or 5YR hues in whole or lower part).

## Taxonomic Classification and Soil Series Establishment

Based on CST, the seven profiles were classified into three orders: Isohumosols (KB06), Argosols (PQ02, ZH03, XH04, ZH09), and Cambosols (XT05, LP10). Suborders were Ustic Isohumosols, Ustic Argosols, Boric Argosols, Udic Argosols, and Ustic Cambosols. Soil groups included Calci-Ustic Isohumosols, Hapli-Ustic Argosols, Molli-Boric Argosols, Claypani-Udic Argosols, and Hapli-Ustic Cambosols, with corresponding subgroups. Seven soil families were defined by particle size (clayey, loamy, sandy), mineralogical type (siliceous mixed), acid-base reaction (calcaric, non-calcaric), and temperature regime (thermic, cold).

Seven new soil series were established: Dasipeng (KB06), Wujiadian (PQ02), Habaqin (LP10), Jinzhongsi (ZH03), and others. These series differ from existing ones in soil body configuration, red clay layer position, and thickness. For example, KB06 has a sandy loam surface overlying loamy clay with abundant carbonate nodules, while ZH09 has a claypan with Fe-Mn mottles. The study recommends adding a "northern red earth lithological characteristic" criterion to CST to better reflect these soils' unique properties, proposing new soil groups such as Red Ustic Cambosols and Red Ustic Argosols.

- The study is limited to seven profiles in Hebei Province; broader validation across other regions with paleo-red clay is needed.

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

This study systematically analyzed the diagnostic horizons and diagnostic characteristics of soils developed from paleo-red clay in Hebei Province to clarify their taxonomic classification and supplement the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (CST). Based on the Third National Soil Census, seven representative soil profiles were selected at the junction of low hills and piedmont plains in the Yanshan and Taihang Mountains. Strictly following CST criteria, the profiles were classified and basic taxonomic units established. The seven profiles exhibited mollic epipedon, ochric epipedon, cambic horizon, argic horizon, and calcic horizon, belonging to three soil orders: Isohumosols, Cambosols, and Argosols. Combined with soil moisture and temperature regimes, they were divided into five suborders: Ustic Isohumosols, Ustic Argosols, Boric Argosols, Udic Argosols, and Ustic Cambosols. Based on diagnostic indices including calcic horizon, surface epipedons, claypan, lithological characteristics of northern red earths, calcaric property, and pH, five soil groups and five subgroups were identified: Calci-Ustic Isohumosols, Hapli-Ustic Argosols, Molli-Boric Argosols, Claypani-Udic Argosols, and Hapli-Ustic Cambosols. Seven soil families were classified by particle size, mineralogical type, acid-base properties, and thermal regime. Comparison with existing soil series, particularly in soil body configuration, red clay layer position, and thickness, led to the establishment of seven new soil series including Dasipeng and Wujiadian. This systematic investigation fills the gap in soil series surveys for paleo-red clay-derived soils in Hebei Province.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Seven profiles were classified into 3 orders, 5 suborders, 5 groups, 5 subgroups, and 7 soil families under CST.
- Clay content (<0.002 mm) ranged from 56 to 451 g/kg, with most between 150 and 400 g/kg; sand content 295-796 g/kg.
- pH ranged from 5.67 (LP10 subsoil) to 8.64 (PQ02 bottom layer); CaCO3 varied from 0 to 103 g/kg across profiles.
- Seven new soil series (e.g., Dasipeng, Wujiadian) were established, filling the gap in Hebei soil series for paleo-red clay parent materials.

## Thermal Profile Progression and Gaseous Emission Dynamics

All experimental treatments attained thermophilic conditions exceeding 70 deg C on Day 1, sustaining high-temperature phases above 50 deg C for 3 to 5 d. Peak temperature and thermal duration exhibited positive correlation with rapeseed cake loading rates due to the rapid metabolic utilization of readily available proteins, lipids, and polyphenols. Introducing rapeseed cake during subsequent cooling or maturation phases triggered secondary microbial activation and distinct temperature surges, protracting the stabilization process.

Gaseous stripping occurred predominantly during early thermophilic surges and secondary reheating windows. Late-stage introduction of rapeseed cake amplified NH3 discharge by 37.3% to 59.4% and H2S emission by 29.6% to 459.9% due to repeated high-temperature cycles and local anaerobic pocket development. Conversely, blending porous mature compost clinker at 10% and 20% reduced NH3 release by 24.5% to 80.0% and H2S by 7.9% to 55.8% via enhanced interstitial oxygen diffusion and physical-chemical surface sorption.

- Inoculation with composite microbial agents decreased H2S release by 14.8% to 26.4% across equivalent clinker ratios via sulfur-oxidizing enzymatic activities and competitive heterotrophic carbon utilization.

- Compost mixtures with 15% rapeseed cake sustained cumulative NH3 outputs that exceeded lower-dosage treatments by 27.5% to 461.2%.

Dairy manure management faces operational obstacles stemming from high moisture content, dense physical structure, deficient humification, and volatile nutrient stripping. This investigation deployed an L9(34) orthogonal composting trial utilizing 85% dairy manure and 15% straw as baseline feedstocks to examine the co-regulatory dynamics of rapeseed cake dosage, recycled mature compost inoculation, microbial agent proportion, and cake feeding timing. Findings show delayed rapeseed cake addition triggers multiple thermal peaks, inflating gaseous emissions. Incorporating mature compost suppresses ammonia and hydrogen sulfide while facilitating humic acid synthesis and nutrient conservation, pinpointing an optimal formulation balancing humic acid formation and plant safety.

Humic substance fractions demonstrated an initial decline during the opening 7 d as thermophilic heterotrophs catabolized labile carbon backbones, followed by progressive replenishment via polymerization of amino acids, quinones, and polyphenolic precursors. Late addition of organic amendments preserved total organic matter and humic substances; however, initial addition facilitated stable condensation pathways, avoiding phytotoxic intermediate accumulation.

Ultraviolet-visible spectral markers tracked molecular stabilization across reactor batches. SUVA254 and SUVA280 metrics declined initially before rising after Day 14, indexing the breakdown of non-humic aromatics followed by progressive macromolecular condensation. ## Nutrient Conservation Mechanics and Agronomic Maturity Evaluation

Total nutrient mass fraction across all treatments increased from initial ranges of 4.8% to 7.7% up to terminal values between 7.3% to 8.9%, comfortably exceeding commercial organic fertilizer compliance criteria. While volatile nitrogen experienced substantial early losses via ammonia volatilization, total nitrogen concentrated through overall organic dry matter reduction, finishing between 2.2% and 2.9%.

Phosphorus and potassium remained chemically stable, with P2O5 and K2O mass fractions displaying sustained upward trends. Mature clinker exerted a dominant influence on terminal potassium and phosphorus enrichment. Phyto-compatibility assessments highlighted critical timing dependencies: late cake additions severely depressed seed germination indices, whereas initial addition enabled microbial decomposition of short-chain volatile fatty acids, driving final GI values to 167.9% in the optimized treatment.

- Terminal electrical conductivity values stabilized between 1.4 and 3.1 mS/cm across all groups, falling safely below standard crop salinity thresholds.

- Treatment T5 containing 10% mature compost, 0.05% microbial inoculum, and 10% initial rapeseed cake achieved top-tier rankings in total nutrients, humic substance yield, and organic matter.

## Process Scale Boundaries and Raw Material Sensitivities

This study conducted bench-scale trials using 160 L cylindrical polyethylene batch reactors under forced aeration of 0.3 L/(min*kg). Extrapolation to commercial windrow or dynamic industrial channel composting requires accounting for thermal dissipation gradients, ambient weather shifts, and localized bulk density variations.

- Feedstock specifications require continuous monitoring of moisture and bulk density, as raw dairy manure exhibiting 83.8% initial moisture necessitates precise blending with bulking straw.

- Postponing secondary organic amendments to cooling or maturation phases should be avoided in commercial settings unless prolonged secondary stabilization curing stages are implemented to purge phytotoxic organic acids.

- The screening threshold of mature compost clinker (> 5 mm) requires dedicated sizing equipment to maintain the structural aeration benefits observed in bench trials.

This investigation establishes a standardized in vitro oxidative damage model in donkey mammary epithelial cells (DMECs) using diethylenetriamine/nitric oxide polymer (DETA/NO). Second-passage DMECs were challenged across various concentrations and incubation times. Exposure to 1000 μmol/L DETA/NO for 6 h reduced cell proliferation to 66.61%, fitting the 60% to 70% threshold required for stable cellular damage without causing extensive cell death. This exposure significantly suppressed antioxidant enzyme activities (CAT, GPx, and SOD), depleted total antioxidant capacity, and elevated reactive oxygen species, lipid peroxidation, and inflammatory factors through NF-kappaB activation and PPARgamma suppression.

## Optimization of Nitric Oxide Exposure Duration and Concentration

Mammary gland tissues in lactating equines undergo intensive metabolic turnover, creating vulnerability to excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species and reactive nitrogen intermediates. To simulate pathological nitric oxide overload in vitro, second-generation donkey mammary epithelial cells were subjected to seven graded concentrations of the slow-releasing nitric oxide donor DETA/NO across four time intervals. Systematic CCK-8 proliferation assays demonstrated that cell viability declined in a dose- and time-dependent manner.

A proliferation rate settling between 60% and 70% is recognized as the standard benchmark for sub-lethal oxidative damage in epithelial cells, preventing irreversible lytic death while providing sufficient stress to evaluate cytoprotective compounds. Following 6 h of treatment, cell proliferation rates for the 800 and 1000 μmol/L cohorts reached 69.48% and 66.61%, respectively. The 1200 μmol/L dosage reduced viability below optimal limits to 58.60%, while shorter exposure durations failed to induce uniform injury within the designated viability window.

- Proliferation after 2 h ranged from 89.67% at 200 μmol/L to 70.75% at 1200 μmol/L.

- Proliferation after 6 h dropped to 66.61% at 1000 μmol/L, remaining precisely within the targeted 60% to 70% range.

## Biochemical Perturbations in Antioxidant Defense and Redox Status

Assessment of enzymatic defenses following 6 h of DETA/NO challenge revealed marked depletion of free-radical scavenging capacity. ## In Vitro Protocol Boundaries and Translational Applicability

This cellular protocol accurately replicates sub-acute nitric oxide-induced oxidative damage in isolated donkey mammary epithelial cells. However, in vitro monolayer models lack the systemic physiological feedback, vascular perfusion, and complex hormonal interactions present in vivo.

- The experimental findings are derived from isolated F2 generation DMECs in monolayer culture, which cannot reproduce tissue-level architectural defense or systemic immune interactions.

- The 6 h challenge with 1000 μmol/L DETA/NO represents an acute chemical surge of nitric oxide donor, which may differ from the chronic, low-grade oxidative stress encountered during protracted dairy lactation in vivo.

- Quantitative model validation was specifically executed using primary cells derived from 5-year-old lactating jennies, requiring verification before extrapolation to other age groups or non-equid ruminant species.

## Export Scale Trajectory and Product Composition Dynamics

Hebei Province observed substantial expansion in vegetable export trade across the 2019-2024 observation period, driven by policy support and trade facilitation initiatives implemented jointly by provincial agricultural departments and customs authorities. Export value grew from 15.60 billion yuan in 2019 to 23.16 billion yuan in 2024, reflecting an average annual growth rate of 8.08%. The temporal trajectory exhibited a distinct U-shaped growth rate curve: annual growth decelerated to an average of 5.61% during the 2020-2022 period amidst external disruptions, before rebounding sharply to 12.25% in 2023 and 12.32% in 2024.

Significant structural adjustments characterized product category dynamics across four core Harmonized System classifications: fresh vegetables, frozen vegetables, simply processed vegetables, and pickled vegetables. Pickled vegetables demonstrated the most rapid progression, rising from 4.07 billion yuan in 2019 to 8.36 billion yuan in 2024, an overall increase of 105.41%. Simply processed vegetables peaked at 7.98 billion yuan in 2021 before recording 7.70 billion yuan in 2024, representing 33.25% of exports. Frozen vegetables reached 4.89 billion yuan (21.11%) in 2024, whereas fresh vegetable exports contracted from 2.47 billion yuan to 2.21 billion yuan (9.54%).

At the disaggregated HS tariff line level, market concentration among top items gradually diversified. The combined export share of the top four vegetable varieties decreased from 70.60% in 2019 to 63.96% in 2024. Shelled dried legumes (HS 0713) held the leading position from 2019 to 2022 before being surpassed by frozen vegetables (HS 0710) in 2023, with HS 0713 dropping to 3.19 billion yuan (13.79%) by 2024.

- Pickled vegetables emerged as the dominant export classification in 2023, expanding to 8.36 billion yuan in 2024.

- Frozen vegetables (HS 0710) expanded its share from 19.80% in 2019 to 21.11% in 2024.

- Dried vegetables (HS 0712) and preserved non-refrigerated vegetables (HS 2005) captured 16.17% and 12.89% respectively in 2024.

This study analyzes the longitudinal export dynamics of the vegetable sector in Hebei Province from 2019 through 2024 utilizing General Administration of Customs data. Provincial vegetable export value expanded from 15.60 billion yuan to 23.16 billion yuan, reflecting a cumulative increase of 48.46% and an average annual growth rate of 8.08%. The sector underwent significant structural shifts, transitioning from dried legumes toward pickled and frozen categories, while general trade maintained a dominant share exceeding 91%. Despite ranking fourth nationwide in vegetable production, Hebei ranked only 13th to 14th in export value, highlighting structural bottlenecks in deep processing, cold chain logistics, and brand internationalization.

## Destination Market Distributions and Trade Modality Structures

Geographical distribution patterns reveal that Hebei's vegetable exports have diversified across global regions while maintaining dense concentration in East Asia and Southeast Asia. The United States exhibited notable expansion, rising from 1.46 billion yuan in 2019 to 4.07 billion yuan in 2024, a cumulative increase of 178.77%, which surpassed South Korea to establish the United States as Hebei's premier export destination. Meanwhile, traditional regional partners such as South Korea, Japan, and Taiwan maintained substantial trade volumes, recording 3.39 billion yuan, 2.96 billion yuan, and 0.77 billion yuan respectively in 2024.

Emerging markets under regional trade agreements and international initiatives demonstrated accelerating trade momentum. Indonesia, Australia, and Thailand emerged as prominent growth vectors, with 2024 shipments registering 0.75 billion yuan, 0.72 billion yuan, and 0.62 billion yuan respectively. However, conventional destinations demonstrate market maturation and vulnerability to escalating external tariff actions and technical barriers.

Analysis of trade modalities indicates that general trade serves as the overwhelming transaction mechanism, persistently accounting for more than 91% of total provincial exports. General trade rose from 14.28 billion yuan (91.54%) in 2019 to 22.10 billion yuan (95.45%) in 2024, having peaked at 95.52% in 2021. Conversely, processing trade with imported materials declined from 1.26 billion yuan (8.10%) in 2019 to 0.85 billion yuan (3.66%) in 2024, while customs special supervision logistics and overseas contracting goods occupied negligible shares.

## Structural Industry Deficits and Strategic Countermeasure Pathways

A critical disparity persists between Hebei's vegetable agricultural production volume and its international trade standing. With annual vegetable output exceeding 54 million tons, ranking fourth nationally, Hebei's export value captured only 1.54% to 1.93% of the national total between 2019 and 2024, stagnating at 13th to 14th place among Chinese provinces. By comparison, leading province Shandong achieved 409.55 billion yuan in exports in 2024, representing 34.12% of the national aggregate.

This structural lag stems from several systemic vulnerabilities: traditional markets are reaching saturation while high technical production costs hinder flexible pivot into cost-sensitive emerging markets; industrial chain integration remains weak, characterized by small-scale primary processing enterprises reliant on coastal provinces for deep processing and contract packaging; cold-chain logistics capacity is constrained by outdated refrigerated warehousing; and independent brand equity is scarce, leaving exporters dependent on white-label manufacturing.

To resolve these barriers, strategic interventions must prioritize export destination diversification through differentiated production lines, establishment of dedicated SME trade financing funds, and rapid deployment of modern cold-chain infrastructure. Enterprisewide adoption of international certifications such as GlobalGAP and USDA NOP is essential alongside reinforced chemical pesticide residue management and heavy metal soil remediation to mitigate technical trade barriers.

- Development of flexible modular processing lines targeting emerging ASEAN and African markets.

- Expansion of advanced cold-chain storage to minimize transit degradation and spoilage.

- Systematic adoption of Good Agricultural Practices and international quality accreditations.

## Empirical Scope Constraints and Industrial Boundary Conditions

This study draws exclusively on provincial customs aggregation data covering 2019 to 2024, providing macroeconomic trade insights that must be interpreted within specific industrial and trade policy constraints.

- Macroeconomic customs statistics do not track intra-provincial intermediate transactions where Hebei vegetable products are sold to coastal provinces for secondary processing before foreign shipment.

- The empirical dataset precedes the long-term impacts of revised international tariff structures and heightened green trade barriers enacted after early 2025.

- Analysis is bounded by the four broad Harmonized System vegetable categories and does not extend to ultra-deep-processed functional extracts or cross-border e-commerce micro-shipments.

This study investigates canopy light utilization characteristics and architectural determinants across 19 commercial greenhouse cucumber cultivars grown in solar greenhouses. Evaluated through growth dynamics, principal component analysis (PCA), and dynamic time-series technique for order preference by similarity to an ideal solution (DTOPSIS), light use efficiency (LUE) exhibited an initial rise followed by a decline, peaking at a fitted leaf area index (LAI) of 3.0. Leaf dry weight and leaf area duration (LAD) served as dominant evaluation drivers. Cultivars 'Modi' and '958' achieved top comprehensive ranks, serving as benchmark ideotypes for winter-spring protected horticulture.

## Canopy Microclimate Dynamics and Leaf Area Trajectories

In northern Chinese solar greenhouse production, winter and early spring environments suffer from persistent low temperature and weak solar irradiation. Under these constraints, whole-canopy light interception and subsequent conversion into dry matter depend directly on canopy spatial structure. To examine light capture and dry matter allocation, 19 grafted cucumber cultivars were grown in a solar greenhouse under standard wide-row, raised-bed cultivation with a density of 3 500 plants per 667 m2.

Measurements of solar radiation and canopy microclimate revealed that LUE followed a unimodal trajectory across the crop ontogeny. Between 15 and 25 d after transplanting, coinciding with initial flowering to peak fruit set, dry matter accumulation accelerated, driving a rapid rise in LUE. The fitted peak LUE of 3.0% occurred at 45 d after transplanting. Thereafter, during the stem-lowering and lower-leaf pruning stages (45 to 65 d), dry matter accumulation decelerated, causing a downward trend in LUE.

Canopy expansion mirrored this trajectory, with LAI rising from 15 to 47 d before settling after canopy pruning. Peak fitted LAI reached 2.75 at 47 d after transplanting. When LAI remained below 2.5, restricted leaf area constrained total photon interception. Conversely, when LAI exceeded 3.0, mutual shading among upper leaves impaired light penetration into intermediate and lower canopy zones, depressing whole-canopy LUE. The fitted maximum LUE occurred at LAI = 3.0.

- Plant density established at 3 500 plants per 667 m2 across 24 m2 plots with 3 replications.

- Solar radiation and canopy microclimate tracked via TES-1333R and Top Cloud-Agri CMC-100 instrumentation.

- Fitted maximum LUE reached 3.0% at 45 d after transplanting.

- Fitted maximum LAI reached 2.75 at 47 d after transplanting, with optimal LUE occurring at LAI = 3.0.

## Multivariate Trait Variability and Morpho-Physiological Coordination

Evaluation of agronomic traits and photosynthetic indexes during peak fruiting (35 to 45 d after transplanting) showed substantial genotypic divergence. Leaf dry weight displayed the highest coefficient of variation at 34.51%, followed by CGR at 28.46%, NAR at 22.81%, LUE at 22.13%, and YP at 19.32%, while plant height showed the lowest phenotypic variance (CV = 8.81%).

Correlation analysis indicated that plant height was negatively correlated with NAR (r = -0.65) and SLW (r = -0.57). In contrast, LUE displayed a significant positive correlation with LAI (r = 0.52) and extremely significant positive correlations with NAR (r = 0.82), CGR (r = 0.95), SLW (r = 0.73), leaf dry weight (r = 0.91), and YP (r = 0.78). Yield per plant was likewise positively correlated with leaf dry weight (r = 0.81) and CGR (r = 0.77).

Principal component analysis extracted two components with eigenvalues exceeding 1.0, capturing 87.11% of total variance. PC1 (eigenvalue 4.47, 55.90% variance) functioned as the photosynthetic conversion and biomass factor, heavily loaded by leaf dry weight (0.450), CGR (0.449), YP (0.408), and NAR (0.396). PC2 (eigenvalue 2.50, 31.21% variance) represented canopy structure and light-interception capacity, loaded primarily by LAD (0.595), LAI (0.538), and plant height (0.416).

- Variability hierarchy ranked: leaf dry weight (34.51%) > CGR (28.46%) > NAR (22.81%) > LUE (22.13%) > YP (19.32%) > LAI (17.40%) > LAD (14.69%) > SLW (11.02%) > plant height (8.81%).

- LUE correlated positively with LAI (r = 0.52, P < 0.05) and strongly with CGR (r = 0.95, P < 0.01) and leaf dry weight (r = 0.91, P < 0.01).

- PC1 captured 55.90% of variance and was led by leaf dry weight (0.450); PC2 captured 31.21% and was led by LAD (0.595).

## DTOPSIS Multi-Trait Cultivar Ranking and Cluster Categorization

Hierarchical cluster analysis using the furthest neighbor method partitioned the 19 cultivars into three distinct clusters at an Euclidean distance cutoff of 0.7. Group I contained seven high-LUE cultivars: 'Liangjian', 'Hongyun', '303', 'Meiyu', 'Modi', '216', and '958'. Group II comprised six intermediate-LUE cultivars: 'Shenqing', '12', 'Yuxiu', '88', 'Wanxing', and '778'. Group III consisted of six low-LUE cultivars: '218', '726', 'No. 1', 'No. 5', '215', and 'Changfeng 4'.

To establish a comprehensive performance hierarchy, dynamic time-series TOPSIS (DTOPSIS) integration assigned objective dispersion weights across standardized indicators. Cultivar comprehensive proximity values (D) ranged from 0.02 to 0.74. 'Modi' achieved the highest score (D = 0.74, U1 = 0.70, U2 = 0.78), followed closely by '958' (D = 0.73, U1 = 1.00, U2 = 0.40) and '303' (D = 0.59, U1 = 0.71, U2 = 0.44). Conversely, 'Changfeng 4' ranked lowest (D = 0.02).

The top-performing cultivars balance moderate canopy stature with superior light interception and photosynthetic conversion. 'Modi' and '958' combine an optimal LAI near 3.0 with elevated leaf dry weight and compact canopy geometry, preventing severe inter-whorl self-shading during prolonged greenhouse cultivation.

- Cluster I (highest LUE) grouped 'Liangjian', 'Hongyun', '303', 'Meiyu', 'Modi', '216', and '958'.

- Cluster III (lowest LUE) grouped '218', '726', 'No. 1', 'No. 5', '215', and 'Changfeng 4'.

- Top-ranked cultivars by DTOPSIS: 'Modi' (D = 0.74, rank 1), '958' (D = 0.73, rank 2), and '303' (D = 0.59, rank 3).

## Methodological Scope and Production Boundaries

This investigation evaluated 19 grafted cucumber cultivars within a single solar greenhouse facility during the spring season (March to June 2025). Canopy architecture, light extinction, and carbon assimilation patterns reflect conditions specific to winter-spring solar greenhouses in northern China.

- Field trials were conducted from March to June 2025 in a solar greenhouse situated in Tai'an, Shandong; seasonal light angles and thermal regimes differ from autumn-winter production cycles.

- All cultivars were evaluated at a fixed plant density of 3 500 plants per 667 m2 using pumpkin rootstocks, precluding assessment of rootstock-scion interactions or ultra-high planting densities.

- The recommended high-efficiency cultivars 'Modi' and '958' require further validation under severe low-temperature, low-radiation regimens typical of late autumn and mid-winter cultivation.

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

## Processing Technology Evolution and Chemical Matrix Divergence

Traditional dry-grind processing involves milling, cooking, liquefaction, saccharification, yeast fermentation, distillation, and subsequent drying of thin stillage co-products. Under this scheme, starch is efficiently converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide, effectively concentrating non-fermentable components—such as crude protein, crude fiber, and crude fat—by approximately threefold compared with parent corn grain. Yeast proliferation contributes microbial protein accounting for roughly 20% of total DDGS protein. However, dry-grind plants increasingly incorporate mechanical centrifugation and post-fermentation oil extraction, segregating corn oil as a high-value commodity and shifting the residual co-product into medium-oil (6% to 9% ether extract) or low-oil (<4% ether extract) tiers.

Novel fractionation technologies modify upstream and downstream fiber separation to generate high-protein streams. In ProCap DDGS, high-protein and low-fiber components are isolated directly from distillers dried solubles (DDS) before distinct dehydration, yielding higher crude protein and lower fiber than de-oiled co-products. Similarly, Lincolnway high-protein DDGS separates fiber mechanically prior to fermentation based on solubility, extracts oil post-distillation, and utilizes a gentle compression drying system that mitigates thermal Maillard reactions. These structural upgrades alter the fundamental nutrient matrix, yielding neutral detergent fiber ranges from 28.80% to 53.77% and acid detergent fiber from 10.28% to 20.01% on a dry matter basis across diverse commercial batches.

- Classification under NRC standards categorizes corn DDGS by ether extract into high-oil (>10%), medium-oil (6% to 9%), and low-oil (<4%).

- Chinese national standard GB/T 25866-2010 specifies high-fat DDGS at >=7% and low-fat DDGS at >=2% crude fat.

- Advanced fractionated co-products avoid extreme heat exposure, preserving standardized ileal digestibility of critical essential amino acids.

Corn distillers dried grains with solubles (DDGS) serves as an alternative energy and protein ingredient replacing corn and soybean meal in swine diets. Modern fractionation and processing technologies have created diverse co-product categories, ranging from conventional high-oil dry-grind sources to de-oiled variants and novel high-protein products such as ProCap DDGS and Lincolnway high-protein DDGS. Systematic nutritional evaluation confirms crude protein concentrations between 26.80% and 54.78% on a dry matter basis, alongside variable digestible energy (3462 to 4945 kcal/kg DM). Successful dietary inclusion requires phase-specific upper bounds: under 25% for nursery piglets, up to 30% for growing-finishing pigs without compromising carcass quality, and up to 50% for gestating sows.

## Bioavailable Energy Quantification and Amino Acid Digestibility

The bioavailable energy content of corn DDGS is governed primarily by residual ether extract and non-starch polysaccharide (NSP) fiber concentrations. Swine metabolic assessments demonstrate digestible energy (DE) values fluctuating from 3462 to 4945 kcal/kg DM and metabolizable energy (ME) from 3248 to 4669 kcal/kg DM. High-protein variants like DDGS-HPLincolnway deliver 4424 kcal/kg DM DE and 4275 kcal/kg DM ME, outperforming conventional co-products that average 4148 kcal/kg DM DE and 3983 kcal/kg DM ME. Because in vivo digestion trials are resource-intensive, robust mathematical prediction models correlate available energy with proximate chemical fractions, incorporating dry matter, ash, crude fiber, and gross energy.

Standardized ileal digestibility (SID) of amino acids demonstrates pronounced variability, particularly for heat-sensitive basic amino acids. In conventional DDGS, SID lysine varies widely from 52.4% to 84.8%, while novel ProCap DDGS achieves superior SID values of 85.8% for lysine and 97.0% for tryptophan. Essential amino acid profiles exhibit persistent imbalances characterized by elevated leucine (3.00% to 7.69% DM) paired with modest lysine (0.60% to 1.89% DM) and tryptophan (0.18% to 0.49% DM). Excess leucine induces branched-chain amino acid antagonism, accelerating catabolism of isoleucine and valine unless rations are carefully balanced with synthetic amino acids.

- Metabolizable energy decreases substantially when high concentrations of insoluble xylan-rich dietary fiber displace digestible starch.

- Standardized ileal digestibility of methionine and phenylalanine consistently exceeds 80% across both conventional and high-protein variants.

- Dietary addition of exogenous xylanase and phytase significantly elevates apparent total tract digestibility of dry matter and gross energy.

## Stage-Specific Swine Diet Formulation and Carcass Quality Dynamics

Dietary integration of corn DDGS must be titrated to the physiological maturity of the digestive tract across nursery, growing-finishing, and breeding herds. In weaned piglets below 10 kg body weight, immature intestinal morphology and susceptibility to oxidative stress restrict DDGS inclusion. Incorporating DDGS up to 20% generally maintains acceptable performance, but inclusions of 25% to 30% suppress average daily feed intake and average daily gain due to bulking fiber and branched-chain amino acid imbalances. Nursery formulations containing DDGS benefit from supplemental crystalline valine, isoleucine, and threonine alongside exogenous carbohydrases.

Growing-finishing swine tolerate higher dietary proportions, with substitution levels between 15% and 30% maintaining average daily gain and feed conversion efficiency comparable to corn-soybean meal controls. However, high concentrations of polyunsaturated linoleic acid in corn DDGS oil increase belly fat unsaturation, raising carcass iodine values and carcass lightness. For reproductive herds, gestating sows possess expansive hindgut fermentation capacity, allowing up to 50% DDGS inclusion to satisfy maintenance energy requirements while supporting intestinal satiety. Lactating sows tolerate up to 30% DDGS without compromising litter growth, milk yield, or wean-to-estrus intervals.

- Nursery pig feeding trials confirm that exceeding 25% inclusion impairs growth rates and apparent ileal nutrient digestibility.

- Finishing pig diets containing 30% DDGS elevate linoleic acid percentages and iodine values in backfat and longissimus dorsi muscle.

- Gestating sows maintain productive stability at inclusion rates up to 50%, whereas lactating sows should not exceed 30% inclusion.

## Nutritional Constraints and Application Boundaries

Application of corn DDGS in swine production is restricted by inherent compositional challenges, including extreme batch-to-batch nutrient variation, thermal protein damage, high non-starch polysaccharide concentrations, and mycotoxin concentration.

- Thermal damage during drum drying induces advanced Maillard reactions that bind lysine, driving standardized ileal digestibility of lysine down to 52.4% to 56.16% in overheated batches.

- Ethanol fermentation consumes fermentable carbohydrates and concentrates original corn mycotoxins by approximately threefold in residual DDGS fractions.

- Elevated concentrations of linoleic and polyunsaturated fatty acids in high-oil and medium-oil DDGS alter adipose tissue composition, increasing carcass iodine value and softening commercial bacon slices when fed above 20% to 30% in finishing diets.

- Branched-chain amino acid disproportions caused by high leucine (reaching 7.69% DM) provoke metabolic antagonism that necessitates supplementary valine and isoleucine in young pig rations.

Gestating sows utilize high-fiber DDGS efficiently up to 50% inclusion, while lactating sows maintain reproductive performance when inclusion is capped at 30%. This review establishes definitive nutritional benchmarks and predictive energy equations for optimal DDGS integration across all swine production stages.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Crude protein spans 26.80% to 54.78% and crude fat spans 1.24% to 12.50% on a dry matter basis across different processing variants.
- ProCap DDGS achieves a digestible energy of 4945 kcal/kg DM and metabolizable energy of 4669 kcal/kg DM compared to 3667 and 3454 kcal/kg DM for conventional oil-extracted DDGS.
- Limiting amino acids remain deficient in conventional sources, with lysine ranging from 0.60% to 1.89% and tryptophan from 0.18% to 0.49% on a dry matter basis.
- Dietary inclusion thresholds require restriction below 25% in post-weaning nursery pigs, up to 30% in growing-finishing pigs, and up to 50% in gestating sows.
- Enzymatic supplementation using exogenous xylanase and phytase counteracts high non-starch polysaccharides and phytate-bound phosphorus, improving apparent ileal digestibility.

analysis_markdown_en:
This preclinical investigation evaluated the transgenerational effects of feeding gestating sows unconventional diets and an unconventional low-protein regimen on the intestinal development of neonatal piglets. Replacing conventional corn and soybean meal with wheat, broken rice, rice bran meal, and rapeseed meal maintained mucosal barrier integrity while enhancing mucosal architecture and digestive enzyme activities. Concurrently reducing dietary crude protein by 2 percentage points modulated colonic microbial colonization, raising Shannon diversity, suppressing potential bacterial pathogens such as Proteobacteria and Acinetobacter, and restoring short-chain fatty acid concentrations.

## Intestinal Mucosal Architecture and Digestive Hydrolase Activation

Maternal nutritional management during gestation exerts lifelong programming effects on fetal enteric tissue morphogenesis and metabolic maturation. Substituting standard corn and soybean meal with agricultural coproducts, specifically wheat, broken rice, rice bran meal, and rapeseed meal, altered the luminal nutritional matrix available to the sow without compromising gestational performance. In newborn piglets sampled prior to colostrum ingestion, small intestinal weights remained unaffected across dietary cohorts. However, microscopic examination of the intestinal mucosa demonstrated significant regional structural adaptations in response to maternal unconventional dietary exposure.

Histomorphometrical profiling revealed that neonates from sows fed the unconventional diet exhibited an increased jejunal villus height alongside a marked increase in ileal crypt depth compared with the control group. Concurrently, hydrolytic capacities within the small intestine exhibited pronounced enhancement. Duodenal trypsin activity increased significantly, accompanied by upward trends in jejunal trypsin activity. Furthermore, lipase activity expanded markedly in the ileum, confirming that maternal raw material substitution stimulates endogenous digestive enzyme synthesis in neonatal enterocytes and exocrine pancreatic tissue.

- Jejunal villus height measured 714.59±22.84 μm in CON versus 822.63±45.78 μm in UG (P=0.056).

- Ileal crypt depth increased from 95.27±3.46 μm in CON to 110.96±3.97 μm in UG (P=0.011).

- Duodenal trypsin rose from 172.37±13.83 U/mL in CON to 216.59±13.37 U/mL in UG (P=0.040).

- Ileal lipase activity expanded from 361.46±50.77 U/L in CON to 660.82±91.85 U/L in UG (P=0.017).

## Enteric Barrier Integrity and Inflammatory Cytokine Modulation

The integrity of the intestinal epithelial interface is governed by apical junctional complexes and protective mucin secretions. Assessment of jejunal tight junction markers indicated stable transcript levels of zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) and occludin (OCLN) across all experimental groups, verifying that maternal unconventional diets do not compromise mechanical barrier structure. Although mucin-2 (MUC2) expression and goblet cell counts did not differ significantly between treatments, quantitative tissue averages remained stable across small intestinal segments.

Systemic oxidative status indicated an upward trend in serum malondialdehyde (MDA) content in UG piglets compared with CON, whereas enzymatic antioxidants including glutathione peroxidase and total antioxidant capacity remained unchanged. At the mucosal transcript level, the unconventional diet induced a significant parallel upregulation of jejunal pro-inflammatory tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and anti-inflammatory interleukin-10 (IL-10). This dual activation reflects regulated physiological immune maturation and intestinal immune training rather than unchecked pathogenic inflammation.

- Relative mRNA abundance of jejunal TNF-alpha and IL-10 increased concurrently in the UG group (P<0.05).

## Colonic Microbial Succession and Short-Chain Fatty Acid Dynamics

High-throughput 16S rRNA gene profiling of neonatal colonic contents demonstrated that reducing crude protein in maternal unconventional diets shifted early pioneer bacterial colonization. While alpha diversity remained comparable between the CON and UG groups, reducing crude protein by 2 percentage points in the LUG cohort elevated colonic community Shannon diversity above UG levels. Principal coordinate analysis demonstrated distinct clustering tendencies between maternal feeding regimes, highlighting maternal metabolic input as an upstream regulator of neonatal microbiome assembly.

Taxonomic shifts under the LUG regimen were characterized by suppression of opportunistic taxa and enrichment of functional commensals. At the phylum level, Proteobacteria abundance decreased while Patescibacteria increased significantly in LUG neonates compared with UG neonates. At the genus level, Acinetobacter abundance dropped markedly alongside a reduction in Methylobacterium-Methylorubrum. Concurrently, beneficial Bacillus populations expanded significantly, complemented by increasing trends in Lachnospiraceae NK4A136 group, Lachnospiraceae UCG-006, and Alistipes. These microbial shifts supported a restorative trend in colonic propionic acid and butyric acid concentrations.

- Colonic propionic acid trended upward from 1.90±0.08 μg/g in UG to 2.11±0.08 μg/g in LUG (P=0.096).

- Colonic butyric acid trended upward from 0.83±0.04 μg/g in UG to 0.92±0.03 μg/g in LUG (P=0.078).

- Relative abundance of colonic Proteobacteria and Acinetobacter decreased significantly in LUG vs. UG (P<0.05).

- Relative abundance of colonic Patescibacteria and Bacillus increased significantly in LUG vs. UG (P<0.05).

## Experimental Constraints and Translational Scope

This study demonstrates physiological feasibility in gestating sows using alternative feedstuffs, but specific experimental boundaries must guide commercial implementation.

- The sample size was limited to 21 multiparous sows across 3 treatment cohorts, requiring validation in larger commercial breeding herds across varying parities.

- Measurements were conducted strictly at farrowing prior to colostrum suckling, leaving post-weaning growth kinetics and lifetime disease resistance unassessed.

- The 2 percentage point dietary protein reduction was evaluated alongside synthetic amino acid balancing, which remains mandatory when formulating practical low-protein diets.

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

abstract_en: Continuous cropping obstacles significantly restrict sustainable apple production during orchard replanting across the Loess Plateau. To clarify the microecological mechanisms by which exogenous microbial agents alleviate replant disease, pot experiments combined with high-throughput sequencing were conducted using continuous cropping orchard soil and Malus sieversii seedlings. Two inoculants were compared against untreated continuous cropping soil (CK1), autoclaved continuous cropping soil (CK2), and non-continuous cropping soil (CK3): a composite soil remediation agent comprising Trichoderma longibrachiatum, Aspergillus niger, and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (T10), and a single Trichoderma harzianum agent (T8). Application of T10 elevated leaf SPAD values by 12.15% over CK1 and raised seedling quality index by 146.51%, whereas T8 yielded a 25.58% increase. T10 and T8 enhanced total root length by 123.20% and 35.50%, total root surface area by 146.34% and 42.25%, average root diameter by 9.55% and 5.10%, total root volume by 178.95% and 48.37%, and root tip counts by 136.06% and 22.12%, respectively. Microbial inoculants reshaped the rhizosphere microbiome by increasing bacterial phylogenetic diversity and decreasing fungal community diversity and evenness. Trichoderma relative abundance surpassed 55% in inoculated treatments, while pathogenic Fusarium was markedly repressed. Furthermore, T10 augmented beneficial Pseudomonas and Lysobacter was enriched in T8. Consequently, composite microbial inoculation effectively restores rhizosphere microecology and promotes replanted apple seedling vigor.

analysis_markdown_en:
Continuous cropping obstacles severely impair the renewal and productivity of apple orchards across the Loess Plateau. This study evaluated two microbial interventions in replant soil using Malus sieversii seedlings: a composite soil remediation agent containing Trichoderma longibrachiatum, Aspergillus niger, and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (T10), and a single-strain Trichoderma harzianum agent (T8). Inoculation with T10 substantially stimulated shoot and root morphogenesis, increasing the seedling index by 146.51% and total root volume by 178.95% relative to continuous cropping controls. High-throughput sequencing demonstrated that microbial applications restructured rhizosphere communities by expanding bacterial phylogenetic diversity, enriching beneficial Proteobacteria and Pseudomonas, and establishing Trichoderma as the dominant fungal genus while suppressing pathogenic Fusarium.

## Alleviation of Seedling Growth Suppression Under Replant Conditions

Replant disease in aged apple production regions creates severe biological and physical stress, manifested as stunted root elongation, chlorosis, and depressed biomass accumulation. In this pot trial utilizing 25-year-old replant orchard substrate, seedling vigor was quantified across growth and photosynthetic indicators. The composite remediation agent T10 (incorporating Trichoderma longibrachiatum, Aspergillus niger, and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens) induced superior phenotypic recovery compared to both untreated replant soil (CK1) and the single-strain agent T8 (Trichoderma harzianum). Inoculation with T10 elevated leaf SPAD values to levels exceeding non-replant control soil (CK3) by 7.65% and CK1 by 12.15%, restoring photosynthetic pigment density.

Morphological measurements confirmed substantial vegetative recovery under microbial amendment. Apple seedlings treated with T10 achieved a plant height of 6.25 cm, stem circumference of 0.93 cm, and leaf count of 13.1 per plant, outperforming CK1 values of 5.28 cm, 0.67 cm, and 6.6 leaves per plant. Shoot dry weight reached 0.18 g and root dry weight reached 0.34 g in T10, generating a seedling index of 1.06 compared to 0.43 in CK1 and 0.47 in uninoculated virgin soil CK3. While single-strain T8 promoted shoot and root development beyond CK1 levels, its seedling index reached 0.54, verifying that multispecies microbial consortia confer greater vigor restoration in continuous cropping soils than single-strain inoculants.

- Seedling shoot fresh weight increased from 0.43 g in CK1 to 0.90 g in T10, representing a 109.30% enhancement.

- Root fresh weight rose from 0.42 g in CK1 to 1.03 g in T10, reflecting a 145.24% increase.

## Stimulation of Root Morphological Architecture and Absorptive Capacity

Root systems represent the immediate interface mediating replant soil sickness and nutrient assimilation. Analysis via root scanning systems demonstrated that continuous cropping severely restricts spatial root distribution, an inhibition counteracted by microbial inoculation. Seedlings grown in untreated CK1 displayed a total root length of 252.43 cm, surface area of 24.71 cm2, and total volume of 0.19 cm3. Following treatment with composite agent T10, root architectural parameters increased to 563.41 cm in length, 60.87 cm2 in surface area, and 0.53 cm3 in total volume, surpassing both sterilized replant soil (CK2) and healthy virgin soil (CK3).

Root branch points and absorptive tips serve as primary zones for water and mineral uptake. Inoculation with T10 stimulated root tip count to 1846 tips per plant, an increase of 136.06% relative to the 782 tips recorded in CK1. Single-strain T8 also enhanced root development, yielding 342.05 cm in root length, 35.15 cm2 in surface area, 0.28 cm3 in volume, and 955 root tips. The root-to-shoot ratio increased from 1.67 in CK1 to 1.80 in T8 and 1.89 in T10, indicating targeted resource allocation toward root system expansion that aids young trees in bypassing localized soil-borne stress.

- Average root diameter expanded from 0.157 mm in CK1 to 0.172 mm in T10 and CK3.

- Total root surface area under T10 (60.87 cm2) was more than double that of untreated continuous cropping control CK1 (24.71 cm2).

## Restructuring of Rhizosphere Bacterial and Fungal Community Ecology

High-throughput 16S and ITS amplicon sequencing demonstrated fundamental taxonomic and ecological restructuring within the seedling rhizosphere. Bacterial community diversity indices indicated that T10 generated the highest Faith phylogenetic diversity (Pd-faith of 355.07), markedly exceeding CK1 (212.62) and CK2 (143.18). Conversely, fungal community Shannon diversity dropped from 5.67 in CK1 to 4.80 in T10 and 4.03 in T8, accompanied by reductions in Pielou evenness. ## 1. Executive Abstract

Continuous cropping obstacles significantly restrict sustainable apple production during orchard replanting across the Loess Plateau. To clarify the microecological mechanisms by which exogenous microbial agents alleviate replant disease, pot experiments combined with high-throughput sequencing were conducted using continuous cropping orchard soil and Malus sieversii seedlings. Two inoculants were compared against untreated continuous cropping soil (CK1), autoclaved continuous cropping soil (CK2), and non-continuous cropping soil (CK3): a composite soil remediation agent comprising Trichoderma longibrachiatum, Aspergillus niger, and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (T10), and a single Trichoderma harzianum agent (T8). Microbial inoculants reshaped the rhizosphere microbiome by increasing bacterial phylogenetic diversity and decreasing fungal community diversity and evenness. Trichoderma relative abundance surpassed 55% in inoculated treatments, while pathogenic Fusarium was markedly repressed. Furthermore, T10 augmented beneficial Pseudomonas and Lysobacter was enriched in T8. Consequently, composite microbial inoculation effectively restores rhizosphere microecology and promotes replanted apple seedling vigor.

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Inoculation established Trichoderma as the predominant rhizosphere fungal genus (>55% relative abundance) while significantly decreasing the relative abundance of pathogenic Fusarium.

analysis_markdown_en:
The study addresses the shortage of high-quality roughage and the "human–livestock feed competition" constraint by testing whole-plant quinoa silage, a salt- and drought-tolerant dual-purpose crop, as a partial substitute for whole-plant corn silage in late-lactation dairy goats. The central engineering bottleneck is that quinoa alone is highly palatable but low in fiber structure, whereas blending with wheat straw raises fiber but depresses intake; adding 2% urea to the 7:3 quinoa–wheat straw mixture resolves this trade-off by supplying non-protein nitrogen that supports rumen fibrolytic and microbial protein synthesis.

The T3 formulation produced a "low intake, high conversion" response: feed intake fell 4.2% while 4% fat-corrected milk rose 54.9% and the feed-to-milk ratio dropped 33.6% versus the corn-silage control. The economic relevance lies in substituting a conventional corn silage with a marginal-land crop plus a low-cost straw and urea input, while simultaneously improving nitrogen utilization (serum urea nitrogen 9.78 to 7.73 mmol/L) and antioxidant/immune status. The main trade-off is that straw inclusion without urea (T2) depressed intake without a milk yield benefit, so urea addition is the decisive formulation variable.

### Abstract

This trial evaluated differently treated whole-plant quinoa silage as a partial replacement for whole-plant corn silage in late-lactation dairy goats. Sixty-four Wendeng dairy goats of similar body weight (47.54 ± 8.42 kg) and milk yield (1.05 ± 0.29 kg/d) were randomly allotted to four groups (four replicates of four goats). Under iso-nutrient conditions, the control (CON) received a total mixed ration containing 20% whole-plant corn silage, while T1, T2 and T3 replaced 10% of the corn silage (dry matter basis) with whole-plant quinoa silage, quinoa–wheat straw (7:3) mixed silage, and the same mixture plus 2% urea, respectively. The 60-d trial comprised a 15-d pre-trial and a 45-d formal period. Compared with CON, average daily feed intake was extremely significantly increased in T1 (P<0.01) but decreased in T2 and T3 (P<0.01). T3 increased average daily milk yield (P<0.05) and 4% fat-corrected milk (P<0.01) and lowered the feed-to-milk ratio (P<0.05). T2 and T3 improved crude protein and phosphorus apparent digestibility (P<0.05 or P<0.01); T3 also improved neutral and acid detergent fiber digestibility (P<0.05 or P<0.01). Serum urea nitrogen fell in all test groups (P<0.05). T3 reduced malondialdehyde (P<0.01), while T1 and T3 raised total antioxidant capacity and glutathione peroxidase activity (P<0.05). T1 and T3 elevated immunoglobulin G and interleukin-2 (P<0.01), and all test groups raised interleukin-10 and interferon-γ (P<0.05 or P<0.01). Replacing 10% corn silage with quinoa–wheat straw (7:3) silage plus 2% urea best improved lactation performance, digestibility, antioxidant status and immunity.

## Whole-Plant Quinoa–Wheat Straw (7:3) Silage with 2% Urea: Formulation and Chemical Composition

Whole-plant quinoa (cultivar Jinli No.1) was harvested at the late grain-filling stage and chopped to 2–3 cm; wheat straw was dried post-threshing straw. Three silages were prepared: quinoa alone (T1), quinoa–wheat straw at 7:3 (T2), and the same 7:3 mixture sprayed with 2% urea on a fresh-weight basis (2 kg urea per 100 kg fresh mixture, dissolved in water). All materials were wrapped in six layers of stretch film and ensiled 60 d in a cool, ventilated store. Whole-plant corn silage (Xianyu 335, milk stage) served as the control roughage.

Analyzed composition (DM basis) showed T1 at 28.84% DM, 8.97% CP, 44.60% NDF, 31.03% ADF and 3.85% ADL; T2 at 30.51% DM, 10.66% CP, 54.58% NDF, 31.84% ADF and 6.32% ADL; T3 at 26.09% DM, 9.26% CP, 59.73% NDF, 36.94% ADF and 7.99% ADL. Corn silage contained 24.76% DM, 11.94% CP, 56.88% NDF, 34.22% ADF and 7.35% ADL. Calcium was highest in T1 (1.16%) and lowest in T2 (0.67%), while phosphorus ranged from 0.17% (corn silage) to 0.42% (T1).

## Lactation Performance, Digestibility and Serum Biomarker Response in Wendeng Dairy Goats

Sixty-four late-lactation Wendeng dairy goats (210 d post-kidding; 47.54 ± 8.42 kg BW; 1.05 ± 0.29 kg/d milk) were assigned to four groups of four replicates (four goats each) under a single-factor completely randomized design. Diets were iso-nutrient (ME 9.94–9.99 MJ/kg; CP 14.41–14.44%; NDF 47.39–47.99%), with test silages replacing 10% of corn silage on a DM basis. Goats were fed TMR twice daily at 08:00 and 18:30 with free water and a target 5% refusal rate; milk was machine-collected at 06:00 and 18:00. The trial ran 60 d (15 d pre-trial, 45 d formal) at the Shandong Wendeng Dairy Goat Science and Technology Backyard.

Apparent digestibility was measured on days 41–45 using acid-insoluble ash as an internal marker. ## Boundary Constraints of the 10% Substitution Regime and Urea-Dependent Response

- The substitution was fixed at 10% of dietary DM (replacing half of the 20% corn silage); higher inclusion rates and their effect on rumen pH and fiber kinetics were not tested.

- Straw inclusion without urea (T2) depressed average daily feed intake to 1.99 kg/d (P<0.01) without a milk yield gain, so the benefit is conditional on 2% urea addition.

- The trial used 64 goats over 45 d; long-term effects on body condition, reproduction and milk fatty acid profile in late lactation remain unmeasured.

- Urea handling requires dissolution and uniform spraying on fresh mixture (2 kg per 100 kg) before six-layer stretch-film ensiling for 60 d.

## Experimental Cohort Design and Growth Dynamics

A 42-day feeding trial was performed using 288 healthy 1-day-old Arbor Acres (AA) white-feathered broilers (initial weight 46±0.64 g), allocated across 6 treatments with 6 replicates of 8 birds each. Experimental dietary phases were divided into starter (1-21 d) and grower-finisher (22-42 d) periods. Treatments evaluated baseline feed against two inclusion levels of B. subtilis (BS1 at 5×10^9 CFU/kg; BS2 at 6×10^9 CFU/kg), chitosan oligosaccharide (COS at 125 mg/kg; molecular weight <1,500 u, purity 98%), and their combinations (MIX I and MIX II).

During 1-21 days of age, average daily gain was significantly increased in BS2 (44.05±0.66 g/d), COS (44.06±0.54 g/d), MIX I (44.87±0.59 g/d), and MIX II (44.32±0.49 g/d) compared to CON (42.92±1.04 g/d, P<0.01). Across the entire 42-day period, combined groups exhibited superior growth velocity over single-additive cohorts, validating synergistic interaction between probiotic spore formers and prebiotic oligosaccharides.

- MIX I 42-day final body weight reached 2,788.12±78.21 g versus 2,716.77±29.32 g in CON.

- ADFI in the starter phase was 56.95±1.12 g/d in MIX II compared with 59.20±0.76 g/d in CON (P=0.002).

This study evaluated dietary supplementation with Bacillus subtilis (BS), chitosan oligosaccharides (COS), and their combined synbiotic mixtures across 288 Arbor Acres (AA) broilers over a 42-day feeding period. Co-supplementation of 6×10^9 CFU/kg BS plus 125 mg/kg COS (MIX II) significantly enhanced average daily gain (ADG) during days 1-21, 22-42, and overall days 1-42 (P<0.01). Crude protein utilization was elevated in the MIX I group (67.50±0.46%, P<0.05). Furthermore, high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing revealed that MIX II enriched beneficial cecal populations, notably Bacteroidetes, Verrucomicrobia, and Akkermansia, verifying functional microfloral modulation.

## Carcass Characteristics, Meat Quality, and Nutrient Digestibility

Slaughter performance evaluated at 42 days demonstrated that the standalone BS2 treatment produced marked improvements in carcass metrics, yielding significant increases in semi-eviscerated and full-eviscerated percentages (P<0.05). Conversely, breast muscle percentage (ranging between 27.06% and 27.83%), thigh muscle percentage (21.05% to 21.92%), and abdominal fat rate (1.27% to 2.22%) showed no statistically significant differences across groups (P>0.05).

Metabolic evaluations demonstrated that MIX I enhanced crude protein retention to 67.50±0.46% (P=0.023), likely mediated by bacterial secretion of active proteases, phytases, and glucanases that degrade anti-nutritional compounds. Meat quality parameters, including pH at 45 minutes and 24 hours, shear force, water loss rate, and CIE color metrics (L*, a*, b*), remained stable across treatments. However, breast drip loss was elevated in MIX I (P=0.005), which is associated with altered membrane permeability from low-molecular-weight oligosaccharides and elevated polyunsaturated fatty acid incorporation.

## Cecal Microbiome Taxonomic Shifts and Alpha-Diversity

Amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA V3-V4 hypervariable region highlighted that Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Verrucomicrobia constituted over 96% of the cecal microbial community across all cohorts. In the COS group, Chao1, ACE, and Shannon diversity metrics increased by 0.13%, 0.52%, and 1.56% respectively, alongside a 5.2% reduction in the Simpson index, though alpha-diversity shifts did not cross significance thresholds (P>0.05).

Principal coordinate analysis (PCoA) revealed that PC1 and PC2 accounted for 40.23% and 11.04% of total variation, with BS2 displaying clear separation while BS1, COS, MIX I, and MIX II formed tight overlapping clusters. Taxonomic profiling revealed that MIX II co-supplementation expanded relative abundances of Bacteroidetes (0.56 vs 0.55 in CON) and Verrucomicrobia (0.04 vs 0.02 in CON) at the phylum level, while concurrently driving genus-level increases in Bacteroides (0.45 vs 0.40 in CON) and Akkermansia (0.04 vs 0.02 in CON), reinforcing intestinal mucin integrity and short-chain fatty acid generation.

## Experimental Boundaries and Methodological Constraints

The findings are bounded by specific broiler genetic stock, environmental cage-rearing protocols, and chemical characteristics of the tested oligosaccharide batch.

- The chitosan oligosaccharide utilized possessed a molecular weight under 1,500 u, which increased breast muscle drip loss in MIX I (2.35±0.46% vs 2.24±0.40% in CON); heavier fractions (2,400-3,600 u) reported in literature may yield different water-holding profiles.

- The trial operated under sanitized, 3-tier battery cage housing at temperatures gradually declining from 33 ℃ to 21 ℃, which lacks the pathogen and environmental stressors commonly encountered in high-density commercial floor-litter housing.

- Growth performance benefits were most pronounced in starter phases (1-21 d), suggesting that additive dosages require dynamic titration across distinct physiological development stages.

# Effects of Bacillus subtilis, Chitosan Oligosaccharide and Their Combination on Growth Performance, Meat Quality and Cecal Microflora Diversity of Broilers

---

**DOI:** `10.11843/j.issn.0366-6964.2026.03.030` | **Journal:** Acta Veterinaria et Zootechnica Sinica (畜牧兽医学报) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** YANG Guang, ZHAO Yahui, LIU Yeqing, ZHANG Gaowei, WANG Ke, LU Xinyu, SU Xiangtan, SUN Jiale, CHEN Jiwei, GAO Aiqin  
**Affiliation:** College of Animal Science, Inner Mongolia Agricultural University, Hohhot 010018, China

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

This study was conducted to investigate the effects of Bacillus subtilis (BS) and chitosan oligosaccharides (COS) on growth performance, nutrient utilization, slaughter performance, meat quality, and cecal microflora diversity of AA broilers. A total of 288 one-day-old broilers with similar initial body weight (46±0.64 g) were randomly divided into six treatment groups with six replicates per treatment and eight chickens per replicate. Treatments comprised a control basal diet (CON), 5×10^9 CFU/kg BS (BS1), 6×10^9 CFU/kg BS (BS2), 125 mg/kg COS, 5×10^9 CFU/kg BS + 125 mg/kg COS (MIX I), and 6×10^9 CFU/kg BS + 125 mg/kg COS (MIX II) for 42 days. From 1 to 42 days of age, ADG in MIX I and MIX II groups was significantly increased compared with CON (P<0.01). The crude protein utilization rate of broilers in MIX I was significantly elevated (P<0.05). In slaughter performance, BS2 significantly improved semi-eviscerated and eviscerated yields (P<0.05). Meat quality attributes (pH, shear force, color) showed no significant differences among groups, though MIX I elevated breast muscle drip loss (P<0.01). Cecal profiling indicated that MIX II increased the relative abundances of Bacteroidetes, Verrucomicrobia, Bacteroides, and Akkermansia, demonstrating that synbiotic administration supports digestive health and growth performance in broilers.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Across the entire 1-42 day trial, average daily gain (ADG) was significantly improved in MIX I (65.29±1.86 g/d) and MIX II (65.00±3.88 g/d) relative to CON (63.59±0.70 g/d, P<0.01).
- Apparent crude protein utilization reached 67.50±0.46% in the MIX I group, significantly outperforming the control group (65.20±0.90%, P=0.023).
- Dietary BS2 (6×10^9 CFU/kg) significantly raised semi-eviscerated and full-eviscerated carcass yields (P<0.05).
- Microbial community profiling demonstrated that MIX II enriched cecal Bacteroidetes and Verrucomicrobia at the phylum level, alongside Bacteroides and Akkermansia at the genus level.
- Low-molecular-weight COS (<1,500 u) increased breast drip loss in MIX I (2.35±0.46% vs 2.24±0.40% in CON, P=0.005), whereas leg muscle drip loss exhibited a downward trend.

---

## Edaphic Acidification and Nutrient Dynamics Across Cultivation Ages

Continuous monoculture of medicinal plants frequently induces soil degradation and severe replanting obstacles. In this study, rhizosphere soils of Asarum heterotropoides var. liaoningense were harvested from plantations spanning 0 (XX0), 2 (XX2), 3 (XX3), 4 (XX4), and 6 years (XX6) in Xinbin County, Liaoning Province. Edaphic analysis demonstrated marked shifts in soil chemical properties along the temporal chronosequence. Soil pH dropped progressively from an initial baseline of 5.67±0.20 in uncultivated soil to 4.88±0.03 at year 3, eventually reaching extreme acidification at 3.99±0.06 by year 6.

Nutrient availability exhibited pronounced non-linear trajectories over the cultivation lifespan. Soil organic matter (SOM) and total nitrogen (TN) peaked during the second year of cultivation, reaching 57.37±19.81 g·kg-1 and 3 153.33±920.07 mg·kg-1 respectively, before plummeting to their lowest concentrations at year 3 (11.27±0.96 g·kg-1 SOM and 725.33±93.33 mg·kg-1 TN). In contrast, total phosphorus (TP) and total potassium (TK) peaked sharply at year 3, attaining 4.33±0.56 g·kg-1 and 24 883.03±797.32 mg·kg-1. These nutrient fluctuations reflect intensive early-stage organic inputs followed by severe nutrient imbalances and acidification stress as cultivation progresses.

- Rhizosphere pH decreased monotonically: 5.67±0.20 (XX0), 5.26±0.11 (XX2), 4.88±0.03 (XX3), 4.05±0.07 (XX4), and 3.99±0.06 (XX6).

- Year 2 supported peak accumulation of soil organic matter (57.37±19.81 g·kg-1) and total nitrogen (3 153.33±920.07 mg·kg-1).

- Year 3 exhibited maximal reserves of total phosphorus (4.33±0.56 g·kg-1) and total potassium (24 883.03±797.32 mg·kg-1).

This study decodes the edaphic and taxonomic dynamics in the rhizosphere of Asarum heterotropoides across a chronosequence of 0, 2, 3, 4, and 6 cultivation years in Xinbin County, Liaoning Province. High-throughput amplicon sequencing identified 16 119 bacterial OTUs and 3 512 fungal OTUs. Edaphic acidification drove progressive ecological restructuring, dropping soil pH from 5.67 to 3.99 by year 6. Alpha-diversity metrics decreased significantly with planting duration, correlating positively with declining pH. Concurrently, dominant phytopathogenic fungi such as Didymella and Alternaria proliferated in aged plantations, while beneficial taxa declined, underscoring acidification-mediated microecological dysbiosis.
