## Microbial Community Reconfiguration and Diversity Degradation Patterns

High-throughput Illumina NextSeq sequencing of the bacterial 16S rRNA gene (primers 338F/806R) and fungal ITS region (primers ITS1F/ITS2) revealed profound structural reorganization in rhizosphere microecology. Among bacterial assemblages, 14 phyla exhibited average relative abundances exceeding 1%, dominated globally by Proteobacteria (29.25%). As cultivation years advanced, Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota expanded their relative shares, whereas Actinobacteriota decreased. At the genus tier, beneficial plant-growth-promoting taxa such as RB41 dominated early soils (XX0 and XX2), transitioning toward Sphingomonas, Bradyrhizobium, and Bryobacter by year 3.

The fungal community was governed by six major phyla, overwhelmingly dominated by Ascomycota with an overall mean relative abundance of 63.56%, followed by Mortierellomycota and Basidiomycota. In pristine and young soils (XX0 and XX2), Mortierella co-dominated with Ascomycota, accounting for 19.36% and 28.76% of relative fungal abundance, respectively. By years 4 and 6, Basidiomycota surged to 17.22% and 19.13%, accompanied by an aggressive dominance of Ascomycota (63.52% and 72.42%). Alpha-diversity analyses demonstrated that bacterial and fungal Ace, Chao, and Shannon indices declined continuously across the chronosequence while the Simpson index climbed, verifying a severe attrition of microbial species richness and evenness.

- Proteobacteria maintained cross-treatment bacterial dominance with an average relative abundance of 29.25%.

- Ascomycota dominated fungal communities at an overall average abundance of 63.56%, peaking at 74.06% in XX3.

- Significant divergence across age cohorts confirmed by ANOSIM for bacteria (R2 = 0.908 1, P<0.001) and fungi (R2 = 0.989 6, P<0.001).

## Edaphic Drivers of Pathogen Enrichment and Dysbiosis Mechanisms

Pearson correlation matrices established soil pH as the predominant edaphic driver governing rhizosphere microecological succession. Bacterial Ace (r = 0.850 0, P<0.001), Chao (r = 0.864 0, P<0.001), and Shannon (r = 0.717 4, P<0.01) indices were positively correlated with pH. Similarly, fungal Ace (r = 0.887 3, P<0.001), Chao (r = 0.860 5, P<0.001), and Shannon (r = 0.853 3, P<0.001) indices displayed strong positive correlations with pH, while fungal Simpson index correlated negatively (r = -0.822 9, P<0.001). Conversely, soil organic matter and total nitrogen exhibited weak correlations with overall microbial diversity indices, confirming that acidification directly suppresses community richness.

Taxonomic correlation analyses revealed that falling pH selectively favored acid-tolerant and necrotrophic phytopathogens. Negative correlations with soil pH were recorded for Chujaibacter (r = -0.864 82, P<0.001), Rhodanobacter (r = -0.864 04, P<0.001), Didymella (r = -0.771 02, P<0.01), Trichoderma (r = -0.762 08, P<0.01), and Alternaria (r = -0.685 15). Crucially, Didymella and Alternaria represent primary causative agents of leaf blight and black mold disease in A. heterotropoides. Meanwhile, beneficial growth-promoting Mortierella correlated positively with pH (r = 0.858 68, P<0.001). The loss of suppressive microbes alongside severe soil acidification precipitates pathogen outbreaks in mature plantations.

- Bacterial richness indicators Ace (r = 0.850 0) and Chao (r = 0.864 0) correlated positively with pH at P<0.001.

- Fungal pathogen Didymella (r = -0.771 02, P<0.01) and bacterial Chujaibacter (r = -0.864 82, P<0.001) correlated negatively with pH.

- Beneficial fungal genus Mortierella exhibited strong positive correlation with pH (r = 0.858 68, P<0.001).

Bulk density exhibited limited variation among treatments, spanning from 1.22±0.10 g·cm-3 in NHS to 1.37±0.02 g·cm-3 in NPK.

- Single straw returning (NS) raised ammonium nitrogen to 6.06±0.47 mg·kg-1 compared with 3.89±0.11 mg·kg-1 under CK.

- Soil organic carbon reached its maximum under biochar returning at 11.36±0.60 g·kg-1, closely followed by double straw at 11.25±0.29 g·kg-1.

## Minimum Dataset Construction via Principal Component Analysis

To condense indicator dimensionality while preserving diagnostic capacity, twenty-four soil variables were analyzed via principal component analysis. Five principal components exhibited eigenvalues exceeding 1.0, accounting for a cumulative variance contribution rate of 84.09%. Variables possessing loadings greater than 0.5 were grouped, and comprehensive norm values were computed to retain indicators within the top 10% range of the highest group score.

Subsequent correlation filtering eliminated redundant parameters. In group one, sucrase correlated strongly with total nitrogen (r = 0.81, P < 0.001); sucrase was retained due to its superior norm value of 1.897. In group two, urease correlated with protease (r = 0.7, P < 0.05); urease (norm 1.734) was selected over protease (norm 1.651). The finalized minimum dataset comprised soil organic carbon, available phosphorus, available potassium, sucrase, and urease, carrying weights of 0.213, 0.199, 0.188, 0.196, and 0.204, respectively.

Integrating standard S-shaped and parabolic scoring functions yielded the principal component soil health index (PCA-SHI). The health index ranked treatments in the order of NS > NBC > NHS > NPK > CS > CK. Straw incorporation elevated health scores over mineral fertilization alone by 19.85% under NS and 14.45% under NHS, whereas unfertilized straw returning boosted scores by 16.49% over CK. Excess straw input under NHS reduced overall index performance relative to standard straw returning, underscoring short-term nutrient imbalances provoked by over-amendment.

## Random Forest Screening of Key Microbial Community Indicators

High-throughput sequencing revealed distinct taxonomic shifts across treatments. Fungal alpha diversity proved markedly more sensitive to field practices than bacterial diversity. Mineral nitrogen application reduced fungal richness, causing a 67.79% decline in fungal Chao1 index in NPK relative to CK. Direct straw returning partially ameliorated this suppression, increasing fungal Chao1 by 26.32% over NPK. Remarkably, biochar input (NBC) expanded fungal Chao1 by 167.53%, fungal Shannon diversity by 59.16%, and Pielou evenness by 27.29% compared to NS.

Using PCA-SHI as the response metric, a random forest model was executed using the rfPermute package in R to quantify feature importance via the percentage increase in mean squared error (MSE). Nine biological parameters were extracted: phylum-level relative abundances of Spirochaetota, Actinobacteriota, and Mortierellomycota; bacterial Chao1 and fungal Shannon diversity; alongside functional genes rbcL, nosZ, ureC, and soxA. Actinobacteriota demonstrated the highest feature importance at 5.506% MSE increase (weight 0.169), followed by Mortierellomycota at 4.535% (weight 0.140).

The computed random forest soil health index (RF-SHI) yielded scores of 0.623 for NBC, 0.569 for NS, and 0.367 for CK. While RF-SHI scores shifted NBC slightly ahead of NS due to pronounced microbial diversity gains in biochar-amended plots, overall cohort stratification closely preserved the trajectory defined by standard physical and chemical datasets.

Intensive rice-wheat cropping in southern Jiangsu requires sensitive bio-indicators to diagnose soil degradation early. This field study evaluates soil physicochemical properties, enzyme kinetics, and high-throughput sequencing profiles across six straw and fertilization regimes. Principal component analysis identified a minimum dataset comprising soil organic carbon, available phosphorus, available potassium, sucrase, and urease. Coupling the resulting soil health index with a random forest machine learning pipeline isolated nine critical microbial community indicators, including Actinobacteriota, Mortierellomycota, and nutrient-cycling genes rbcL, nosZ, ureC, and soxA, establishing a biologically responsive monitoring architecture.

## Regional Scope and Methodological Boundary Constraints

This evaluation framework reflects single-season sampling within a multi-year field experiment on orthic stagnic hydragric soils in southern Jiangsu, requiring consideration of decomposition kinetics and longitudinal climate variability.

- Field sampling was conducted in November 2023 during the rice maturity stage of a field trial initiated in 2022, capturing relatively short-term biological equilibration after straw and biochar inputs.

- The minimum dataset was derived under specific hydrological regimes of rice-wheat rotation; generalizability to continuous upland cereals or dryland soils remains unverified without recalibrating membership thresholds.

- Functional gene profiles derived from metagenomic sequencing represent potential genetic abundance rather than real-time in situ transcriptomic activity.

abstract_en: Winter survival is the primary determinant governing the northward expansion of winter rapeseed (Brassica napus L.) in cold and arid zones. In this study, nine cultivars spanning strong, moderate, and weak winterness were evaluated across consecutive overwintering cycles (2023-2025) in Qingyang, Gansu Province. Field phenotyping coupled with histological and physiological assays demonstrated that overwintering survival was tightly and negatively correlated with growth point height (r=-0.972, P<0.001) and positively correlated with the root/crown ratio (r=0.677, P=0.045). Strong cold-tolerant cultivars, such as NTS309 (74.00% overwintering rate), sustained recessed growth points (3.07 cm) and compact growth cones (161.5 μm), accompanied by reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation and minimal cellular damage. In contrast, cold-sensitive lines like Qinzao 1 protruded 4.89 cm above ground with 252.9 μm growth cones. Targeted LC-MS/MS hormone profiling combined with RNA sequencing demonstrated that a multi-hormonal network governs apical morphology. Tolerant lines exhibited significant elevations in conjugated indole-3-acetic acid (IAA-Glu), jasmonoyl-L-isoleucine (JA-Ile), and abscisic acid glucosyl ester (ABA-GE), alongside suppression of specific cytokinin glucosides (iP9G, mT9G, BAP9G). Orthogonal partial least squares analysis confirmed that metabolic shifts co-vary with auxin and AP2/ERF signaling pathways, establishing a feedback loop that curbs longitudinal cell elongation, drives bud dormancy, and shields shoot apical meristems from sub-zero injury.

Winter survival in northern Brassica napus cultivation hinges on low-temperature avoidance through meristematic architecture. Across a two-year field evaluation (2023-2025) of nine cultivars with distinct winterness in Qingyang, Gansu Province, overwintering rate exhibited an extremely significant negative correlation with growth point height (r=-0.972, P<0.001). Cultivars with overwintering rates exceeding 70% maintained compact growth points retracted approximately 3 cm relative to ground level, alongside growth cone heights of 161.5 μm. Integrated LC-MS/MS targeted hormone profiling and RNA-seq revealed that coordinated signaling across auxins, cytokinins, gibberellins, abscisic acid, and jasmonates suppresses cell elongation and induces meristem dormancy.

## Phenotypic Screening and Microscopic Morphometry of Overwintering Meristems

Field evaluations conducted between 2023 and 2025 in Qingyang, Gansu Province, revealed pronounced phenotypic divergence across nine Brassica napus cultivars possessing variable winterness. Cultivars categorized as strong winterness (GAU30, NTS309, GAU24, and 16-2444) sustained overwintering survival rates from 73.67% to 75.00%, whereas weak-winterness lines such as Ganza 9 and Qinzao 1 dropped to 57.00% and 49.67%, respectively. Notably, gross biomass traits exhibited minimal direct correlation with cold hardiness; dry weight showed no correlation (r=0.012, P=0.976), while collar diameter correlated weakly (r=-0.191, P=0.622). In contrast, the growth point height displayed a decisive inverse relationship with field survival (r=-0.972, P<0.001), identifying apical retraction as a defining morphological criterion.

Microscopic examination of the shoot apical meristem via paraffin sectioning established that the dome-shaped growth cone dimensions differed substantially across genotypes. Strong cold-tolerant NTS309 formed a compact growth cone measuring 161.5 μm in vertical dimension. Intermediate Tianyou 14 and cold-sensitive Qinzao 1 exhibited extended growth cones measuring 248.9 μm and 252.9 μm, respectively. Trypan blue and nitroblue tetrazolium staining confirmed that recessed, low-stature growth points suffered markedly lower superoxide accumulation and membrane breakdown following low-temperature exposure, thereby isolating sensitive vegetative stem cells beneath the thermal insulation of the soil surface.

- GAU30 and NTS309 recorded the highest overwintering rates at 75.00±3.06% and 74.00±2.31%, respectively.

- Qinzao 1 exhibited the highest collar diameter (30.65±1.96 mm) yet the lowest overwintering rate (49.67±2.60%).

- Growth cone micro-morphology ranged from 161.5 μm in NTS309 up to 252.9 μm in Qinzao 1.

## Multi-Hormonal Profiling and Phytohormone Feedback Coordination

Targeted LC-MS/MS quantification across three representative cultivars (NTS309, Tianyou 14, and Qinzao 1) demonstrated that growth point height is orchestrated by an intricate hormonal equilibrium rather than an isolated pathway. Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) metabolism varied extensively: although free IAA was elevated in Qinzao 1 (28.34±3.34) and NTS309 (24.37±0.56) relative to Tianyou 14 (17.49±0.19), NTS309 maintained significantly higher levels of auxin storage conjugates and intermediates, including IAA-Glu (1.79±0.17), MEIAA (285.43±30.95), IAM (85.23±9.41), and IAN (1796.08±69.00). In contrast, Qinzao 1 displayed unrestrained apical development that promoted premature pre-winter bolting and floral bud differentiation.

Cytokinin profiles exhibited contrasting distributions between free active ribosides and inactive glucosides. Trans-zeatin riboside (tZR) decreased steadily from cold-hardy NTS309 (2.27±0.15) to Tianyou 14 (1.60±0.15) and Qinzao 1 (0.40±0.03). Concurrently, specific cytokinin-9-glucosides, including iP9G, mT9G, and BAP9G, accumulated exclusively in the less tolerant lines, with iP9G reaching 4.40±0.34 in Qinzao 1 while remaining undetectable in NTS309. Defense-associated phytohormones further differentiated the hardiness classes: jasmonate derivatives JA-Ile (8.09±0.71) and MeJA (2.84±0.08), alongside the abscisic acid conjugate ABA-GE (21.61±1.07), were elevated in NTS309 but dropped to zero in Qinzao 1.

- Active trans-zeatin riboside (tZR) dropped 82.38% from 2.27±0.15 in NTS309 to 0.40±0.03 in Qinzao 1.

- Inactivating cytokinin glucoside iP9G was absent in NTS309 but rose to 4.40±0.34 in Qinzao 1.

## Transcriptomic Signaling Cascades and Apical Dormancy Regulation

RNA sequencing and orthogonal partial least squares (O2PLS) integration revealed that differentially expressed genes between strong and weak cold-tolerant varieties enriched significantly in tryptophan metabolism, zeatin biosynthesis, plant hormone signal transduction, and alpha-linolenic acid metabolism. Key auxin transcriptional repressor genes, including IAA7, IAA17, IAA18, IAA19, and IAA29, were significantly up-regulated by 3.3-, 2.5-, 3.0-, 1.7-, and 2.1-fold in high-growth-point Tianyou 14 relative to NTS309, whereas IAA9 and IAA30 showed relative down-regulations of 36.0% and 63.6%.

Abscisic acid signaling components, notably SnRK2 (ZS11A01G001170) and ABF27 (ZS11A07G003150), displayed differential expression that supported meristem quiescence. Activation of the SnRK2-ABF signaling module induces downstream LEA factors while restraining gibberellin synthesis and cell wall loosening machinery. Furthermore, differential expression across eleven ethylene-responsive factor (ERF) genes, such as ZS11A01G005570 and ZS11A06G011380, connects membrane oxylipin signaling (via 12-oxo-phytodienoic acid) with local auxin and cytokinin synthesis, establishing a closed feedback circuit that restricts growth cone elevation prior to freezing onset.

- Auxin repressor IAA18 demonstrated a 3.0-fold elevation in Tianyou 14 compared to NTS309.

- Auxin signal components IAA9 and IAA30 declined by 36.0% and 63.6%, respectively, in Tianyou 14.

- Differential expression of SnRK2 and ABF27 facilitates dormancy transition and suppression of cell elongation.

## Environmental Scope and Selection Applicability Boundaries

This study clarifies the phenotypic and endocrine determinants of overwintering survival in northern winter rapeseed, yet several operational boundaries define its field applicability.

- Field trials were executed specifically within the Qingyang loess plateau environment (35.73°N, 107.65°E, altitude 1404 m, 148 d frost-free period), meaning micro-climate variations such as prolonged snow cover or differing soil thermal conductivity may shift absolute growth point thresholds.

- Phenotypic selection thresholds defining dwarf growth points at height ≤3.00 cm apply specifically to pre-winter measurements conducted in mid-November prior to full vegetative freezing.

- Targeted metabolomic and transcriptomic profiling examined three focal genotypes (NTS309, Tianyou 14, Qinzao 1), warranting broader functional validation across diverse genetic backgrounds.

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

**Affiliation:** School of Agriculture and Bioengineering, Longdong University

## 1. Executive Abstract

Winter survival is the primary determinant governing the northward expansion of winter rapeseed (Brassica napus L.) in cold and arid zones. In this study, nine cultivars spanning strong, moderate, and weak winterness were evaluated across consecutive overwintering cycles (2023-2025) in Qingyang, Gansu Province. Field phenotyping coupled with histological and physiological assays demonstrated that overwintering survival was tightly and negatively correlated with growth point height (r=-0.972, P<0.001) and positively correlated with the root/crown ratio (r=0.677, P=0.045). Strong cold-tolerant cultivars, such as NTS309 (74.00% overwintering rate), sustained recessed growth points (3.07 cm) and compact growth cones (161.5 μm), accompanied by reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation and minimal cellular damage. In contrast, cold-sensitive lines like Qinzao 1 protruded 4.89 cm above ground with 252.9 μm growth cones. Targeted LC-MS/MS hormone profiling combined with RNA sequencing demonstrated that a multi-hormonal network governs apical morphology. Tolerant lines exhibited significant elevations in conjugated indole-3-acetic acid (IAA-Glu), jasmonoyl-L-isoleucine (JA-Ile), and abscisic acid glucosyl ester (ABA-GE), alongside suppression of specific cytokinin glucosides (iP9G, mT9G, BAP9G). Orthogonal partial least squares analysis confirmed that metabolic shifts co-vary with auxin and AP2/ERF signaling pathways, establishing a feedback loop that curbs longitudinal cell elongation, drives bud dormancy, and shields shoot apical meristems from sub-zero injury.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Field overwintering survival correlated negatively with growth point height (r=-0.972, P<0.001) and positively with root/crown ratio (r=0.677, P=0.045).
- Strong cold-tolerant cultivars achieved overwintering rates over 70.00% (GAU30 at 75.00±3.06%, NTS309 at 74.00±2.31%) with growth point heights around 3 cm.
- Paraffin section micro-morphology verified that growth cone height was 161.5 μm in cold-hardy NTS309 versus 248.9 μm in Tianyou 14 and 252.9 μm in Qinzao 1.
- Targeted profiling identified elevated JA-Ile (8.09±0.71 ng/g in NTS309 vs 0.00±0.00 ng/g in Qinzao 1) and ABA-GE (21.61±1.07 ng/g vs 0.00±0 ng/g).
- Auxin-responsive transcriptional repressors IAA7, IAA17, IAA18, IAA19, and IAA29 were up-regulated by 3.3, 2.5, 3.0, 1.7, and 2.1 fold in Tianyou 14 compared to NTS309.

Eighteen parameters encompassing germination, root morphology, plant height, dry biomass partitioning, and high-throughput photosynthetic fluorescence traits were measured after 20 d of exposure. Stress tolerance index (STI) conversions eliminated dimensional discrepancy while penalizing low basal yield. Extensive genetic diversity was identified across accessions, with variation coefficients spanning 17% to 188%. ## Multivariate Factor Extraction and Orthogonal Dimensionality Reduction

Soil salinization across the Songnen Plain is characterized by elevated pH and high sodium bicarbonate and carbonate levels that severely impede plant establishment and physiological growth. Leymus chinensis represents the dominant native rhizomatous grass across this biome, possessing high forage nutritional value and natural abiotic stress resilience. Nevertheless, natural populations exhibit broad phenotypic divergence in salt-alkali adaptability, necessitating systematic multidimensional screening.

Under simulated mixed sodic conditions of 60 mmol/L at pH=9.5, 18 traits were quantified after 20 d of continuous cultivation. To overcome distortions associated with conventional relative ratios, raw phenotypes were converted into the dimensionless multiplicative Stress Tolerance Index (STI). Principal component analysis resolved these metrics into 6 principal components possessing eigenvalues of 7.125, 2.840, 1.997, 1.167, 1.077, and 1.024, achieving an 84.615% cumulative contribution rate. Principal component 1 explained 39.583% of variance, dominated by photochemical competence metrics including relative chlorophyll index, normalized difference vegetation index, and maximum quantum efficiency.

Component 2 captured 15.779% of variance, reflecting germination percentage and biomass accumulation, while Component 3 accounted for 11.092% governed by vertical plant height and primary root extension. Weighting individual factor scores against individual variance contributions yielded unified composite D-values that accurately ranked overall tolerance across the 70 evaluated germplasm accessions.

- Eigenvalues of extracted components: PC1=7.125, PC2=2.840, PC3=1.997, PC4=1.167, PC5=1.077, and PC6=1.024.

- Cumulative variance contribution reached 84.615%, with PC1 contributing 39.583% and PC2 contributing 15.779%.

- Multiplicative STI standardization prevented low-baseline artifacts observed in raw proportional indices.

## Germplasm Cluster Stratification and Geographical Lineage Distribution

Hierarchical cluster analysis combining Euclidean distance metrics across the composite D-value and the 6 weighted principal component scores (μ1 through μ6) classified the 70 germplasms into three distinct ecological response groups. Cluster I comprised 11 highly salt-alkali tolerant accessions displaying a mean D-value of 1.889 across a range of 1.511 to 3.019, representing 15.71% of total evaluated materials. Cluster II encompassed 13 moderately tolerant accessions with an average D-value of 0.834 (range: 0.369 to 1.203, accounting for 18.57%). Cluster III formed the largest cohort consisting of 46 sensitive lines (65.71%), averaging a D-value of -0.688 across an interval from -1.657 to 0.559.

Spatial and genetic lineage cross-referencing revealed pronounced correlations between tolerance capacity, habitat provenance, and selection background. Among the 11 highly tolerant accessions, 54.55% were artificially selected cultivars or elite lines developed by the Institute of Forage and Grassland Sciences at the Heilongjiang Academy of Agricultural Sciences, led by elite material Jingmu No. 8 (YC47, D=3.019). Wild collections originating from the severe natural alkali soils of Anda, Suihua constituted 36.36% of the tolerant cluster, demonstrating that prolonged natural edaphic selection fixes high-stability tolerance alleles.

Conversely, sensitive accessions included both unimproved wild meadow ecotypes and specific cultivated lines, confirming substantial internal genetic variation within active breeding stocks.

- Cluster III (Sensitive): 46 accessions (65.71%), mean D-value -0.688 (range -1.657 to 0.559).

- Geographic distribution: 54.55% of Cluster I comprised institutional cultivars, while 36.36% originated from Anda saline soils.

## Stepwise Mathematical Modeling and Rapid Phenotyping Verification

To compress the laborious phenotyping burden required for large germplasm panels, a multivariate stepwise regression framework was developed. Modeling utilized 66 accessions allocated at a 9:1 training-to-validation ratio, designating composite D-values as the dependent variable and testing all 18 phenotypic and physiological variables as independent predictors.

The resulting 6-parameter equation is expressed as: D = -4.153 + 3.089*(Fv/FmSTI) + 0.161*(GRSTI) + 1.682*(ChlIdxSTI) + 0.606*(PHSTI) + 0.111*(BGBSTI) - 0.281*(AGBSTI). The regression model exhibited an accuracy of 96.8% with an R2 of 0.968 and an F-statistic of 115.080 (P<0.01). Multicollinearity testing confirmed variance inflation factor (VIF) values below 5 for all retained terms.

Model validity was evaluated against the 4 independent test germplasms, yielding a linear correlation coefficient of 0.987 between observed and predicted D-values. This compressed formula allows high-throughput computational screening of Leymus chinensis populations using only 6 foundational seedling-stage traits.

- Regression formula: D = -4.153 + 3.089*Fv/FmSTI + 0.161*GRSTI + 1.682*ChlIdxSTI + 0.606*PHSTI + 0.111*BGBSTI - 0.281*AGBSTI.

- Model parameters: R2=0.968, F=115.080, P<0.01, with all VIF values below 5.

- Predictive validation achieved a 0.987 correlation coefficient between predicted and empirical D-values.

This study evaluated 70 Leymus chinensis accessions under mixed saline-alkaline stress of 60 mmol/L at pH=9.5 across 18 physiological and morphometric indicators. Principal component analysis extracted 6 core components accounting for an 84.615% cumulative variance contribution rate. Comprehensive evaluation D-values spanned from -1.657 to 3.019, categorizing germplasms via hierarchical clustering into salt-alkali tolerant (11 accessions), moderately tolerant (13 accessions), and sensitive (46 accessions) cohorts. A 6-parameter stepwise linear regression equation predicted composite tolerance with 96.8% accuracy (R2=0.968), establishing an empirical framework for Songnen Plain grassland ecological restoration.

## Phenological Boundaries and Stress Regime Constraints

This study evaluated early-stage tolerance dynamics under fixed laboratory conditions, which may differ from full-season agronomic performance across fluctuating field environments.

- Phenotyping was restricted to seed germination and early seedling growth across a 20 d duration, omitting mature tillering, overwintering rhizome bud survival, and flowering phases.

- A single constant salt-alkali concentration of 60 mmol/L at pH=9.5 was tested, precluding identification of maximum tolerance thresholds under gradient salinity regimes.

## 1. Executive Abstract

To establish an objective methodology for characterizing saline-alkaline adaptability in forage grasses, 70 Leymus chinensis germplasm accessions were evaluated under 60 mmol/L mixed salt-alkali stress (pH=9.5). A streamlined predictive regression model incorporating 6 core traits achieved an R2 of 0.968 (F=115.080, P<0.01) without collinearity, providing a rapid computational standard for breeding selection and degraded sodic grassland restoration.

## Compensatory Somatic Growth Dynamics and Flock Uniformity

Metabolizable energy restriction during the crucial rearing phase between 7 and 15 weeks of age transiently suppresses growth rates without compromising final target body mass at the onset of lay. In this controlled feeding trial, pullets subjected to 90% and 80% dietary energy density exhibited significantly depressed body weights at 15 and 16 weeks of age (P<0.01). By week 17, pullets fed the 80% ME regimen remained significantly lighter than control and 90% ME cohorts (P<0.01). However, following three weeks of ad libitum realimentation on a standard pre-lay formulation containing 11.72 MJ/kg metabolizable energy, body weights across all experimental groups equalized at 18 weeks of age, showing no significant differences relative to the ad libitum control (P>0.05).

A critical commercial metric in pullet rearing is flock uniformity, as synchronous reproductive maturation ensures sustained peak egg-laying persistency. Body weight coefficient of variation at 18 weeks was significantly lower in both energy-restricted treatments than in the control group (P<0.05), with the 80% ME group establishing a CV of 7.58%. Over the entire 7 to 18 week duration, average daily feed intake and feed-to-gain ratio scaled with restriction intensity, reaching 68.45 g and 5.84 in the 80% ME cohort, whereas average daily metabolizable energy intake declined to 716.52 kJ.

- Week 18 body weights displayed no significant statistical disparity across treatments (P=0.228).

- Body weight coefficient of variation was markedly reduced in the 80% ME cohort (7.58%) compared to control (P=0.028).

- Average daily metabolizable energy intake decreased linearly across escalating restriction levels (P<0.001).

This investigation evaluated dietary metabolizable energy restriction during weeks 7 to 15 followed by ad libitum realimentation during weeks 16 to 18 in 540 Hy-Line Brown laying pullets. Evaluated energy levels comprised 12.34 MJ/kg, 11.11 MJ/kg, and 9.87 MJ/kg. Although restricted birds exhibited reduced body weights at weeks 15 and 16, compensatory growth aligned body weights across all cohorts at week 18. Furthermore, energy restriction significantly reduced the body weight coefficient of variation, decreased jejunal crypt depth in the 80% cohort, suppressed opportunistic Actinobacteriota, and significantly enriched beneficial methanogens alongside metabolic pathways releasing free energy.

## Gastrointestinal Morphological Integrity and Enterocyte Kinetics

Quantitative necropsy at 18 weeks of age established that rearing energy restriction followed by unrestricted feeding preserved overall digestive tract development without structural atrophy. The proventriculus papillae count, proventriculus papillae amount index, and relative weights and lengths of the duodenum, jejunum, ileum, caeca, and colon exhibited no significant differences relative to the ad libitum control (P>0.05). The only macroscopic anatomical distinction observed was the relative gastric wall thickness of the gizzard, which registered lower values in restricted cohorts compared to the control group (P<0.05).

Microscopic examination of jejunal tissue sections revealed favorable histomorphological adaptations supporting intestinal mucosal maturity. The 80% ME cohort displayed a significantly shallower jejunal crypt depth of 122.66 μm, contrasting with 140.44 μm in the control group and 142.18 μm in the 90% ME group (P=0.035). Because villus height remained comparable across groups (1058.03 μm in 80% ME versus 1170.67 μm in control, P=0.302), mucosal absorptive surface integrity was fully retained while reduced crypt depth signaled decreased enterocyte turnover and advanced mucosal functional differentiation.

- Jejunal crypt depth decreased significantly to 122.66 μm under 80% ME restriction (P=0.035).

- Relative weights and lengths of small and large intestinal compartments exhibited complete functional equivalence to control birds (P>0.05).

- Villus height to crypt depth ratio remained stable across all nutritional treatments (P=0.450).

## Cecal Taxonomic Shifts and Energy Metabolic Remodeling

High-throughput sequencing of 16S rRNA gene V3-V4 variable regions demonstrated that dietary energy restriction profoundly restructured cecal microecology after three weeks of ad libitum feeding. Both alpha and beta diversity indices differed significantly between restricted pullets and ad libitum controls (P<0.05). Principal coordinate analysis and non-metric multidimensional scaling revealed close clustering between the 90% and 80% ME cohorts, clearly separating them from the unrestricted control profile. Operational taxonomic unit counts reached 3334 in controls, 1865 in the 90% ME group, and 2129 in the 80% ME group.

Taxonomic profiling demonstrated that the 80% ME regimen significantly reduced the relative abundance of potentially detrimental phyla, including Actinobacteriota and its class Actinobacteria (P<0.01), while markedly expanding protective Euryarchaeota (P<0.01). LEfSe biomarker identification pinpointed Methanobacteria, Methanobacteriales, and Methanobacteriaceae as core taxa driving the 80% ME microenvironment. Predictive functional annotation via Tax4Fun indicated that cecal microorganisms in restricted groups actively enriched pathways releasing free energy, notably starch and sucrose metabolism, galactose metabolism, purine and pyrimidine metabolism, cysteine and methionine metabolism, and the citric acid cycle.

- Significant suppression of phylum Actinobacteriota in the 80% ME cohort (P<0.01).

- Biomarker enrichment of methanogenic taxa including Methanobacteriaceae in restricted birds.

- Upregulation of free-energy metabolic pathways facilitating post-restriction compensatory feed efficiency.

## Nutritional Boundary Conditions and Practical Application Context

This management strategy applies directly to floor- or cage-reared brown egg layers transitioning from rearing to early lay phases, requiring careful balance between energy intake restriction and skeletal elongation.

- Skeletal frame indices at 18 weeks of age, including body slanting length, keel length, and shank length, remained significantly smaller in the 80% ME group (P<0.05), indicating that harsher restriction regimes require longer realimentation windows to complete skeletal expansion.

- The experimental protocol implemented quantitative feeding based on control cohort volumetric intake from 7 to 15 weeks of age, demanding rigorous feeding automation in large commercial flocks.

- Trial measurements terminated at the onset of lay (18 weeks of age), necessitating subsequent lifecycle monitoring to quantify long-term cumulative egg mass and shell breaking strength.

abstract_en: The formation of dietary advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) is intimately linked to thermal processing regimes in food manufacturing. In this study, fresh Lycium barbarum fruits were subjected to convective hot air drying at 40 deg C, 50 deg C, and 60 deg C to elucidate the kinetic formation patterns of AGEs and their functional interplay with intrinsic bioactive metabolites. Targeted metabolomic profiling via UHPLC-Q-Trap 5500 MS identified 436 metabolites, including eight distinct AGE species. Lysine-derived AGEs—comprising Nepsilon-(carboxymethyl)lysine (CML), Nepsilon-(carboxyethyl)lysine (CEL), N6-threonyl, N6-oxalyl, and N6-lactyl—exhibited considerably higher quantitative concentrations than arginine-derived AGEs, namely Nepsilon-(carboxymethyl)arginine (CMA), Nepsilon-(carboxyethyl)arginine (CEA), and methylglyoxal-hydroimidazolone (MG-H1). Across all thermal drying treatments, total AGE accumulations exhibited an initial escalation followed by a terminal decrease. While both processing parameters governed AGE synthesis, drying temperature exerted a markedly stronger impact than processing time. Concurrently, dynamic shifts in endogenous precursors and micronutrients were observed: lysine and arginine depleted progressively as critical reactive precursors, while free carbohydrates and unsaturated fatty acid unsaturation levels positively correlated with AGE accumulation. Conversely, endogenous vitamins (vitamin B6, thiamine, and niacinamide) alongside saturated fatty acids exhibited suppressive correlations against AGE generation, providing empirical benchmarks for optimizing industrial goji dehydration.

## Targeted Metabolomic Identification and AGE Profiling

Thermal dehydration remains the primary industrial technique for preserving fresh Lycium barbarum, which possesses an initial moisture content near 80% and elevated sugar levels that render it susceptible to postharvest decay. Using targeted UHPLC-Q-Trap 5500 MS metabolomics, 436 metabolites spanning 18 functional classes were annotated, comprising 37 amino acids and peptides, 28 organic acids, 22 nucleosides and nucleotides, and 14 sphingolipids. High analytical stability was maintained throughout the sequence, with all quality control (QC) relative standard deviations falling below 30% and the first two principal components accounting for 20.00% and 13.71% of variance.

Among all annotated features, eight distinct AGEs accounted for 4.42% of differentiated metabolomic products. The identified panel comprised five lysine-derived structures—Nepsilon-(carboxymethyl)lysine (CML), Nepsilon-(carboxyethyl)lysine (CEL), N6-threonyl, N6-oxalyl, and N6-lactyl—and three arginine-derived adducts: Nepsilon-(carboxymethyl)arginine (CMA), Nepsilon-(carboxyethyl)arginine (CEA), and methylglyoxal-hydroimidazolones (MG-H1). Quantitative measurements revealed that lysine-derived species predominated over arginine-derived congeners, highlighting N6-threonyl and CMA as the primary empirical markers for tracking total AGE burdens in dehydrated wolfberry products.

- Metabolite distribution encompassed 259 positive-ion and 177 negative-ion features, exhibiting excellent instrumental repeatability across QC clusters.

- Novel food matrix detection was verified for N6-threonyl, N6-oxalyl, and N6-lactyl alongside conventional glycation markers CML and CEL.

Thermal processing of goji berries (Lycium barbarum) induces non-enzymatic Maillard cascades that generate hazardous dietary advanced glycation end-products (AGEs). Applying targeted UHPLC-Q-Trap 5500 MS metabolomics across convective hot air drying regimes (40 deg C, 50 deg C, and 60 deg C), researchers mapped 8 distinct AGE congeners. Lysine-derived AGEs dominated over arginine-derived adducts, with N6-threonyl and Nepsilon-(carboxymethyl)arginine (CMA) emerging as primary abundance markers. Kinetic monitoring across convective hot air regimes (40 deg C for 38 h, 50 deg C for 30 h, and 60 deg C for 18 h) demonstrated a uniform biphasic trajectory wherein AGE concentrations increased steadily during mid-phase dehydration before exhibiting measurable declines at process termination. Fresh fruit contained baseline AGE quantities that accelerated rapidly as moisture diminished. Samples dried under 50 deg C sustained elevated lysine-derived AGE concentrations relative to 40 deg C and 60 deg C runs, reflecting an interaction between lower activation rates at 40 deg C and abbreviated total drying duration at 60 deg C.

Cross-correlation with intrinsic bioactive fractions highlighted the mechanistic drivers of Maillard progression. Endogenous lysine and arginine concentrations exhibited steep, temperature-dependent declines, confirming their consumption as key nitrogenous precursors. Concurrently, reducing carbohydrates including glucose, sucrose, fructose, and mannose displayed positive associations with glycation intensity. This investigation establishes foundational metabolomic kinetics for hot air drying of goji berries, though processing boundaries and sample specificities require consideration when adapting parameters industrially.

# Study on Formation Regularity of Advanced Glycation End-Products and Changes of Bioactive Components in Process of Hot Air Drying of Lycium barbarum

---

**DOI:** `10.13995/j.cnki.11-1802/ts.042981` | **Journal:** Food and Fermentation Industries (食品与发酵工业) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** WANG Xiaolan, YANG Yuanyuan, GE Zhiwei, MA Siyang, WANG Zelan, LIU Jingze, ZHANG Ximing, WEI Chaokun  
**Affiliation:** College of Food Science and Engineering, Ningxia University

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

The formation of dietary advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) is intimately linked to thermal processing regimes in food manufacturing. In this study, fresh Lycium barbarum fruits were subjected to convective hot air drying at 40 deg C, 50 deg C, and 60 deg C to elucidate the kinetic formation patterns of AGEs and their functional interplay with intrinsic bioactive metabolites. Targeted metabolomic profiling via UHPLC-Q-Trap 5500 MS identified 436 metabolites, including eight distinct AGE species. Lysine-derived AGEs—comprising Nepsilon-(carboxymethyl)lysine (CML), Nepsilon-(carboxyethyl)lysine (CEL), N6-threonyl, N6-oxalyl, and N6-lactyl—exhibited considerably higher quantitative concentrations than arginine-derived AGEs, namely Nepsilon-(carboxymethyl)arginine (CMA), Nepsilon-(carboxyethyl)arginine (CEA), and methylglyoxal-hydroimidazolone (MG-H1). Across all thermal drying treatments, total AGE accumulations exhibited an initial escalation followed by a terminal decrease. While both processing parameters governed AGE synthesis, drying temperature exerted a markedly stronger impact than processing time. Concurrently, dynamic shifts in endogenous precursors and micronutrients were observed: lysine and arginine depleted progressively as critical reactive precursors, while free carbohydrates and unsaturated fatty acid unsaturation levels positively correlated with AGE accumulation. Conversely, endogenous vitamins (vitamin B6, thiamine, and niacinamide) alongside saturated fatty acids exhibited suppressive correlations against AGE generation, providing empirical benchmarks for optimizing industrial goji dehydration.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Targeted UHPLC-Q-Trap metabolomics identified 8 distinct AGEs among 436 total metabolites across 18 chemical classes in Lycium barbarum.
- Lysine-derived adducts predominated over arginine-derived forms, with N6-threonyl reaching up to 4.68 * 10^-2 +- 2.81 * 10^-2 micromol/L at 40 deg C (26 h).
- CMA peaked at 4.46 * 10^-2 +- 4.54 * 10^-2 micromol/L during 50 deg C drying (20 h), while CEA remained below detection limits at 40 deg C and 50 deg C, reaching 4.290 * 10^-3 +- 1.16 * 10^-4 micromol/L only after 18 h at 60 deg C.
- AGE accumulation followed a biphasic rise-and-fall curve across 40 deg C, 50 deg C, and 60 deg C, with thermal processing temperature displaying greater regulatory impact than drying duration.
- Vitamin B6, thiamine, niacinamide, and saturated fatty acids FA(4:0) and FA(8:0) correlated with AGE suppression, contrasting with precursor consumption of lysine and arginine.

abstract_en: The domain of unknown function 247 (DUF247) gene family executes vital regulatory roles in plant architecture, environmental adaptation, and secondary metabolic pathways. In this study, twelve ApDUF247 genes were identified across the Andrographis paniculata reference genome (NCBI PRJNA421867) using hidden Markov model searches (PF03140) and BLASTp alignment. Physicochemical characterization revealed amino acid lengths spanning 127 to 1680 residues and molecular weights from 14731.38 to 186638.71 Da, with seven proteins localized to the cytoplasm. Collinearity assessments identified eleven orthologous pairs with Strobilanthes cusia, seven with Sesamum indicum, and one with Arabidopsis thaliana. Promoter analyses uncovered high densities of hormone-responsive and stress-responsive cis-acting motifs, including 29 ethylene-responsive elements, 26 abscisic acid-responsive elements, and 48 MYC binding sites. Transcriptomic expression mapping indicated tissue specificity, with ApDUF247_11 expressed exclusively in roots and ApDUF247_9 showing stem-specific abundance. Abiotic stressors, including drought, 45 degrees Celsius heat, 15 degrees Celsius cold, 200 micromol per liter methyl jasmonate, and 3.8 W per square meter ultraviolet-C radiation, induced pronounced transcriptional reprogramming. Protein interaction mapping revealed that ApDUF247_8 interacts with five serine/threonine protein kinases, whereas ApDUF247_3 associates with five peroxisomal proteins and one E3 ubiquitin ligase. Crucially, ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_9, and ApDUF247_12 exhibited tight co-expression with MEP pathway structural genes (Cor>0.8), pinpointing candidate regulators governing bioactive diterpenoid lactone accumulation.

This study conducts a genome-wide survey of the DUF247 domain-containing gene family in the medicinal plant Andrographis paniculata. Computational screening identified 12 ApDUF247 members distributed across 8 chromosomes, classified into three phylogenetic subfamilies. Comparative genomics revealed 11 collinear gene pairs with Strobilanthes cusia, 7 with Sesamum indicum, and 1 with Arabidopsis thaliana. Transcriptomic profiling across tissues and abiotic stress treatments demonstrated distinct regulatory divergence. Network analysis showed that ApDUF247_8 interacts with 5 serine/threonine protein kinases, while ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_9, and ApDUF247_12 strongly correlate with andrographolide MEP biosynthetic pathway genes with correlation coefficients exceeding 0.8.

## Genomic Distribution and Collinear Evolutionary Trajectories

Bioinformatic mining of the Andrographis paniculata reference assembly uncovered 12 non-redundant DUF247 domain-containing genes designated ApDUF247_1 through ApDUF247_12. These genes mapped unevenly across eight chromosomes, with chromosomes Ap-4, Ap-12, Ap-13, and Ap-20 each housing two loci, whereas Ap-2, Ap-3, Ap-14, and Ap-21 each harbored a solitary member. An intra-genomic synteny event was detected between ApDUF247_5 and ApDUF247_12, suggesting duplication from a shared ancestral progenitor.

Comparative orthology profiling illustrated closer evolutionary conservation between Andrographis paniculata and its Acanthaceae relative Strobilanthes cusia, sharing 11 collinear gene pairs spanning 9 ApDUF247 and 9 ScDUF247 loci. In contrast, 7 collinear pairs were observed with Sesamum indicum, and only 1 collinear pair was conserved with the model crucifer Arabidopsis thaliana. ApDUF247_5 exhibited expanded syntenic duplication, maintaining collinearity with two orthologs each in S. cusia and S. indicum, highlighting lineage-specific retention.

- ApDUF247_3 and ApDUF247_5 each maintained collinear pairing with two distinct Strobilanthes cusia orthologs.

- Phylogenetic clustering segregated the gene family into subfamilies A, B, and C, matching structural exon-intron boundaries.

## Structural Architecture and Abiotic Stress Transcriptional Dynamics

Conserved motif scanning revealed 10 signature motifs across ApDUF247 proteins, where Motif 1 served as the foundational functional core present in nine members but absent in ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_9, and ApDUF247_12. Motif 9 uniquely distinguished subfamily B. Exon-intron structural diversification was pronounced: seven genes (ApDUF247_5, ApDUF247_7, ApDUF247_8, ApDUF247_9, ApDUF247_10, ApDUF247_11, and ApDUF247_12) consisted of a single coding sequence, whereas ApDUF247_3 possessed 22 exons.

Expression profiling demonstrated distinct tissue-specific compartmentalization. ApDUF247_2 and ApDUF247_11 exhibited predominant expression in root tissues, while ApDUF247_5, ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_7, and ApDUF247_8 were enriched in aerial organs. Under abiotic stress, ApDUF247_1, ApDUF247_2, ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_7, and ApDUF247_8 were upregulated under drought and after 3 h of 45 degrees Celsius heat exposure, subsequently declining at 6 h. Methyl jasmonate exposure (200 micromol per liter) elevated ApDUF247_2, ApDUF247_7, and ApDUF247_8 transcript levels while repressing ApDUF247_1, ApDUF247_4, ApDUF247_5, ApDUF247_9, and ApDUF247_12.

- ApDUF247_7 promoter harbored 9 abscisic acid-responsive elements, matching strong transcriptional activation during drought.

- ApDUF247_11 expression remained strictly restricted to root tissues, showing zero baseline transcription in leaf stress samples.

## Interactome Networks and Andrographolide Biosynthetic Coordination

Protein interaction networks constructed from orthologous mapping identified specific functional hubs within the gene family. ApDUF247_8 was predicted to interact directly with 5 serine/threonine protein kinases, supporting its involvement in phosphorylation-mediated stress signal transduction cascades. Additionally, ApDUF247_3 interacted with 5 peroxisomal membrane proteins and 1 peroxisomal biogenesis-associated E3 ubiquitin ligase, indicating participation in lipid metabolism and reactive oxygen species homeostatic regulation.

Correlation analysis between ApDUF247 transcription and diterpenoid lactone structural pathway genes revealed divergent pathway partitioning. ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_9, and ApDUF247_12 demonstrated strong co-expression with plastidial methylerythritol phosphate (MEP) pathway structural genes (Cor>0.8), including ApDXS4, ApHDR2, ApCMK, and diterpene synthases. ApDUF247_12 exhibited the strongest correlation with ApDXS4 and ApCMK, while ApDUF247_9 correlated highest with ApGGPPS7 and ApDXS2. Conversely, ApDUF247_2, ApDUF247_4, and ApDUF247_11 clustered with cytosolic mevalonate pathway genes including ApHMGR1, ApMK, and ApPMK1.

- ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_9, and ApDUF247_12 are prioritized as primary candidate transcriptional regulators of andrographolide production.

- ApDUF247_8 and ApDUF247_3 represent central post-translational signaling nodes governing stress adaptation.

## Methodological Constraints and Experimental Boundaries

This genome-wide analysis provides predictive bioinformatic associations and transcriptomic co-expression patterns in Andrographis paniculata, which require direct biochemical validation before commercial agronomic or metabolic engineering deployment.

- Protein interaction networks were computationally inferred by homology mapping to Arabidopsis thaliana interactome databases and lack in vivo bimolecular fluorescence complementation or co-immunoprecipitation confirmation.

- Stress-responsive expression patterns were measured in leaf tissues, precluding observation of leaf-specific abiotic responses for root-delimited members such as ApDUF247_11.

- Regulatory links between candidate genes ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_9, ApDUF247_12 and andrographolide accumulation remain correlation-based (Cor>0.8) without functional knockout or overexpression validation.

Detailed process conditions, instrument calibrations, and complete supplementary datasets beyond the core quantitative benchmarks are preserved in the Peer-Reviewed PDF Edition below.

# Identification, Evolution and Functional Analysis of ApDUF247 Gene Family in Andrographis paniculata

---

**DOI:** `10.11924/j.issn.1000-6850.casb2025-0369` | **Journal:** Chinese Agricultural Science Bulletin (中国农学通报) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** ZHANG Long, XU Shiqiang, LI Jingyu, LI Xulong, WANG Jihua  
**Affiliation:** Key Laboratory of Crop Genetic and Improvement of Guangdong Province, Crop Research Institute, Guangdong Academy of Agricultural Sciences

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

The domain of unknown function 247 (DUF247) gene family executes vital regulatory roles in plant architecture, environmental adaptation, and secondary metabolic pathways. In this study, twelve ApDUF247 genes were identified across the Andrographis paniculata reference genome (NCBI PRJNA421867) using hidden Markov model searches (PF03140) and BLASTp alignment. Physicochemical characterization revealed amino acid lengths spanning 127 to 1680 residues and molecular weights from 14731.38 to 186638.71 Da, with seven proteins localized to the cytoplasm. Collinearity assessments identified eleven orthologous pairs with Strobilanthes cusia, seven with Sesamum indicum, and one with Arabidopsis thaliana. Promoter analyses uncovered high densities of hormone-responsive and stress-responsive cis-acting motifs, including 29 ethylene-responsive elements, 26 abscisic acid-responsive elements, and 48 MYC binding sites. Transcriptomic expression mapping indicated tissue specificity, with ApDUF247_11 expressed exclusively in roots and ApDUF247_9 showing stem-specific abundance. Abiotic stressors, including drought, 45 degrees Celsius heat, 15 degrees Celsius cold, 200 micromol per liter methyl jasmonate, and 3.8 W per square meter ultraviolet-C radiation, induced pronounced transcriptional reprogramming. Protein interaction mapping revealed that ApDUF247_8 interacts with five serine/threonine protein kinases, whereas ApDUF247_3 associates with five peroxisomal proteins and one E3 ubiquitin ligase. Crucially, ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_9, and ApDUF247_12 exhibited tight co-expression with MEP pathway structural genes (Cor>0.8), pinpointing candidate regulators governing bioactive diterpenoid lactone accumulation.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Identified 12 ApDUF247 family members unevenly distributed across 8 chromosomes in Andrographis paniculata.
- Established cross-species synteny identifying 11 collinear DUF247 pairs with Strobilanthes cusia, 7 with Sesamum indicum, and 1 with Arabidopsis thaliana.
- Mapped promoter architecture showing 29 ethylene-responsive elements, 26 abscisic acid-responsive elements, 45 Box-4 motifs, and 48 MYC binding sites across the gene family.
- Demonstrated protein-protein associations between ApDUF247_8 and 5 serine/threonine protein kinases, as well as ApDUF247_3 with 5 peroxisomal proteins and 1 E3 ubiquitin ligase.
- Identified ApDUF247_6, ApDUF247_9, and ApDUF247_12 as key candidate regulators displaying high expression correlation (Cor>0.8) with andrographolide biosynthetic structural genes.

analysis_markdown_en:
Automated harvesting of camellia fruit requires real-time, high-precision visual recognition under unstructured orchard conditions characterized by leaf occlusion, fluctuating illumination, and multi-scale targets. This study presents YOLO-Camellia, an architectural optimization of YOLOv11 tailored for edge deployment. By substituting standard convolutions with GhostConv in the backbone, integrating a parallel cascade attention mechanism (PCAM) to suppress background foliage noise, and designing a multi-path feature enhancement pyramid network (Multi-PANet) across three scales, the model achieves 94.8% average precision (AP) with 28.7 M parameters and 95.6 G FLOPs. TensorRT-accelerated deployment on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX platform yields 93.2% AP at 51.7 f·s-1.

## Lightweight Backbone Engineering and Parallel Attention Integration

Conventional deep convolutional architectures face substantial deployment barriers in agricultural robotics due to excessive arithmetic density and parameter redundancy. YOLO-Camellia addresses this limitation by embedding GhostConv modules within the YOLOv11 Darknet-53 backbone. GhostConv generates an initial set of intrinsic feature maps via standard convolution and subsequently derives redundant phantom feature maps through lightweight linear transformations. When the linear kernel size matches the spatial convolution kernel, GhostConv approaches an s-fold compression in computational overhead and parameter volume relative to standard convolutions.

To mitigate severe background foliage interference and fruit-leaf visual similarity in natural orchard environments, the backbone incorporates a Parallel Cascade Attention Mechanism (PCAM). Unlike sequential attention structures such as CBAM that risk feature degradation through intermediate dimensionality reduction, PCAM decouples spatial and channel attention into isolated, concurrent pipelines. The channel path utilizes global average and max pooling coupled with 1D convolutions to assign adaptive inter-channel weights, while the spatial path processes pooled descriptors through a 2D convolution to delineate boundary contours. Parallel fusion preserves gradient fidelity while sharpening target saliency under diverse ambient illumination.

- GhostConv replaces standard convolutions to compress baseline backbone parameters down to 29.8 M in isolation.

- Independent spatial and channel branches in PCAM eliminate cross-module information bottlenecks.

- Ablation isolated to PCAM elevates baseline AP from 92.6% to 93.9%.

## Multi-Scale Multi-PANet Neck and Embedded Edge Benchmark

Natural orchard imagery features significant target scale variance, ranging from distant clustered fruits to foreground mature specimens. Standard PANet configurations suffer feature attenuation across deep semantic pathways, causing small-target misdetections. Multi-PANet remedies this by introducing residual lateral bridges between encoder downsampling and decoder upsampling stages across three fixed resolution scales (80x80, 40x40, and 20x20 grid cells). Decoder concatenation merges multi-source inputs prior to upsampling, preventing high-resolution boundary degradation while bounding computational complexity.

Model viability was validated on an embedded NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX edge computing unit equipped with a 6-core ARMv8.2 CPU, 384 CUDA cores, and 48 Tensor Cores. Post-training graph optimization via NVIDIA TensorRT eliminated redundant execution graphs. In embedded testing averaged across 10 evaluation runs, YOLO-Camellia attained an AP of 93.2%, recall of 93.4%, and precision of 93.9% at an execution rate of 51.7 f·s-1, exceeding the baseline YOLOv11 frame rate by 81.4% while reducing active runtime parameters to 15.9 M and compute load to 39.2 G FLOPs.

- Three-scale feature processing restricts unnecessary dimensional scaling while preserving small-fruit bounding accuracy.

- TensorRT optimization on Jetson Xavier NX achieves 51.7 f·s-1, safely exceeding real-time visual servoing thresholds.

- Edge parameters decrease by 58.6% and edge FLOPs drop by 62.2% compared to uncompressed baseline deployment.

## Domain Constraints and Edge Deployment Boundaries

Although YOLO-Camellia achieves high precision and edge efficiency, operational limitations persist regarding cultivar diversity, severe occlusion thresholds, and precision loss during edge compilation.

- Evaluation was conducted on a single cultivar, Ganshi84-8, leaving generalization performance across diverse camellia fruit morphologies and skin colorations unquantified.

- Standalone integration of GhostConv caused an isolated drop of 0.8 percentage points in AP (down to 91.8%), indicating that cheap linear transformations omit subtle edge nuances if uncompensated by attention modules.

- TensorRT layer fusion and FP16/INT8 graph quantization on the Jetson Xavier NX induced an AP degradation of 1.6 percentage points (from 94.8% to 93.2%) relative to uncompressed workstation inference.

analysis_markdown_en:
This study conducts a systematic phenotypic and biochemical evaluation of 42 mulberry accessions conserved at the Chongqing Three Gorges Academy of Agricultural Sciences repository. The investigation quantified 18 qualitative traits, 9 quantitative morphological features, and 6 leaf nutritional properties using standardized botanical protocols. Quantitative traits exhibited wide phenotypic divergence, with coefficients of variation ranging from 7.68% to 37.61%. Leaf nutritional quality varied substantially, recording peak crude protein content of 256.91 mg/g and crude fiber levels up to 14.81%. Multivariate cluster and principal component analyses resolved the accessions into distinct functional cohorts, clarifying breeding selection criteria for forage and sericultural applications.

## Phenotypic Variation and Morphological Divergence Across Germplasm

Morphological characterization of the 42 mulberry germplasm accessions revealed pronounced variation across both vegetative architecture and foliar dimensions. Qualitative traits demonstrated notable polymorphism; Shannon-Wiener diversity indices exceeded 1.0 for leaf surface (1.42), leaf base (1.16), winter bud color (1.16), and winter bud shape (1.15). In contrast, stem straightness showed zero variation, with all 42 accessions exhibiting erect stem habit. Foliar morphological traits showed predominant clustering around entire leaf and entire plus bilobed leaf structures.

Quantitative measurements confirmed significant foliar differentiation across the repository. Leaf length averaged 19.57 cm across all accessions, with Jianpuzhaisang exhibiting the maximum leaf length of 30.35 cm and maximum leaf width of 19.94 cm. The overall leaf size averaged 285.08 cm2, ranging from 98.19 cm2 to 605.84 cm2. Coefficients of variation showed marked spread, ranging from 7.68% for leaf shape index to 37.61% for leaf size, 33.23% for lenticel number, and 32.32% for winter bud size. Statistical normality assessments confirmed that leaf length, width, and shape index adhered to normal distribution models, whereas lenticel count and internode length exhibited significant skewed departures.

- Leaf length mean: 19.57 cm (range: 11.37 cm to 30.35 cm; standard deviation: 4.16 cm; CV: 21.25%).

- Leaf width mean: 14.06 cm (range: 8.57 cm to 19.94 cm; standard deviation: 2.58 cm; CV: 18.32%).

- Petiole length mean: 4.85 cm (range: 2.66 cm to 8.03 cm; CV: 27.13%).

- Mesophyll thickness mean: 2.36 mm (range: 1.77 mm to 3.17 mm; CV: 14.1%).

## Biochemical Nutritional Profiles and Metabolic Trade-Off Dynamics

Biochemical analysis identified pronounced differences in foliar nutrient accumulation among accessions. Total crude protein reached 256.91 mg/g in Baokan 61, demonstrating high nitrogen assimilation capacity suitable for specialized livestock forage. Foliar crude fiber levels ranged from a minimum of 7.44% in Da 10 to a maximum of 14.81% in Mengjian 5. Ash content peaked distinctly in Hekou Guosang at 20.87%, significantly outperforming all other conserved accessions in mineral accumulation.

Analysis of metabolic correlations revealed a negative association between foliar crude protein and crude fat content. This inverse relationship points toward metabolic competition in carbon-nitrogen allocation under distinct nitrogen assimilation states. Furthermore, the correlation between external leaf morphology and nutritional indicators remained weak overall, indicating that leaf dimensional metrics cannot serve as standalone proxies for biochemical quality.

## Multivariate Dimensionality Reduction and Taxonomic Germplasm Classification

Hierarchical cluster analysis using the UPGMA algorithm and Euclidean distance grouped the 42 accessions into 7 major clusters at a distance threshold of 2.5. Clusters B, C, and E comprised the primary germplasm architecture, accounting for 71.4% of total evaluated materials. Accessions within clusters exhibited strong internal morphological consistency while showing marked divergence across clusters, offering structured guidance for parental combination selection in breeding programs.

Principal component analysis reduced the 15 quantitative phenotypic and nutritional parameters into 6 components with a cumulative variance explanation of 81.96%. The first component (PCA1) explained 34.86% of total variance, dominated by leaf length (-0.41), leaf size (-0.41), leaf width (-0.39), and fresh weight (-0.38) on the negative axis, alongside crude fiber (0.24) and ash (0.22) on the positive axis. The second component (PCA2) explained 14.60% of variance, primarily governed by crude fat (0.56) and crude protein (-0.52). Together, leaf length, leaf size, crude protein, and crude fat were identified as primary diagnostic markers for germplasm differentiation.

- Six extracted principal components yielded eigenvalues of 5.23, 2.19, 1.64, 1.33, 1.07, and 0.83.

- Cumulative explained variance: PCA1 (34.86%), PCA2 (49.46%), PCA3 (60.39%), PCA4 (69.26%), PCA5 (76.41%), PCA6 (81.96%).

- UPGMA clustering delineated 7 discrete taxons with clusters B, C, and E representing 71.4% of all tested materials.

## Methodological Constraints and Breeding Application Scope

This study is limited to single-season evaluations at one repository, excluding environmental interaction, fruit biochemical traits, and multi-stress tolerance data.

- Foliar sampling occurred exclusively during mature leaf stages in October 2024 at Wanzhou, leaving genotype-by-environment (GxE) stability across varying ecological zones untested.

- Traditional length-width leaf area models overstate photosynthetically active area in deeply lobed accessions such as Jianpuzhaisang, requiring planar image integration.

- Comprehensive evaluation of fruit yield, biochemical fruit quality, and abiotic stress resistance is necessary before finalizing commercial deployment recommendations.

## 1. Executive Abstract

To address the insufficient comprehensive evaluation of phenotypic traits and leaf nutritional quality in mulberry (Morus spp.) germplasm and the lack of criteria for selecting superior accessions, 42 mulberry accessions conserved at the Mulberry Germplasm Repository of the Chongqing Three Gorges Academy of Agricultural Sciences (Wanzhou, Chongqing) were evaluated. Eighteen qualitative phenotypic traits, nine quantitative phenotypic traits, and six leaf nutritional quality traits were measured, and genetic diversity analysis, cluster analysis, principal component analysis (PCA), and correlation analysis were conducted. The results showed that qualitative traits such as leaf surface, leaf base, and winter bud color exhibited high diversity, while quantitative traits including leaf length, leaf width, leaf shape index, and mesophyll thickness showed significant variation, with coefficients of variation ranging from 7.68% to 37.61%. Leaf nutritional quality differed markedly among accessions, with the highest crude protein content reaching 256.91 mg/g and crude fiber content reaching 14.81%. Cluster analysis classified the 42 mulberry accessions into seven clusters, with clusters B, C, and E containing the largest numbers of accessions. PCA extracted six principal components, of which the first five had eigenvalues greater than 1, achieving a cumulative contribution rate of 81.96%, with leaf length, leaf size, crude protein, and crude fat identified as the main contributing traits. Significant correlations were observed among phenotypic traits, whereas correlations between phenotypic traits and leaf nutritional quality traits were relatively weak.

This study evaluated dietary supplementation with succinic acid, sodium butyrate, and isobutyric acid (each at 1 g/L in whole milk) across a 56-day trial in 64 male Holstein suckling calves. Sodium butyrate significantly increased total dry matter intake from days 1 to 56 and enhanced late-stage average daily gain alongside succinic acid. Both organic acids stimulated rumen nitrogen metabolism, yielding elevated microbial protein and volatile fatty acid concentrations. Concurrently, 16S rDNA sequencing revealed selective microbial remodeling, where succinic acid suppressed Methanobacteriota and enriched Fibrobacter, while sodium butyrate promoted Prevotella and Desulfovibrio, establishing sodium butyrate as the most efficacious additive for calf rearing.

## Somatic Growth Performance and Starter Intake Dynamics

In neonatal dairy calves, early rumen functional establishment directly governs starter feed intake and nutrient accretion. During the first four weeks (days 1 to 28), initial body weight and feed-to-gain ratios showed no statistically significant differences across dietary cohorts. However, as calves transitioned into the accelerated growth phase (days 29 to 56), the metabolic effects of milk-borne organic acid administration became prominent.

Calves in the sodium butyrate (SB) and succinic acid (SA) cohorts achieved superior average daily gains of 1.03 kg/d and 1.05 kg/d, respectively, surpassing both the control group (0.91 kg/d) and the isobutyric acid group (0.90 kg/d) (P = 0.016). The sodium butyrate intervention uniquely stimulated dry matter appetite, yielding a full-period (days 1 to 56) dry matter intake of 1.25 kg/d compared to 1.13 kg/d in controls (P = 0.006). This intake expansion reflects accelerated anatomical and functional rumen development, which permits greater solid feed utilization without compromising feed efficiency.

- Initial body weight averaged 43.31 kg in CK, 43.18 kg in SA, 42.89 kg in SB, and 43.49 kg in IB without baseline disparity (P = 0.984).

- Full-period average daily gain reached 0.86 kg/d in SB versus 0.77 kg/d in CK (P = 0.018).

- Overall feed-to-gain ratio across days 1 to 56 remained stable across groups at 1.44 to 1.53 (P = 0.529).

## Rumen Fermentation Modulation and Nitrogen Assimilation

Evaluation of ruminal fluid parameters confirmed that the supplemented organic acids preserved a healthy physiological rumen environment, maintaining fluid pH within 6.38 to 7.13 across all testing intervals. At day 42, ruminal ammonia nitrogen concentrations surged in both SA (22.07 mg/dL) and SB (18.70 mg/dL) groups relative to controls (12.06 mg/dL) (P < 0.001), indicating intensified microbial deamination and dietary nitrogen breakdown.

Importantly, elevated ammonia nitrogen was effectively channeled into microbial biomass synthesis. Microbial protein concentrations in SA and SB cohorts were significantly higher than CK across days 28, 42, and 56. By day 56, microbial protein reached 1.85 mg/mL in SA and 1.67 mg/mL in SB compared to 1.22 mg/mL in CK (P = 0.007). In parallel, volatile fatty acid accumulation reached its peak at day 56, where total volatile fatty acid levels in SB reached 54.13 mmol/mL, significantly exceeding the 32.01 mmol/mL observed in the control group (P = 0.005).

- Ruminal pH on day 56 declined moderately to 6.45 in SA and 6.38 in SB versus 6.75 in CK (P < 0.001), consistent with robust active fermentation.

- Propionic acid concentrations at day 42 peaked in the SB group at 9.54 mmol/mL compared with 3.92 mmol/mL in CK (P = 0.001).

- Acetic acid at day 56 was significantly elevated in SB (27.98 mmol/mL) over CK (19.54 mmol/mL) (P = 0.011).

## Taxonomic Restructuring of the Ruminal Microbiome

High-throughput sequencing of the 16S rDNA V3-V4 hypervariable regions identified Bacteroidota and Bacillota as the dominant phyla throughout the preweaning timeframe. Alpha diversity metrics showed structural shifts by day 56, where ACE richness in SB (1088.38) and IB (1022.00) decreased relative to CK (1172.32) and SA (1203.72) (P < 0.001), reflecting competitive dominance by specialized functional taxa.

Taxonomic shifts were accompanied by distinct metabolic niches. At day 56, the Methanobacteriota phylum was significantly attenuated in the SA cohort (0.56%) compared to CK (1.50%) and IB (1.56%) (P = 0.021). LEfSe biomarker analysis revealed early enrichment of hydrogen-consuming sulfate-reducing Desulfovibrio and cellulolytic Fibrobacter in SA calves at day 28. By day 56, Fibrobacter remained enriched in SA, while SB enriched Prevotella and Desulfovibrio, demonstrating that sodium butyrate and succinic acid foster distinct metabolic cascades that enhance carbohydrate and protein catabolism while curtailing methanogenesis.

- Day 28 relative abundance of Thermodesulfobacteriota was 2.14% in SA versus 0.62% in CK (P = 0.005).

- Day 28 Spirochaetota relative abundance increased to 2.76% in SA versus 0.37% in CK (P = 0.031).

- Day 56 Pseudomonadota abundance expanded to 15.38% in IB compared with 7.26% in CK (P = 0.002).

## Experimental Boundaries and Practical Applicability Constraints

The findings are grounded in a controlled 56-day liquid milk feeding regimen in male Holstein calves, presenting specific boundary constraints regarding dosing gradients and weaning transition dynamics.

- The experimental design tested a single inclusion dosage of 1 g/L for each organic acid; optimal dose-response curves and threshold toxicity limits for succinic acid and isobutyric acid remain undefined.

- Calves received an escalating liquid milk allowance scaling up to 10 L/d from days 30 to 56, which depressed starter solid feed intake relative to step-down milk feeding protocols.

- Post-weaning physiological persistence was not monitored past day 56 to verify whether microbial enrichment and mucosal ruminal advantages persist after milk cessation.

## Solid-State Fermentation Kinetics and Nutrient Upgrading

Flaxseed meal serves as an abundant non-grain protein source rich in alpha-linolenic acid, yet its conventional inclusion in monogastric feeding regimens is constrained by recalcitrant anti-nutritional compounds including cyanogenic glycosides and viscous mucilaginous fiber. In this trial, bioconversion was executed by inoculating a tailored raw substrate comprising 90% flaxseed meal, 5.2% wheat bran, 3% glucose, 1.5% urea, and 0.3% dipotassium hydrogen phosphate with 0.5% compound enzymes and 5% compound bacterial consortium. Fermentation proceeded for 3 d at 35 °C at a 1:3 mass-to-volume solid-to-water ratio within specialized anaerobic venting bags.

The cooperative multi-strain consortium integrated duck-derived Lactobacillus plantarum, Bacillus subtilis, Aspergillus niger, and Candida utilis, coupled with cellulase, pectinase, and glucose oxidase. This biological treatment degraded complex structural carbohydrates, shifting crude fiber downward from 12.61% to 7.57%. Concurrently, microbial protein accumulation and enzymatic macromolecular breakdown raised crude protein from 34.88% to 39.56% and doubled small peptide availability from 149.8 mg/g to 298.3 mg/g, ensuring enhanced intestinal absorptive kinetics.

- Crude protein increased from 34.88% to 39.56% following cooperative solid-state fermentation.

- Crude fiber decreased from 12.61% to 7.57% through targeted enzymatic hydrolysis.

- Small peptide concentration doubled from 149.8 mg/g to 298.3 mg/g in the finished substrate.

This study evaluated dietary supplementation of compound bacteria-enzyme cooperative fermented flaxseed meal in male Wulong geese over a 10-week feeding trial. Solid-state bioprocessing improved substrate nutritional value by elevating crude protein from 34.88% to 39.56% and small peptide content from 149.8 mg/g to 298.3 mg/g while reducing crude fiber from 12.61% to 7.57%. Dietary replacement with 5% fermented flaxseed meal significantly enhanced whole-period average daily gain to 43.08 g/d, decreased feed-to-gain ratio to 3.10, elevated breast muscle n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids to 3.58%, and reduced the muscle n-6/n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid ratio to 13.00 alongside marked systemic antioxidant gains.

## Growth Dynamics and Commercial Carcass Metrics

In vivo feeding trials spanning 70 days demonstrated that dietary addition of 5% fermented flaxseed meal in experimental group II overcame the growth suppression typically observed with untreated flaxseed meal. During the brooding period (days 1 to 21), average daily gain reached 36.73 g/d in group II compared with 32.64 g/d in control and 32.72 g/d in group I, producing a significant end-of-brooding body weight advantage of 840.50 g versus 754.33 g in control birds. Throughout the growing period (days 22 to 70), group II maintained superior feed conversion with a feed-to-gain ratio of 3.58 against 4.00 in controls.

Evaluation of slaughter characteristics at 70 days revealed marked improvements in edible carcass yields. Pre-slaughter live weight reached 3145.00 g in group II versus 2962.50 g in control birds, accompanied by a dressed weight of 2726.67 g and an eviscerated yield of 70.75%. Prime retail cuts showed pronounced development, with breast muscle weight expanding to 217.50 g in group II compared with 175.00 g in controls and 177.50 g in group I, while leg muscle weight reached 330.00 g. Interestingly, directly mixing dry enzymes and bacteria into the feed without pre-fermentation produced slaughter weights indistinguishable from the control diet.

- Whole-period average daily gain rose significantly to 43.08 g/d in group II versus 39.67 g/d in controls.

- Whole-period feed-to-gain ratio fell from 3.47 in controls to 3.10 in group II.

- Breast muscle weight achieved 217.50 g in group II compared with 175.00 g in control geese.

## Lipid Metabolic Regulation and Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid Profile

Dietary inclusion of fermented flaxseed meal elicited profound remodeling of circulatory lipid profiles and pectoral muscle lipid architecture. Serum biochemical testing demonstrated that group II exhibited lower circulating triglyceride concentrations at 0.62 mmol/L compared with 0.94 mmol/L in controls and 0.88 mmol/L in group I. Concurrently, serum low-density lipoprotein cholesterol decreased to 1.77 mmol/L while protective high-density lipoprotein cholesterol rose to 4.28 mmol/L, reflecting accelerated reverse cholesterol transport and optimized peripheral lipid clearance.

Gas chromatographic profiling of breast muscle demonstrated selective deposition of essential long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids. In group II, alpha-linolenic acid climbed to 1.17%, eicosapentaenoic acid reached 0.33%, and docosahexaenoic acid reached 2.08%, whereas total n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids rose from 2.03% in controls to 3.58%. Consequently, the muscle n-6/n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid ratio dropped from 23.44 in controls down to 13.00, yielding poultry meat aligned with nutritional lipid targets for human consumption.

Parallel evaluation of circulatory redox status indicated substantial attenuation of oxidative stress. Serum superoxide dismutase activity rose to 171.05 U/mL, catalase reached 5.67 U/mL, and glutathione peroxidase reached 1012.96 U/mL in group II, driving total antioxidant capacity up to 0.65 mmol/L. This coordinated enzymatic activation suppressed systemic lipid peroxidation, decreasing malondialdehyde concentrations from 3.82 nmol/mL in control birds to 2.36 nmol/mL.

- Serum triglycerides decreased from 0.94 mmol/L in control birds to 0.62 mmol/L in group II.

- Total muscle n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids expanded from 2.03% to 3.58% in group II breast tissue.

- The pectoral muscle n-6/n-3 ratio dropped from 23.44 in controls to 13.00 in fermented meal birds.

- Serum malondialdehyde concentration was suppressed from 3.82 nmol/mL down to 2.36 nmol/mL.

## Methodological Constraints and Feed Formulation Boundaries

While the 10-week investigation confirms tangible performance and nutritional advantages of fermented flaxseed meal in male Wulong geese, specific formulation parameters and biological boundaries require careful consideration before broader commercial implementation.

- The experiment evaluated a single fixed inclusion rate of 5% fermented flaxseed meal, leaving dose-dependent responses, upper safety boundaries, and economics of higher replacement levels uncharacterized.

- The bird cohort was exclusively composed of 180 male Wulong geese raised under controlled elevated wire-floor housing, which may not mirror sex-specific responses or deep-litter and free-range commercial management systems.

- Preparation required specialized 3 d solid-state anaerobic incubation with a four-strain inoculum and three industrial enzymes at 35 °C, which adds secondary handling and equipment overhead compared with direct in-feed additive blending.

# Effects of Compound Bacteria-Enzyme Cooperative Fermented Flaxseed Meal on Growth Performance, Slaughter Performance, Muscle Fatty Acid Composition and Antioxidant Capacity of Wulong Geese

---

**DOI:** `10.12418/CJAN2026.092` | **Journal:** Chinese Journal of Animal Nutrition (动物营养学报) | **Year:** 2026  
**Authors:** CHANG Chunjing, WANG Binghan, REN Xiangquan, FAN Wenlei, ZHANG Jing, LAI Xuexiang, YANG Mengxiao, BAI Chuning, JIANG Yajing, TENG Xingyi, WANG Baowei, ZHANG Ming'ai  
**Affiliation:** College of Animal Science and Technology, Qingdao Agricultural University

---

## 1. Executive Abstract

This experiment investigated the effects of compound bacteria-enzyme cooperative fermented flaxseed meal on growth performance, slaughter performance, lipid metabolism, muscle fatty acid profile, and antioxidant capacity in Wulong geese. A cohort of 180 one-day-old male Wulong geese of similar body weight were randomized into three dietary treatment groups with six replicates of ten birds each. The control group received a basal diet supplemented with 5% unfermented flaxseed meal; experimental group I received the basal control diet directly supplemented with 0.25% compound bacteria and 0.025% compound enzymes; experimental group II was fed a diet formulated with 5% pre-fermented flaxseed meal over a 10-week feeding period spanning brooding and growing phases. Results showed that experimental group II exhibited significantly higher average daily gain across brooding, growing, and whole periods (P < 0.05), and significantly lower feed-to-gain ratios than the control group (P < 0.05). Carcass traits, including dressed weight, eviscerated rate, breast muscle weight, and leg muscle weight, were significantly improved in group II compared with control and group I (P < 0.05). Furthermore, experimental group II showed reduced serum triglycerides and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, alongside marked enrichment of alpha-linolenic acid, eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, and total n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids in breast muscle. Serum superoxide dismutase, catalase, and glutathione peroxidase activities were elevated while malondialdehyde fell significantly.

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Solid-state co-fermentation elevated crude protein from 34.88% to 39.56% and small peptides from 149.8 mg/g to 298.3 mg/g, while lowering crude fiber from 12.61% to 7.57%.
- Supplementation with 5% fermented flaxseed meal reduced whole-period feed-to-gain ratio from 3.47 in controls to 3.10 and elevated whole-period average daily gain from 39.67 g/d to 43.08 g/d.
- Breast muscle total n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids expanded from 2.03% to 3.58%, driving a beneficial contraction of the n-6/n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid ratio from 23.44 down to 13.00.
- Systemic serum antioxidant defenses improved through an increase in superoxide dismutase to 171.05 U/mL and a reduction in malondialdehyde to 2.36 nmol/mL.
- Direct in-feed unfermented bacteria and enzyme additions in group I failed to match the physiological and performance gains achieved by pre-fermented dietary substrate.
